title: [Model] Add Laya decision model (convaiinnovations/laya)
body:
## Motivation

[Laya](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya) is a non-autoregressive decision model: a bidirectional ModernBERT encoder (28 layers, hidden 1024) plus a small transformer decision head, 421M parameters. Every answer option is a `[MASK]` marker in the prompt, the head scores each marker, and the softmax over those markers is the answer distribution. A second head predicts whether the agent should escalate to a human.

Nothing is generated, so it does not fit the generation-based `/v1/decisions` path, which needs a chat template and single-token answer labels. SGLang also has no ModernBERT implementation at all. This adds one, together with the decision head, and serves the checkpoint as an embedding model where one request returns `[p_0, ..., p_{K-1}, act_escalate, act_not_escalate]`, with `K` varying per request.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/laya.py` (new): `LayaForDecision`, its ModernBERT encoder (alternating full and sliding attention, per-layer RoPE base) and the per-request pooling path.
- `python/sglang/srt/configs/embedding_model_spec.py`: declare the architecture as a bidirectional encoder that needs the full prompt, and switch off prefix reuse and chunked prefill for it.
- `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/model_hook.py`: honour `safe_disable_radix_cache` and `safe_disable_chunked_prefill` for every spec, not only the Gemma embedding path. A bidirectional encoder must not read a cached prefix, because the cached hidden states were computed without the tokens that follow them and the request silently reaches the model as a suffix-only batch. This is a correctness fix, not an optimization.
- `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`: `LayaForDecision` is never a generation model.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_LAYA_TEMPERATURE_CLAMP` and `SGLANG_LAYA_ATTENTION_BACKEND`.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_laya_registration.py` (new) and `test/registered/unit/configs/test_embedding_model_spec.py`.
- `docs/docs/supported-models/laya.mdx` (new) and the docs nav.

Two details worth knowing when serving this checkpoint. It ships no root `config.json`, so the docs page describes the small script that builds one; the per-question-type temperatures live under `laya_temperature` because `PretrainedConfig` consumes `temperature` as a generation default while building the config object, so a value stored under that name never reaches the model.

A prompt with no `[MASK]` marker returns the act head alone and logs a warning instead of raising: SGLang's own startup warm-up sends such a prompt, and a malformed request must not abort the engine.

The encoder computes its own bidirectional attention instead of routing through the attention backend, because the local layers keep keys within `|i - j| <= local_attention / 2` and the windowed backend path does not reproduce that mask. See the accuracy section for the measurement.

Limitations: tensor parallelism is not supported, because the decision head pools per request and is not sharded, and the encoder does not use the paged KV cache. Only the English root checkpoint is covered; the `multilingual` and `typed-decisions` subfolders use different encoders.

## Accuracy Tests

Evaluated with the model repository's own harness (`research/eval/laya_eval.py`), the one its weekly regression workflow runs: `mteb/amazon_massive_intent`, `en`, `test`, 100 cases, 20 options, seed 13.

| | accuracy | macro F1 | ECE | mean confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| committed baseline | 0.8200 | 0.7876 | 0.1382 | 0.9582 |
| reference SDK | 0.8200 | 0.7876 | 0.1382 | 0.9582 |
| SGLang (bf16) | 0.8200 | 0.7876 | 0.1371 | 0.9571 |
| SGLang (fp32) | 0.8200 | 0.7876 | 0.1382 | 0.9582 |

The repository's `research/evals/check_regression.py` gate passes (`exit=0`, tolerances 0.02 / 0.03 / 0.03). In fp32 the per-case probabilities match the reference to 1.5e-5 (mean 1e-6) with the chosen option identical in 100 of 100 cases; the bf16 difference is dtype rounding, amplified by the 0.5 temperature the checkpoint uses for this question shape.

Backend comparison on the same evaluation: with `--attention-backend fa3` the accuracy drops to 0.8100 with 96 of 100 per-case agreement, which is why the encoder computes its own attention. Sweeping the local-attention radius (63 / 64 / 65) gives the exact published macro F1 and the best per-case agreement only at 64.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. For scale, the 421M-parameter checkpoint answered the 100 requests above in 3.3 s end to end over HTTP; that is a sanity figure, not a benchmark.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: Fix ROCm MHA FP8 projection after prefix KV restoration
body:
## Motivation

On gfx95 with block-scaled FP8 `kv_b_proj`, ROCm MHA preparation normalizes and quantizes only the newly appended tokens. MHA one-shot prefix restoration then replaces `kv_a` and `k_pe` with the complete cached-prefix-plus-suffix tensors, but projection still consumes the old suffix-only quantized tuple. K/V consequently have fewer rows than the restored RoPE keys and the attention metadata; the key concatenation raises a shape mismatch.

This applies to projections recognized by `_is_block_scale_fp8` (FP8 weights with a multi-column `weight_scale`), with restored BF16 KV as well as the FP8-dequantization and DCP gathering branches. Serialized FP8 projections exposing only `weight_scale_inv` do not take this fused path and are covered as unchanged controls. FP8 weight precision is independent of KV-cache precision.

## Modifications

Invalidate the precomputed quantized tuple when restoring a prefix, then project the full, already normalized KV through the linear layer's ordinary input quantization. Keep the fused tuple for requests without a restored prefix. Cached KV is not RMS-normalized a second time.

Add a CPU regression using the actual prepare method with mocked GPU kernel/cache boundaries. It checks complete K/V values and row order against a full-prefill reference for mixed prefix lengths, BF16/FP8 cache restoration, DCP, block-scale/serialized-FP8/BF16 weights and the no-prefix fast path. The test uses the real `_is_block_scale_fp8` predicate, including its `weight_scale_inv` fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mha_prefix_kv.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_nope_mha_k_cast.py
```

34 passed with CPU PyTorch. On unchanged upstream `0bc074db83286449b96198eb340dacdf89041650`, the six new FP8-weight cases with nonempty prefixes reproduce the expected tensor-size mismatch; the other twenty-one new cases pass. The candidate passes all twenty-seven new cases.

These tests import the actual engine module and use CPU tensors with mocked GPU kernels; real GPU kernels and model output accuracy have not yet been validated for this change. The PR remains draft pending that validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The no-prefix fused projection is retained. Prefix restoration uses the existing linear-layer input-quantization path; this PR makes no performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Added registered CPU regression coverage and an unpatched negative control.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] GPU model accuracy and performance validation.

This is an independent ROCm attention fix; it does not depend on the Mooncake early-send synchronization change in #41395.

title: [Model] Support Qwen3.5 text checkpoints with language_model prefix
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Some fine-tuned and distilled text-only Qwen3.5 community checkpoints (such as `Mapika/decider-2b`) retain the `model.language_model.*` hierarchy inherited from the multimodal Qwen base training stack in their `model.safetensors`, while setting their architecture to `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`.
Currently, `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` strips only `model.`, which causes all backbone weights to fail to match the inner backbone model (`qwen3_5.py`). As a result, the weights remain uninitialized (causing NaN logits and null logprobs at inference).
Following the existing patterns in `KimiK25` (`kimi_k25.py`), `Cosmos3` (`cosmos3.py`), and `GraniteMoE` (`granitemoe.py`), this PR adds `hf_to_sglang_mapper` to `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` to remap `model.language_model.` and `language_model.` to `model.` lazily.

## Modifications

In `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_text.py`:
- Imported `WeightsMapper` from `sglang.srt.models.utils`.
- Declared `hf_to_sglang_mapper` on `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` with `orig_to_new_prefix={"model.language_model.": "model.", "language_model.": "model."}`.
- In `load_weights`, applied `mapper = getattr(self, "hf_to_sglang_mapper", None)` lazily before stripping the model prefix.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested loading weights against Mapika/decider-2b (320 checkpoint tensors):
- Before this change: 0 backbone weights loaded (resulting in uninitialized weights / NaN logits).
- After this change: All 320 weights match and load successfully into the backbone without missing keys.
- Standard clean checkpoints (with model.* keys) continue to load with zero modification.

```
from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_text import Qwen3_5ForCausalLM
mapper = getattr(Qwen3_5ForCausalLM, "hf_to_sglang_mapper", None)
assert mapper.apply_list([
    "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "model.language_model.layers.0.input_layernorm.weight",
    "language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "lm_head.weight",
]) == [
    "model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "model.layers.0.input_layernorm.weight",
    "model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "lm_head.weight",
]
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: This change only affects weight name mapping at load time and has zero impact on inference kernels or runtime execution speed.

## Checklist

- [X] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: feat(kda): integrate FlashInfer prefill checkpoints
body:
## Motivation

[FlashInfer #5021](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5021), released in 0.7.0, adds indexed, floor-aligned checkpoints to CuTe DSL KDA prefill. SGLang needs the state at the last complete chunk boundary for radix prefix caching (for example, token 128 of a 130-token extend).

## Modifications

- Add an opt-in KDA prefill adapter for BF16, 128-dimensional safe-gate KDA on SM100/SM103: `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer`.
- Map FlashInfer's packed checkpoints to SGLang's radix-cache track rows, including FP32 state pools and padded gate/beta buffers. Keep beta as logits for this path.
- Route unsupported shapes, speculative draft extend, and CUDA graph capture through the existing Triton kernel.

The FlashInfer package and Docker version pins stay unchanged in this PR. A separate dependency PR must provide FlashInfer 0.7.0 before this path can run in standard images.

## Accuracy Tests

On the 8xGB300 devbox, with FlashInfer 0.7.0 installed on both ranks:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New FlashInfer KDA prefill tests (BF16/FP32 states, indexed and padded state pools, strided K3 beta, 130→128 checkpoint, full attention backend path) | 5 passed |
| Existing FlashInfer KDA decode/verify tests | 11 passed |
| CuTe DSL KDA prefill and FlashInfer GDN checkpoint smoke tests | 2 passed |

The GB300 tests pass, including a strided-beta case that fails if the FlashInfer adapter falls back to Triton. Format, lint, registry, and bare-pytest checks pass (the latter on the devbox with Python 3.12). A TP8/DCP8 Kimi K3 dummy-weight request completed with FlashInfer KDA prefill active. Real-weight output parity remains to be checked.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300 adapter-level prefill microbenchmark, after warmup, without checkpoint tracking:

| Batch × tokens/request | Triton | FlashInfer | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 × 128 | 481 µs | 359 µs | 1.34× |
| 16 × 128 | 552 µs | 227 µs | 2.43× |
| 64 × 256 | 620 µs | 218 µs | 2.84× |

Across nine shapes (batch 4/16/64 × 64/128/256 tokens), measured speedup was 1.14–2.84×. This measures the adapter call, including its tensor conversions; it excludes projection, convolution, scheduler work, and checkpoint-copy overhead.

For the requested 95% prefix hit shape (batch 1, 131,072 input tokens, 124,518 cached, 6,554 new; K3 TP8-like H12/D128, FP32 state), three independent synthetic adapter runs gave:

| Checkpoint tracking | Triton | FlashInfer | Triton / FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Off | 760–851 µs | 553–598 µs | 1.34–1.42× |
| On | 655–764 µs | 711–848 µs | 0.90–0.93× |

Each figure is the median of 12 calls after warmup. The tracked path includes indexed checkpoint allocation and copy. These are per-layer synthetic timings, not full K3 request latency.

### Full Kimi K3, matched dummy weights

On two nodes / 8×GB300, both arms used the same local Kimi K3 NVFP4 config with `--load-format dummy --speculative-draft-load-format dummy`; only `--linear-attn-prefill-backend` changed. Workload: batch 1, 131,072 input, 1,024 output, requested 95% prefix hit, TP8/DCP8/DP1/EP1, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, DSPARK (block 7, 1 step, topk 1, 8 draft tokens), simulated acceptance length 5.5, spec ReplaySSM with `extra_buffer`. The cache actually reused 124,416 tokens and extended 6,656 (94.92% hit) on both arms.

| Prefill backend | Unprofiled latency | TTFT | Output throughput | Acceptance length |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Triton | 9.328 s | 6.845 s | 412.30 tok/s | 5.52 |
| FlashInfer | 9.342 s | 6.844 s | 409.81 tok/s | 5.53 |

Separate CPU+GPU EXTEND and DECODE traces were captured for 16 steps on all 8 TP ranks. In the EXTEND traces, median summed KDA kernel GPU time across ranks was 29.07 ms for Triton and 15.09 ms for FlashInfer (1.93×), across 69 KDA calls per rank. FlashInfer traces contain its CuTe DSL prefill kernels and no Triton KDA compute kernels. The summed kernel durations are not request wall time; communication, MLA, and MoE dominate this TP8/DCP8 request. One unprofiled request per arm showed no measurable end-to-end gain. Dummy weights validate routing and allow a matched performance baseline, but do not establish output parity with real model weights.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code style checks
- [x] Add registered tests
- [x] Update test coverage documentation
- [x] Provide kernel-level accuracy and speed results
- [x] Profile matched full Kimi K3 requests with dummy weights and confirm FlashInfer KDA kernels run
- [ ] Validate full Kimi K3 output parity with model weights

title: [diffusion] Refactor ComfyUI integrated mode onto native pipelines + adapters
body: ## Summary ComfyUI integrated mode is no longer a third copy of each diffusion pipeline. It is a **DiT-only runtime profile** on the native Flux / Z-Image / Qwen pipelines (`--comfyui-mode`). - Drop the three `comfyui_*_pipeline.py` forks (~1450 lines). - Keep one shared executor. Model differences live in a **checkpoint spec** (single-file `.safetensors` remap) and a **step adapter** (`pack` / `unpack` / `fill_req`). - Keep the existing process topology (ComfyUI process + spawned workers). Local hops use **CUDA IPC handles** instead of pickling GPU tensors through host memory. Multi-rank `--comfyui-mode` detaches CUDA tensors and broadcasts them over **NCCL**. Conditioning is cached in a **run-scoped worker session**. Adding another image DiT that already has ComfyUI UNET / CLIP / VAE / KSampler should be two small files, not another 400–700 line pipeline. ## Motivation Integrated mode exists so ComfyUI keeps CLIP, VAE, the sampler loop, CFG, and community nodes, while SGLang only accelerates the DiT. That boundary is unchanged. The old implementation encoded that boundary by **copying a pipeline and an executor per model**. Flux / Z-Image / Qwen already had native pipelines. The ComfyUI copies existed only because: 1. ComfyUI gives a single `.safetensors` UNET, not `model_index.json`. 2. The worker must run one DiT step with a pass-through scheduler. 3. ComfyUI key names do not match SGLang `param_names_mapping`. `comfyui_mode` was already scattered through `DenoisingStage` / `SamplingParams`, but it was never a first-class profile, so each new model copied the skeleton again. | Layer | Before | Actually model-specific | | --- | --- | --- | | `ComfyUIXxxPipeline` | ~1450 lines across 3 files | weight mapping, QKV split, scale/shift order | | `XxxExecutor` | ~300 lines across 4 classes | pack / unpack, timestep scale, which `Req` fields get embeds | | `generator.py` tables | edit two dicts per model | none | A new image DiT needed ~500 lines of glue. Most of it was identical. ## Architecture - **Befor** (loop, CFG, `model_options` callables, community nodes) stays in the ComfyUI process. - **After** (DiT, SP/TP, TeaCache / BCG / FSDP) stays in the SGLang workers. - **Between** them: tensors only (IPC-able). No Python closures across the process boundary. No new `comfyui_*_pipeline.py`. `pipeline_class_dict` / `executor_class_dict` are generated from `adapter.model_types`. ## Why this is easier to extend | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | New image DiT | pipeline 400–700 + executor 70–170 + two registries | **checkpoint spec + adapter** (Qwen spec ~55, Z-Image ~63, typical adapter 40–90) | | Weight mapping | ComfyUI copy + native config, easy to diverge | one `ComfyUICheckpointSpec`; `inherit_config_mapping` when the two mappings share a source namespace | | Loader features | Flux used a 175-line handwritten `state_dict` loop (no FSDP / quant) | shared `TransformerLoader` / `weights_iterator` (same shape as GGUF) | | H3 / packed video | executor only understood `forward(x, t, context)` + 4D image pack | `PackedForward.extra_req` and nested latents are reserved; H3 adapter is **not** in this PR | | Server mode | untouched | untouched | Concrete correctness win from making the profile real: the old Flux ComfyUI loader **merged** native `FluxConfig.param_names_mapping` (targets like `to_qkv`, `ff.linear_in`) with the ComfyUI aliases. Mapping is applied to a fixpoint, so already-correct diffusers names were rewritten to names the live module does not have. The handwritten loader built on a real device and left unmatched params **randomly initialized** with a warning. The new path builds on meta device and errors instead, which is how the bug surfaced. Flux now sets `inherit_config_mapping=False`. Z-Image keeps `True` because its native mapping must merge split `to_q/k/v` back into fused `to_qkv`. The adapter interface is sized for H3 (nested latents, structured payload), not for Flux's three-tensor case. This PR does **not** add MiniMax-H3 support; it stops the next model from needing another pipeline fork. ## Transport / performance These hops were using the **per-request** distribution path on every **sampler step**. | Hop | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | ComfyUI ↔ rank 0 | `pickle.dumps` copies CUDA tensors to host. Measured: **460 KB tensor → 461 KB pickle** | `CudaIpcRef` handle. Unit test: handle pickle **< 2 KB**. Receiver `_new_shared_cuda` + `clone` | | Multi-rank `--comfyui-mode` | whole `Req` over `broadcast_pyobj` / gloo CPU, then `_fix_tensor_device` | control envelope still gloo; GPU tensors via existing NCCL `broadcast_tensor_dict`. General SP / CFG / TP `recv` is **unchanged** | | Conditioning | CLIP / pooled / image embeds resent every step | `comfyui_session_id`; later steps send latent + timestep | On current image models this is **not** a large wall-clock win. Flux 1024² packed latent is ~0.5 MB/step, so host pickle was already cheap next to DiT (~124 ms Flux / ~232 ms Qwen). The leftover ~10 ms/step is mostly scheduler wakeup, not the tensor copy. The transport work is for correctness and the next model: stay off host pickle / gloo, keep GPU tensors as IPC / NCCL handles, and cache conditioning so later steps do not resend embeds. A video DiT (H3 ~14 MB/step) would otherwise copy gigabytes over a full sampler. Processes stay separate on purpose — folding ComfyUI into rank-0 would shave that last ~10 ms, but mixes its event loop with NCCL and process-global CUDA state. ## Test plan - [x] `test/unit/test_comfyui_profile.py` — profile assembly + Flux synthetic single-file load (meta device, fused QKV / adaLN) - [x] `test/unit/test_comfyui_adapters.py` — pack / unpack - [x] `test/unit/test_comfyui_session.py` — conditioning cache - [x] `test/unit/test_ipc_cuda.py` — handle pickle < 2 KB, cross-process roundtrip - [x] Weight convert equivalence vs the deleted pipelines on synthetic state dicts (Flux / Z-Image / Qwen names, merge info, values) - [x] Z-Image `comfyui_mode` one-step (`noise_pred` `[1, 16, 1, 90, 160]`) and ComfyUI-format single-file load (6.15B) - [x] Flux `comfyui_mode` 2-GPU one-step (`noise_pred` `[1, 3600, 64]`, ~0.7 s) - [ ] Full ComfyUI UI / KSampler workflow on a machine with matching `comfy_aimdo` / `comfy_kitchen` - [ ] Existing plugin e2e (`test_flux_pipeline.py`, `test_zimage_pipeline.py`, Qwen) on real checkpoints --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #36252148993](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36252148993) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36252148992](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36252148992) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36252149165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36252149165)

title: [diffusion] Add MiniMax-H3 to ComfyUI integrated mode
body: ## Motivation #35960 turns ComfyUI integrated mode into a DiT-only profile on the native pipeline (adapter + checkpoint spec). Flux / Z-Image / Qwen already sit on that path. MiniMax-H3 does not: it is a packed `[video, audio]` DiT with T2V, I2VA, FL2VA, and R2V layouts that ComfyUI already ships as community graphs. This PR adds H3 to that same contract so ComfyUI keeps CLIP / VAE / the sampler loop, and SGLang runs one packed DiT forward per `apply_model`. 24GB skip-step speed-ups are not in this stack. They land in [#35858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35858) (Cache-DiT + layerwise) and [#35684](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35684) (Spectrum). After those merge, a follow-up will expose the recommend recipes on `SGLDOptions`. ## Modifications - **H3 adapter + worker step** — pack/unpack `[video, audio]`, translate ComfyUI layout / RoPE / denoise mask, match the official audio sigma-shift ODE. - **Checkpoint spec** — register MiniMax-H3; GGUF overlay; read AdaLN curve from pruned BF16 so the DiT is not built as the unpruned MLP. - **Session / generator** — cache scoped to one `sampler.sample()`; one SGLD generator per process (two-pass upscaler and back-to-back H3 graphs). - **TP** — shard fused `MergedColumn` per logical matrix. - **Shipped graphs** — T2V, R2V, two-pass latent upscaler. ## Workflows **ComfyUI R2V UI**： Shipped under `apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/workflows/`: | Graph | Task | | --- | --- | | `minimax_h3_t2v_sgld.json` | T2V / fl2va DiT | | `minimax_h3_r2v_sgld.json` | Reference-to-video | | `minimax_h3_t2v_sgld_upscaler.json` | Low-res then 3D ×2 refine | Also tested on this branch (H3 only): | Task | Result | | --- | --- | | I2VA (first frame) / FL2VA (first+last) | OK | | R2V image / R2V video+audio | OK (needs the `ref2va` checkpoint) | | `kitchen_int8` + layerwise | OK | | pruned BF16 + layerwise | OK | | GGUF Q4 overlay | OK | | `sol_attn` / `sage_attn` | OK | | Cache-DiT | OK (24GB + layerwise coexist waits on #35858) | | lightx2v turbo LoRA on BF16 | OK | | Same UNET sampled twice | OK | | GGUF × LoRA | Rejected (expected) | GGUF × LoRA is fail-closed. kitchen-int8 × LoRA is not. H3 SP needs `ulysses_degree=2`. ## Tests Unit: `test_comfyui_h3.py` (layout vs ComfyUI, adapter, step kwargs, profile). 4090 D 24GB · ComfyUI 0.30.0 · CLIP on CPU. Wall is prompt e2e. Smoke (432×240 · 25f · 4 step) unless noted: | H3 path | Wall | | --- | ---: | | kitchen_int8 + sol + layerwise | 96 s | | pruned BF16 + layerwise | 104 s | | R2V ref2va + kitchen | 145 s | | Two-pass upscaler 432→864 | 217 s | 768P quality (1344×768 · 5s · 20 step · kitchen_int8 + FA + layerwise): | Task | Wall | | --- | ---: | | I2VA | 418 s | | FL2VA | 426 s | | R2V image | 609 s | | R2V video+audio | 1433 s | **Test Video：** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ba89329-84f9-4665-bfca-1858804281c1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b202a340-d01c-4b9d-b868-a695b6f15b10 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d00a06b-396d-4035-bea9-414c99e4af26 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36207417721](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36207417721) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36207417476](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36207417476) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36207417726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36207417726)

title: [NPU] Support w8a8_int/w4a4_int online quantization
body: ## Overview This PR adds online integer quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 checkpoints on Ascend NPU. It supports load-time weight conversion and dynamic activation quantization for SRT dense linear and MoE layers, plus the native diffusion W8A8 path. The supported SRT modes are: - `w8a8_int`: W8A8 for supported dense projections and MoE experts. - `w4a4_int`: mixed Qwen3-MoE mode, using W8A8 for dense projections and W4A4 for MoE `w13`/`w2` experts. Dense-only architectures are rejected because dense W4A4 has not met the accuracy requirement. This is separate from offline ModelSlim or other pre-quantized checkpoint formats. ## Key Changes ### SRT Ascend online quantization - Selects online W8A8 for unquantized NPU `q/k/v/qkv/o`, `gate/up/gate_up`, and `down` projections. Existing checkpoint-quantized and non-NPU paths are unchanged. - Converts dense and MoE source weights as soon as their logical shards are completely loaded, instead of retaining a full-model FP16/BF16 copy until post-load processing. - Preserves shard-aware QKV, merged-column, row-parallel, TP, and EP loading behavior. - Uses `npu_dynamic_quant` for weight and activation quantization, then `npu_quant_matmul` or NPU grouped matmul with backend-required weight and scale layouts. - Validates dense and MoE completion-tracked loader state before post-load use, including reload handling. - Detects Ascend through the runtime torch-NPU path so dense online quantization also works when no out-of-tree `SRTPlatform` plugin is active. ### W4A4 policy - Keeps known-good Qwen3-MoE W4A4 expert layouts for `w13` and W8A8 for `w2`. - Keeps dense projections on W8A8 in mixed mode. - Rejects `--online-quantization w4a4_int` for unsupported dense architectures during NPU argument resolution. ### Diffusion - Adds the native Ascend `w8a8_int` transformer quantization method for unquantized diffusion components. - Keeps diffusion component quantization routed through `--transformer-quantization` / component quantization settings rather than the SRT LLM flag. ### Tests and documentation - Adds focused NPU unit coverage for mode selection, dense projection policy, source dtypes, scale layouts, loader completion states, reload behavior, and platform detection. - Documents the SRT and diffusion online quantization interfaces. ## Usage ### Qwen3-32B W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w8a8_int ``` ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w4a4_int ``` ### MiniMax-H3 diffusion W8A8 ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ sglang serve \ --model-path /home/weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 8 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --transformer-quantization w8a8_int \ --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload ``` ## Validation ### Qwen3-32B dense path bf16: w8a8: ### MiniMax-H3 BF16: W8A8: ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 BF16: W8A8: Mixed W4A4/W8A8: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide available accuracy and memory results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36118689166](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36118689166) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36118689217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36118689217) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36118689163](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36118689163)

title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 Spectrum skip-step + fused RMSNorm/AdaLN
body:
## Summary

Wires training-free Spectrum skip-step into MiniMax-H3 and fuses RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN. 
On one 24GB GPU, 50-step BF16+FA (**1008.6 s**) drops to **285.3 s (3.53×)** with exact attention, up to **219.0 s (4.61×)** with Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum.

1344×768 · 107 frames · 50 NFE · same process: warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), timed only. PSNR is per-frame vs the **same-tree** INT8+FA video (Spectrum off).

| Config | timed e2e | vs BF16+FA | PSNR mean / min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 + FlashAttention (baseline) | 1008.6 s | 1.00× | — |
| `kitchen_int8` + FA (Spectrum off) | 718.5 s | 1.40× | — |
| **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`** — recommend | **285.3 s** | **3.53×** | **27.37 / 25.28** |
| `kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 387.4 s | 2.60× | 30.82 / 28.69 |
| `kitchen_int8` + `sage_attn` + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 245.3 s | 4.11× | 23.56 / 21.01 |
| `kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum `15/5/0.5` | **219.0 s** | **4.61×** | 20.57 / 17.75 |
| *(external reference)* ComfyUI INT8 workflow | 752.6 s | 1.34× |- |

ComfyUI is a 24GB yardstick only. Same-INT8 gap is 752.6 vs 718.5 s (**1.05×**). 


## Motivation

[#34581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34581) already moved the 24GB path onto `kitchen_int8` + FlashAttention (~14 s/step). H3's default is **50 steps**, so the remaining cost is running the 50-layer stack every step (~12 min).

Cache-DiT (`quality="high"`) is the in-tree skip-compute for multi-GPU H3, but it cannot combine with `--dit-layerwise-offload`, so a 24GB card that must stream the DiT cannot use it. 
On the audited 4×H200 recipe it is also only 1.40× and still walks the first blocks. Spectrum ([arxiv:2603.01623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01623)) is already wired for FLUX.1 / Wan / HunyuanVideo / SD3: it forecasts DiT features and **skips the whole stack**, and it works with layerwise offload. H3 could not use it because the packed sequence is not a uniform video stream.

## Modifications

### 1. Spectrum on MiniMax-H3

Opt-in via `--enable-spectrum`. Off path does not enter the mixin — bit-exact vs today's H3.

- Forecast only the packed **target** suffix: contiguous target audio immediately before `infer_out_pos` video. Earlier reference-audio rows are dropped (Wan2GP `hidden[audio_start:]`).
- Comfy blends: **audio hold** (0), **video lerp 0.5**.
- History on CPU, default `history_size` 100 → **8** (24GB).
- `layer_names = ["blocks", "token_refiner.blocks"]` so a skip is the 50-layer stack, not a Cache-DiT wrap. Works with DiT layerwise offload.
- Fail-closed with `quality="high"` / `enable_cache_dit`, and with sequence-parallel `sp_ws > 1`.

Generic Spectrum defaults (`warmup=5, window=2, flex=0.75`) are the 20 NFE row. H3's model default is 50 steps; **`warmup=5` is a quality cliff there**. The recommended 50-step schedule is `11 / 5 / 1.0` (all frames >25 dB vs FA).

Sage / Sol + Spectrum is faster but the PSNR ceiling is the attention backend (~23.6 dB vs FA at 50 NFE). If the bar is "looks like FA", keep `fa`.

### 2. Fused RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN

`fused_indexed_rmsnorm_scale_shift` writes `RMSNorm(x) * (1+scale[idx]) + shift[idx]` without materializing the normalized tensor. Gate: BF16, not `torch.compile`; otherwise the existing eager modulate.

Lossless (1 ULP; `mean|Δ|≈2e-8`). Exclusive 20 NFE INT8+FA: 290.8 → **289.7 s** (−1.06 s, ~0.3%). Same kernel every step, so ~−2.3 s at 50 NFE. On whenever the Triton path matches; no flag.

## Accuracy Tests

Same prompt and seed (42). First pair is 50 NFE, exact attention; the Spectrum row is the recommend schedule. Second pair is 20 NFE library defaults.

**`kitchen_int8` + FA, 50 NFE — 718.5 s**

**`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`, 50 NFE — 285.3 s (27.4 dB)**

**`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `5/2/0.75`, 20 NFE — 189.5 s (25.6 dB)**

## Example

Exact-attention recommend (**3.53×** vs BF16) — INT8 Linear, FlashAttention, Spectrum `11/5/1.0`:

```bash
pip install comfy-kitchen   # required only for --quantization kitchen_int8

sglang generate \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --quantization kitchen_int8 \
  --attention-backend fa \
  --enable-spectrum \
  --spectrum-warmup-steps 11 \
  --spectrum-window-size 5 \
  --spectrum-flex-window 1.0 \
  --performance-mode memory \
  --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
  --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \
  --enable-torch-compile false \
  --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
  --save-output
```

Speed ceiling (**4.61×** vs BF16) — same offload, Sage→Sol hybrid on the DiT and Spectrum `15/5/0.5`. Approximate attention; PSNR 20.6 / 17.8 dB vs FA.

```bash
sglang generate \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
  --model-variant fl2va \
  --quantization kitchen_int8 \
  --attention-backend sol_attn \
  --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \
  --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \
  --enable-spectrum \
  --spectrum-warmup-steps 15 \
  --spectrum-window-size 5 \
  --spectrum-flex-window 0.5 \
  --performance-mode memory \
  --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
  --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \
  --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \
  --enable-torch-compile false \
  --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
  --save-output
```

`--layerwise-offload-components` omits `vae` (same as #34581). Omit `--enable-spectrum` and the three `--spectrum-*` flags for the 718 s INT8+FA path. At 20 NFE, `--enable-spectrum` alone is enough (library defaults). Drop `--quantization` for BF16.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

RTX 4090 D 24GB · CUDA 13.0 · 1344×768 / 107 frames / euler · `torch.compile` and Cache-DiT **disabled** · load → warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), **timed pass only**.

Cross-framework PSNR vs Comfy (~16 dB) is TE NVFP4 vs BF16 — not a quality column.

The `kitchen_int8` SwiGLU fuse (`int8_linear(input_act=swiglu)`) is **not** on in these numbers. Released `comfy-kitchen==0.2.26` leaves `silu*up` in fp32 and rewrites INT8 rows (50 NFE vs unfused: **22.0 / 19.8 dB** — a different sample). [comfy-kitchen#124](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen/pull/124) rounds to the storage dtype first; fc2 is then bit-exact and the fuse is about **−4.4 s / 20 NFE** (~−10 s at 50). Leave it off until that lands.

Results are in the table at the top. Text encoding and VAE decode are unchanged; Spectrum only skips selected DiT stacks.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format code with pre-commit hooks
- [ ] Unit tests: `test_minimax_h3_spectrum.py`
- [ ] Default (`--enable-spectrum` omitted) unchanged
- [ ] Cookbook + `spectrum.mdx` list MiniMax-H3 and the 50-step schedule
- [ ] Benchmark and PSNR vs same-tree FA included above

title: [diffusion] In-place LoRA merge/unmerge under layerwise offload
body:
## Motivation

### Memory limits on MiniMax-H3

- **GPU.** The BF16 DiT does not fit on a 24 GB card. Serving uses layerwise offload: weights live on the host, and only the current layer is streamed onto the GPU.
- **Host RAM.** The offload store is already the full weight set (mmap / pin budget). Cloning a second unmerge snapshot is another **38 GB** of anonymous memory on this DiT.
- **The previous runtime LoRA path.** `set_lora`, `merge_lora_weights`, `unmerge_lora_weights`, and `deactivate_lora_weights` all turned offload off and called `load_all` so they could see dense GPU tensors. That pulls the whole DiT onto the card and **OOMs**. Clearing or switching an adapter hits the same path: `unmerge` / `deactivate` restore `W` the same way `set_lora` writes it.

We cannot merge or unmerge by materializing the model, and we cannot afford a second host copy. Both writes have to run **in place** against the existing CPU store, one layer at a time.

### Relation to [#36062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36062)

[#36062](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36062) already fixed the **startup `--lora-path`** case. In-place merge copy-on-writes the checkpoint mapping, and the LoRA wrapper used to clone a full base snapshot for unmerging. Together that peaked at **75.3 GiB** of anonymous host memory on MiniMax-H3 + 4-step turbo LoRA. That PR copy-merges into a file-backed cache and keeps zero-copy unmerge views, so peak host anon falls to **19.2 GiB**.

It explicitly left the **runtime APIs on the in-place path**. This PR is that remaining surface:

| API | What it does |
|---|---|
| `set_lora` | load / apply / switch an adapter |
| `merge_lora_weights` | merge the currently loaded adapter into `W` |
| `unmerge_lora_weights` | restore the base (`W` back to pre-LoRA); required before switching |
| `deactivate_lora_weights` | clear LoRA: unmerge if needed, then disable the wrapper |

HTTP: `POST /v1/set_lora`, `/v1/merge_lora_weights`, `/v1/unmerge_lora_weights`. All four go through `_weight_update_context` and the same CPU writeback. `--lora-path` stays on the #36062 cache.

---

## Approach

Keep layerwise on for every runtime LoRA write (merge **and** unmerge / deactivate). For each layer, read the manager CPU view, run the update on GPU, write the result back with a blocking `copy_`, then release the GPU copy so the next prefetch reloads the new `W`:

```
src = CPU view (or live GPU weight if it is full-sized)
data = src.to(gpu)
data += scale * (B @ A)
dest.copy_(merged) into the CPU store   # blocking
release the stale GPU layer
```

Under offload the live `layer.weight` is a `(1,)` placeholder, so the write must hit the CPU store, not that placeholder. After wrap the live name becomes `*.base_layer.weight` while the manager still records `*.weight`; we alias that pair, rebind the manager to the same Parameter, and never replace the Parameter object. Unmerge snapshots stay zero-copy views of the CPU store (`snapshot_base=False`).

Applies to any `BaseLayerWithLoRA` + dense `weight`. Not GGUF/`qweight`, nested wraps, or DTensor.

---

## Experiments

### Dynamic `set_lora` / unmerge (this PR)

4090 D 24 GB, layerwise `dit,text_encoder`, MiniMax-H3 BF16 + lightx2v 4-step LoRA. `set_lora` after load (not `--lora-path`), then 5-step T2VA.

- Unit: aliases, park skips wrapped layers, writeback keeps the Parameter, view unmerge restores the base.
- E2E: `set_lora` does not `load_all` / OOM; the clip is a normal scene, not a color-noise grid.
- `merge` / `unmerge` / `deactivate` share the same writeback. Unmerge is unit-tested; no extra 5-step clip after unmerge.


---

## Performance

4090 D 24 GB, 4-step LoRA via `set_lora`:

| Stage | Time |
|---|---:|
| `set_lora` (208 layers) | **5.9 s** |
| denoise | ~99 s |
| generate | ~122 s |

A multi-stream H2D / compute / D2H pipeline was tried and dropped. Real merge is already a few seconds; overlapping transfers saved ~1 s and added a lot of code. Denoise still uses its existing prefetch `copy_stream` — that is inference, not LoRA merge.

title: fix(quantization): reject K tiles that cross block-fp8 quantization blocks
body:
## Summary

`w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton` indexes one `As`/`Bs` scale per compute tile, so a compute K tile must sit entirely inside one quantization K block. A hand-supplied `BLOCK_SIZE_K` that does not evenly divide the quantization block (e.g. `64` against `block_size=[32, 32]`) makes `n_tiles_k_per_group_k` zero, the scale pointer never advances past the first block, and the kernel silently returns wrong values: on the reporter's deterministic example every output is 64 where the right answer is 288. The official tuner never emits such a config, so the failure only shows for manual configurations.

The wrapper now fails closed: `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton` raises a `ValueError` naming the incompatibility whenever `block_size[1] % BLOCK_SIZE_K != 0`, before launching either kernel variant (the gfx1250 variant has the same per-tile scale semantics).

## Changes

- `fp8_kernel.py`: the fail-closed check after config selection, covering both kernel variants.
- `test_block_fp8.py`: a test that runs the reporter's exact shapes both ways — `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` raises with the incompatibility named, and the aligned `BLOCK_SIZE_K=32` still computes the expected 288.

## Verification

- Mechanism verified statically against the kernel: with `group_k // BLOCK_SIZE_K == 0`, `scale_step_k` can never advance `As_ptrs`/`Bs_ptrs` past block 0, so all 64 K elements are charged block 0's scales, exactly the reported 64-vs-288.
- The new test compiles; on this machine there is no GPU and no macOS triton build, so the runtime check (rejection fires and the aligned config computes 288) is left to GPU CI, stated plainly rather than dressed up as locally run.

Fixes #39626

title: [mem_cache] Replace `cache_finished_req` with `insert_req`; `release_kv_cache` frees and unpins
body:
- `cache_finished_req(req, *, owned_kv_len)` -> `insert_req(req, *, up_to)`: the tree only inserts and advances `cache_protected_len`; it no longer frees slots or drops the lock
- `release_kv_cache` does the release on both paths: optional `insert_req`, then free `[cache_protected_len, owned_kv_len)`, the over-allocated tail, `unpin`, `on_release`
- `register_session_ref(req, leaf=...)` takes the leaf the insert ended on instead of reading `req.last_node`, which now stays the lock anchor until `unpin`
- Tests: tree-level finish calls go through `finish_req` (`sglang/test/mem_cache_utils.py`) or `release_kv_cache`; stale `cache_finished` test names renamed

title: dsv4.1-amd: serve DeepSeek-V4.1 on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

Integration PR of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD (gfx950 / MI350X) series. It follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain with no callers, then this PR with the callers. With it, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves on gfx950 with DSpark.

**This branch carries the unmerged kernel PRs #41019, #41020 and #41021 (#41018 is merged). Review only the last commit.**

## Modifications

- **Attention.** `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` serves V4.1: the compact V4.1 KV pages through `compact_attention_hip` (#41020), the swap-AB Gluon kernel for small decode batches, DSpark draft and target-verify metadata, and breakable-CUDA-graph prefill. `dsv4/low_ratio_backend_hip.py` orchestrates the ratio-1 / 2 indexer, like main's `dsv4/v41_indexer`: FlyDSL fp4 paged MQA logits over the split index-K pools (#41019), then the candidate-block and sorted top-k kernels (#41020). `hip_flash_mla.py` routes the HIP decode kernels (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=auto`: aiter's sparse kernel on gfx950, tilelang elsewhere).
- **Dense fp8.** `fp8_hip.py` serves 32x32-block fp8 checkpoints as MXFP8 on the gfx950 native route (#41018); the RMSNorm, SiLU and wo_a producers hand it fp8-grid or MXFP8 operands (`deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_gfx95_dense.py`, `deepseek_v2_hip_act.py`).
- **mHC.** `deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` runs each sublayer boundary as one launch, with its Sinkhorn carried by the next RMSNorm, and the TP4 all-reduce fused with the mHC post for decode batches of 1-8 rows (#41021).
- **MoE and Engram.** The split-K router GEMV and gate for DeepSeek-V4 gates (#41019). Engram's all-reduce and reduce-scatter add BF16 rows as int32 on ROCm, so they are bit-exact.
- **Other.** DSpark runs on HIP. `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM` now defaults to on for ROCm.

The ROCm code lives in `models/deepseek_common/amd/` and the HIP backend files. `deepseek_v4.py` and `deepseek_v2.py` call into it only on HIP.

### Changes visible off ROCm
Each of these is a no-op for CUDA / NPU:
- `deepseek_v4.py`: `q=`, `inv_rope=` and `router_logits_partials=` are passed only when set. The hc_mix gate keeps CUDA's conditions. The three input-norm sites keep their gfx95-only fp8 quant, so gfx1250 is unchanged.
- `breakable_cuda_graph.py`: weak-ref'd NamedTuple arguments keep their type (a NamedTuple still indexes as a tuple).
- `dspark_draft_model.py`: the stacked-dequant path requires a 2-D weight.
- `deepseek_v4_backend.py`: the split index-K store is taken only when the pool reports the split layout, which is HIP only.

## Tests

- **Tests.** Runtime tests sit with their subsystem, as in #38798: the HIP backend, fused-compress and aiter_sparse backend tests in `attention/unittests/dsv4/`; the wo_a, MoE, fused-mHC and TP4 torchrun model tests in `unit/models/`; kernel cases live in the kernel PRs. All pass on MI350X on this branch with the kernel PRs' tests; the TP4 test compares fused and unfused mHC outputs eagerly (registered-buffer copy-in) and under graph replay.
- **End to end.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x MI350X, TP4 / EP4, DSpark, `--attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --disable-radix-cache`, `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`. The comparison is back to back on one node against this series' previous integration head (3e8187fa88, kept as `dsv41-amd-4-model-old-stack`), same flags, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128`. The old head aborts in aiter's `_varctx_cta_info_kernel` when it captures decode graphs above 128; #41019's in-tree schedule fixes that.

  This PR's numbers are from the current head (e8d0b1e653); GSM8K is five runs.

  | | previous head | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | GSM8K (200 questions) | 0.895 | 0.891 (0.880-0.905) |
  | random 4096 in / 1024 out, concurrency 1 | 476.7 tok/s | 518.9 tok/s |
  | concurrency 8 | 1,779.6 tok/s | 1,931.4 tok/s |
  | concurrency 32 | 3,175.6 tok/s | 3,302.0 tok/s |

## Deployment note

Set `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` until ROCm/aiter#5802 is in the aiter pin. At the default bound, small batches take aiter's BF16-activation MoE route, which does not apply `swiglu_limit`.

## Not in this PR
- `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` is over 3k lines. Splitting out the late-layer tail and breakable-prefill sections, and binding more CUDA backend methods instead of HIP copies, are follow-ups.

title: dsv4.1-amd: gfx950 sparse decode attention and sorted top-k
body:
> This PR was "stack 3/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the third kernel PR; it does not depend on #41018 or #41019.

## Summary
- `ops/attention/sparse_decode_reduce_hip.py`: `gfx_sparse_split_reduce` combines the split-KV partials of aiter's gfx950 `pa_decode_sparse(..., skip_reduce=True)`, bitwise equal to aiter's own reduce, with the attention sink and an optional inverse RoPE of each head's tail.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/compact_attention_hip.py`: sparse decode attention that reads the compact V4.1 pages (528 B fp8 + ue8m0, 288 B e2m1 + e4m3) directly through aiter's gfx950 `_qkpv_fp8`, with main and extra slot ranges and 16-head groups.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/swapab_gluon_hip.py`: the 16-head swap-AB Gluon kernel for HIP, argument-compatible with the SM100 kernel (CDNA4 MFMA, bf16 hi + lo compensated PV). It reuses the SM100 module's `_load_v4`, which is plain Gluon; `swapab_attention` gains `inv_rope=None`.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/attn_glue_hip.py`: single-launch Triton replacements for the torch glue around the V4.1 sparse decode metadata, each bitwise equal to the torch expression in its docstring.
- ROCm AOT top-k (`deepseek_v4_topk.cu`, `sgl_kernel/top_k.py`): `sort_output` sorts each row's picks ascending with a block-wide bitonic sort, `-1` padding last; the selected set is unchanged; the sort is ROCm-only (under `USE_ROCM`). Strides below the wave width use lane shuffles and the rest LDS, so it is also right on 32-lane waves (gfx1250).
- `q_rope_store.py` on HIP rounds like the batched HIP RoPE kernel.
- `ops/attention/dsv4/candidate_blocks_hip.py`, beside main's `candidate_blocks.py`: the V4.1 two-level indexer's level-one block scores and top blocks, the top-k within the chosen blocks and the paged top-k sorted in the AOT epilogue, graph-safe.
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `decode_attention_sm100.py`: `swapab_attention` takes an optional `partial_gluon` (`swapab_gluon_hip.swapab_attention` binds the gfx950 kernel), with no HIP branch in the SM100 file; `_combine` compiles the inverse RoPE out when `inv_rope=None`, so SM100 output is unchanged. `decode_attention_sm100_gluon.py` is untouched.
- `q_rope_store.py`: the new branch is a HIP-only constexpr; CUDA arithmetic is unchanged.
- The top-k epilogue, op schema and declaration are ROCm-only (`setup_rocm.py`); with `sort_output=False` the kernel is the same, plus a 4 KB static LDS array. The wrapper always passes `sort_output`, so sgl-kernel must be rebuilt from this PR.

## Verification
- New tests: `test_swapab_attention.py` (SM100 and gfx950: fp64 reference over padded and poisoned pages, `-1` / out-of-range slots, sinks, graph replay, and the combine's inverse RoPE bitwise to `fused_rope_inplace`); `test_compact_attention_hip.py` (both packed layouts, a second cache, `-1` slots and a key-less row against a torch softmax with sink); `test_topk.py::test_deepseek_v4_topk_transform_sorted_output`; `test_dsv41_decode_glue_hip.py` (candidate blocks against main's `select_candidate_block_ids` with garbage past each row's reach, the sorted mapping, and the `attn_glue_hip` builders bitwise to their torch forms). `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py` is now also registered for AMD.
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): these tests pass on this branch. The top-k epilogue built from this source matches the installed op over 120 shapes (sorted rows bitwise, unsorted rows the same set) and compiles for gfx1250.
- With the integration PR's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 / EP4 with DSpark serves and scores 0.900-0.905 on GSM8K (200 questions, two runs).
- [ ] Pending on an SM100 runner: `test_swapab_attention.py`, `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`.

## Stack
- Base: `main`. Independent of #41018 (gfx950 MXFP8 matmul kernels) and #41019 (KV cache layouts, FP4 indexer, compressor and router kernels).

title: fix(parser): keep trailing visible text in qwen3_coder one-shot parsing
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40739. For the same complete output, `qwen3_coder`'s non-streaming and streaming paths returned different visible content: `detect_and_parse` built `normal_text` only from `text[:start_idx]`, so `before<tool_call>...</tool_call>after` yielded `content="before"` non-streaming but `"beforeafter"` streaming. Visible text the model emitted after (or between) tool calls was silently dropped on the one-shot path.

## Modifications

One-shot parsing now carves complete `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` blocks out of the text and keeps the rest, matching what the streaming state machine emits for the same output (text before, between, and after calls). An unclosed trailing block or a partial tag is still cut, so malformed tails do not leak into visible content either. Three tests cover the parity: trailing text after a call, text between two calls, and the unclosed-tail case.

## Accuracy Tests

Not kernel/model-forward code; no accuracy impact. Parser-level unit coverage below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed impact (one regex substitution per non-streaming response).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code: `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` and `ruff format --check` clean on both touched files (repo pre-commit gate).
- [x] Unit tests: `TestQwen3CoderDetector` 20/20 pass; the two new parity tests fail pre-fix (`'before' != 'beforeafter'`) and pass here. Full `test_function_call_parser.py`: 238 passed; 15 failures are all DeepSeek detector classes erroring on `PreTrainedConfig` import from the locally installed `transformers` 4.56.1 (repo pins 5.12.1), identical with the change reverted, so environment-only.
- [x] Documentation: no user-facing config/API change; behavior now matches the documented streaming semantics.
- [x] Accuracy/speed benchmarks: not applicable (see above).

title: feat(npu): Support returning indexer top-k results
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`enable_return_indexer_topk` currently supports the CUDA indexer path, but the NPU backend does not create an indexer-topk capturer or expose the top-k results produced by NPU attention indexers.

  Ascend NPU already provides indexer implementations for:

  - DeepSeek DSA models, through `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer`
  - DeepSeek-V4 C4 indexers, through `torch.ops.custom.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`

  However, their results were not connected to the existing request-level return pipeline. As a result, NPU inference requests could not return indexer top-k metadata even when `--enable-return-indexer-topk` and `return_indexer_topk=true` were specified.

  This PR connects the NPU producer paths to the existing indexer-topk capturer and response pipeline while preserving the same output format and layer-index semantics as the CUDA implementation.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Enable indexer-topk capturer creation on both CUDA and NPU backends.
    - Model-specific layer counts continue to be resolved through `get_num_indexer_layers()`.
    - DSA models use one capturer slot per transformer layer.
    - DeepSeek-V4 uses one capturer slot per C4 compression layer.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DSA path.
    - Capture results from `forward_dsa_prepare_npu()`.
    - Cover both freshly computed top-k results and `skip_topk` layers that reuse the previous layer's result.
    - Preserve the transformer layer id in the capturer layout.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DeepSeek-V4 C4 path.
    - Capture the output of `npu_quant_lightning_indexer`.
    - Use `token_to_kv_pool.layer_mapping[].compress_layer_id` to map raw transformer layers to contiguous C4 capturer slots.
    - Keep the captured indices in the logical compressed-token coordinate system used by the NPU sparse attention path.

- Extend overlap result handling to NPU.
    - Reuse the existing `TopkCaptureOutput` and result-finalization pipeline.
    - Add NPU support to asynchronous device-to-host copies through `torch.get_device_module()`.
    - Preserve the existing synchronous path when overlap scheduling is disabled.

- Add unit tests covering:
    - NPU DSA capturer initialization.
    - DeepSeek-V4 C4 layer-count resolution.
    - Non-indexer models being disabled through a zero indexer-layer count.
    - Invalid `index_topk` configurations.

title: [AMD] [Docker] Remove unused LLVM 18 setup from ROCm TileLang build
body:
## Motivation

ROCm image publishing can stop in the TileLang layer when the base image lacks `llvm-config`. The fallback fetches the LLVM 18 signing key from apt.llvm.org; all six connection attempts failed in the [September 26 gfx942/ROCm 7.2 job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36257578919/job/108447174957). The same failure affected other image variants in the [September 18 run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35343480132).

## Change

Remove the LLVM download, `llvm-config-16` shim, and `LLVM_CONFIG` build argument from the TileLang layer. The [pinned TVM configuration](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/34fac3091232a90d4e8b376aa25e1599a0ac189a/cmake/config.cmake#L146) disables LLVM, and a [successful gfx942/ROCm 7.2 build](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36227908720/job/108365372487) reported that `LLVM_CONFIG` was unused while building ROCm support.

## Validation

- [Lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36291904313) at PR commit `3d5d3ab`.
- A [full no-push gfx942/ROCm 7.2 Docker build](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36291676377/job/108542833175) passed at commit `4977123` with the nightly build arguments and `--no-cache`. TileLang imported from the final image.
- At PR commit `3d5d3ab`, the [existing ROCm 7.2 publisher](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36303271364/job/108574867258) built the `gfx942-rocm720` image and pushed `v0.5.20-rocm720-mi30x-20260927` to both `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Both Docker Hub tags resolve to `sha256:5227edbab9a7634cf1b3880f8b91496d1459cac3095f53c87123c86b58240f33`. The TileLang layer compiled and installed successfully. This validates the image build and publication; GPU runtime tests were not part of this run.

title: [XPU] Enable ring attention on XPUAttentionBackend
body:
Ring attention was rejected on XPU by the admission check in layers/attention/layer.py before the kernel was ever called, because XPUAttentionBackend never overrode supports_ring_rotation() and so inherited False from AttentionBackend.

Declaring support is not sufficient on its own: sgl-kernel-xpu returns the LSE as (nheads, total_q), and torch's ring-attention _SDPAMerger._merge_one raised a bare AssertionError, since one unsqueeze cannot bring a 2D LSE to the rank of the 4D output. usp.py's adapter permutes the output to [b, h, s, d] but leaves the LSE untouched, so the impl has to return the LSE as [b, h, s] to broadcast correctly.
