title: [SM120] Add optional FlashInfer PCIe-IPC all-reduce for switch-free hosts
body:
## Motivation

On switch-free intra-node hosts — no NVLink, no multicast, every peer transfer crossing the CPU root complex — none of SGLang's custom all-reduce backends apply. `CustomAllreduce` and `QuickAllReduce` assume NVLink/multicast, `pymscclpp` assumes its own fabric, so on these machines **every per-layer reduction falls back to NCCL**. NCCL's ring is bandwidth-optimal but latency-poor at decode message sizes, and it shows up directly in TPOT.

FlashInfer's `pcie_ipc` kernels ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4393](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4393)) target exactly this fabric: naive all-to-all peer writes collapse here, so the kernels *stage* their pushes to keep one outbound and one inbound stream per rank, and the 8-rank path uses a 4+4 island decomposition so the scarce cross-socket link carries the minimum.

This affects the whole RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 6000D class, where SGLang is otherwise well supported.

**Scope.** This is a decode-latency path, not a general NCCL replacement. It is sized so
prefill chunks stay on NCCL (see *Workspace sizing*), because these kernels win by latency
at small messages and lose to a ring at 200 MB. On a host that also wants prefill improved,
this composes with a bandwidth-optimal backend rather than replacing it.

## Modifications

Opt-in behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_PCIE_IPC_ALLREDUCE` (default off). +527/−0 across five files:

- **`distributed/device_communicators/pcie_ipc_ar.py`** (new) — adapter between `GroupCoordinator` and `PcieIpcAllReduceWorkspace`.
- **`distributed/parallel_state.py`** (+29) — construction, one `"pcie_ipc"` branch in `_resolve_outplace_all_reduce_method`, one dispatch arm. Built only on the TP group; other groups would just pin IPC buffers without issuing the reductions these kernels target.
- **`environ.py`** (+11) — the gate plus `SGLANG_PCIE_IPC_MAX_NUMEL`.
- **`model_executor/runner/base_runner.py`** (+9) — one `prepare()` call from warmup, before the FlashInfer autotune context opens. See *Autotuning* for why the timing is load-bearing.

Two design points worth review:

**No size heuristic lives in SGLang.** `should_pcie_ipc_ar()` delegates to `workspace.supports()`, which consults FlashInfer's own tuning table. A shape the kernels do not beat is reported unsupported and the caller keeps its NCCL path. This avoids a threshold knob that would need per-machine tuning and would drift from the kernel side. SGLang's job is to make sure that table is populated for this host and these shapes rather than left on the seed policy -- see *Autotuning*.

**The workspace is built on the first eligible tensor, not at group construction.** It cannot grow afterwards and costs ~`2 * world_size * max_numel * itemsize` per rank, so it must be sized for the largest reduction the model issues — one prefill chunk, `chunked_prefill_size * hidden`. `chunked_prefill_size` is in the server args but `hidden` is not known when the group is built, so construction is deferred to the first reduction, whose trailing dimension is exactly that. Ranks run the same reduction sequence, so they reach that call with the same shape and build the same workspace without extra exchange.

Sizing it for a prefill chunk instead is the wrong trade, which is worth
spelling out because an earlier revision of this PR did exactly that. These
kernels win by latency at small messages; a prefill chunk is three orders of
magnitude larger than a decode reduction, which is NCCL ring territory. Measured
at 8 ranks, TP8, 8k context:

| workspace | TTFT | TPOT | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| NCCL only | 1910 ms | 21.14 ms | 35.02 |
| prefill-sized (`chunked_prefill_size * hidden`) | 3176 ms | 13.64 ms | 38.43 |
| decode-sized (this PR) | **1849 ms** | **13.62 ms** | **48.05** |

Routing prefill through the kernels costs 66% on TTFT and buys nothing on TPOT.
The decode-sized workspace is also ~250x smaller, which matters at long context:
at 128k with 4 concurrent requests the prefill-sized workspace regressed TPOT by
45% (122.33 ms against NCCL's 84.50 ms), and that regression disappears once it
is sized for decode (84.60 ms).

## Autotuning

`supports()` answers from FlashInfer's tuning table, so what is in that table decides both which
shapes reach the kernels and which launch config they get. Left alone the table holds FlashInfer's
seed policy — a default, not a measurement of this host — so this wires the autotuner in: the
workspace is constructed with `tune_batches` bounded by what it will actually accept and with an
explicit `tune_cache` path, the coordinator's `cpu_group` is handed down as the autotuner's
rendezvous group, and `tune()` runs once when the workspace is built.

**The timing is the load-bearing part.** The workspace is built on the first eligible reduction,
and that reduction arrives inside SGLang's own FlashInfer autotune pass. FlashInfer declines to
profile a collective from an autotune context it did not open, so `tune()` returned having measured
nothing while still returning cleanly — zero `Tuning flashinfer::pcie_ipc_all_reduce` lines and no
cache written. `prepare(hidden)` is therefore called from the runner's warmup, just before that
context opens, which is where vLLM's port of these kernels does the same thing. `_tune()` refuses
and says so if it still finds itself nested, and it logs how many shapes `tune()` actually covered
rather than only that it returned: an autotune that measures nothing otherwise reads as a success,
which is exactly how two revisions of this change were misread.

Measured on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SE (SM120, PCIe, no NVLink), TP4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash,
decode-only TPOT via a warm-prefix method, 2 repeats per cell. Baseline is this PR's own tree with
the backend off, so both columns share one NCCL path:

| ISL | conc | FI AR off | as first submitted | with this fix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8k | 1 | 9.53 ms | 8.62 | **8.18** |
| 8k | 8 | 14.14 | 14.64 | **12.75** |
| 8k | 32 | 23.92 | 26.01 | **21.28** |
| 32k | 1 | 9.10 | 8.36 | **8.25** |
| 32k | 8 | 14.68 | 14.99 | **13.32** |
| 32k | 32 | 27.75 | 29.89 | **24.93** |
| 128k | 1 | 9.33 | 8.60 | **8.47** |
| 128k | 8 | 13.70 | 13.99 | **12.34** |

As first submitted this backend **regressed** decode at concurrency >= 8 (+2% to +4%); with the
table populated it is -9% to -14% across every cell. GSM8K 100q: 0.970.

**Where the win actually comes from, since it is not where I first assumed.** Running the same
build with the tuning genuinely executed and with it silently skipped lands within 1% on all eight
cells. The measured tactics are worth almost nothing here; the gain is the bucket alignment that
`tune_batches` brings, which changes which entry each shape resolves to. FlashInfer's seed tactics
are close to optimal on this fabric — what was wrong was asking the table about buckets the
workspace would never serve. The tuning call is still worth keeping: it is what makes the table
this host's own rather than a default, and on a fabric whose seed policy fits less well it is the
part that adapts.

Two consequences worth knowing before deploying:

- The cache key carries the PCIe topology (`pcieswitch-pairs` on this host, `rootcplx-noswitch` on
  another 8x SM120 box). **Tuning tables do not transfer between machine types**; a new host pays
  the measurement once, about 2 s for six shapes, and reuses it after that.
- Autotuning replays kernels and cannot run under graph capture. If the first reduction still
  arrives there, the seed policy stays in force and a warning says so.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 200 questions, same server and args as the perf runs:

| arm | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| NCCL | 0.960 | 0.000 |
| PCIe-IPC, prefill-sized workspace | 0.955 | 0.000 |
| PCIe-IPC, decode-sized (this PR) | 0.945 | 0.000 |

The 0.015 spread is 3 questions out of 200, within binomial noise at this sample
size (SE ~= 0.015). At the kernel level, 10 shapes from 1 to 16384 tokens at
world 8 / hidden 6144 / bf16 were compared elementwise against NCCL with 0
mismatches; the maximum absolute difference is a constant 2.5e-1, one bf16
quantization step at that magnitude, i.e. accumulation order rather than
corruption.

## Benchmarking Results

One 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition host, GPUs 0-3 and 4-7 on separate
NUMA nodes, no NVLink. Same tree, same client, same server args; the arms differ
by one environment variable.

```
image       lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260812-c7c03ec5
sglang      c54dc4582 + this branch
flashinfer  0.6.15.post1 + flashinfer#4393 @ 090e6466 (the PR was force-pushed on 08-12; this is the rebased equivalent of the 6573c65 the first numbers were taken on)
torch       2.13.0+cu130
sgl-kernel  0.4.6.post1
driver      595.58.03
server      --tp 8 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
            --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.82
            --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64
client      bench_serving random, --random-range-ratio 1.0, --num-prompts 3x bs, OSL 256
```

Mean values. KV pool was 342912 tokens in every arm; `#cached-token` was 0 on
every prefill, so no TTFT is a prefix-cache artifact.

**TTFT (ms)**

| ISL / batch | NCCL | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8k, bs1 | 1909.68 | **1848.65** |
| 8k, bs4 | 6324.39 | **6209.99** |
| 128k, bs1 | **33384.58** | 33410.24 |
| 128k, bs4 | **111272.74** | 111421.98 |

**TPOT (ms)**

| ISL / batch | NCCL | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8k, bs1 | 21.14 | **13.62** (-36%) |
| 8k, bs4 | 30.30 | **25.23** (-17%) |
| 128k, bs1 | 21.51 | **14.11** (-34%) |
| 128k, bs4 | 84.50 | **84.60** |

**Output throughput (tok/s)**

| ISL / batch | NCCL | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8k, bs1 | 35.02 | **48.05** (+37%) |
| 8k, bs4 | 72.82 | **80.93** (+11%) |
| 128k, bs1 | 6.58 | **6.92** (+5%) |
| 128k, bs4 | 7.07 | 7.06 |

TPOT is where these kernels pay: -34% to -36% at bs1, and the ratio does not
depend on context length, since a decode reduction's size is set by the batch.
TTFT and the 128k bs4 cells are level with NCCL by construction -- those
reductions are above the workspace bound and stay on NCCL.

Before any of this was measured, all 56 ordered GPU pairs were verified to carry
data intact. A sister host with the same driver returned zeroed buffers on every
cross-device copy while `nvidia-smi topo -p2p r` reported all-OK; a bandwidth
test does not catch that.

## Known limitations

1. **Requires a recent FlashInfer.** flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4393 merged on 2026-08-20, so `PcieIpcAllReduceWorkspace` is available upstream and its signature is settled. The `ImportError` path degrades to NCCL with a warning, so builds without the module are unaffected.
2. **TP4 coverage arrived mid-review.** Earlier revisions of this description said the
   kernels had no effect at `world_size == 4`: FlashInfer's policy table gated that branch on
   `hidden == 4096` exactly, so GLM's 6144 was rejected on every shape. Upstream has since
   removed that constraint (`remove hidden size constraint` in flashinfer#4393, closing
   [flashinfer#4463](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4463)), and TP4×PP2 now
   works. Measured on the same host, against NCCL:

   | ISL / batch | TPOT | output tok/s |
   |---|---|---|
   | 8k, bs1 | 20.55 → **18.49** (-10%) | 37.19 → **40.28** (+8%) |
   | 8k, bs4 | 31.74 → **30.24** (-5%) | 87.34 → **90.26** (+3%) |
   | 128k, bs1 | 20.80 → **18.79** (-10%) | 11.08 → **11.33** (+2%) |
   | 128k, bs4 | 120.92 → 121.26 | 14.10 → 14.08 |

   The gain is smaller than at 8 ranks (-10% against -36%), which is what the fabric predicts:
   at 4 ranks NCCL has half the peers to reach and a less degraded baseline to beat. Kernel
   numerics at world 4 / hidden 6144: 6 shapes, 0 skipped, 0 mismatches.

3. **Not the best option at every point.** On the same host a bandwidth-optimal FP8-compressing ring beats these kernels on prefill TTFT (1381 ms vs 2239 at 8k bs1) while losing on decode. There is no single best all-reduce on this fabric, which is part of why this is opt-in rather than autodetected.
4. **Single host, single model, bf16 reductions only.** No world-size-2 coverage, no unit test yet.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with `pre-commit run --all-files`
- [x] Accuracy validation (GSM8K vs NCCL)
- [x] Upstream flashinfer#4393 merged (2026-08-20)
- [x] Unit test (`test/registered/unit/distributed/test_pcie_ipc_ar.py`, CPU-only)

title: [Diffusion] Add FLUX.2-klein 4B/9B XPU t2i and ti2i tests
body:
**Title:** `[Diffusion] Add FLUX.2-klein 4B/9B XPU t2i and ti2i tests`

---
## Motivation

FLUX.2-klein has no XPU test coverage. This adds a manual 1-GPU test for
klein-4B and klein-9B on Intel XPU. It covers text-to-image, and
image-to-image against a stored reference, so a quality regression in
either path is caught by hand before release.

## Modifications

Two new files: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_klein.py` and
`test/registered/xpu/conftest.py`. No changes to the shared test harness,
CI workflows, or other test files. The conftest also lets the existing
`test_xpu_flux2_dev.py` and `test_xpu_zimage_turbo.py` run under a plain
`pytest`.

- **t2i** (4B, 9B): one fixed prompt, gated on CLIP score
  (`clip-vit-base-patch32`, threshold 0.25), the same approach as
  `test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`. The threshold was measured on this prompt:
  healthy 4B/9B output scores >= 0.4198, black/white/noise frames
  <= 0.1842. A CLIP model load or scoring failure fails the test rather
  than passing unchecked, as it would under `test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`.
- **ti2i** (4B, 9B): CUDA `flux_2_ti2i`'s edit prompt and input image, at
  1024x1024 with seed 0. The output is compared against a stored reference
  image with the existing `compare_with_gt` (CLIP similarity, SSIM, PSNR,
  mean abs diff), at `flux_2_ti2i`'s H100 thresholds.
  - There is no XPU reference set in `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion`, so
    references are read from `SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR`.
  - A run without a reference fails, and saves its output under
    `$SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ARTIFACT_DIR/missing_consistency_gt/` to be
    inspected and promoted.
- Every output is saved to `$SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ARTIFACT_DIR` before it is
  checked, so a failing image is kept.
- **Config:** bf16 DiT/VAE/text encoder, 4 steps (klein is
  step-distilled), 1024x1024. Residency is pinned per size: 4B uses
  `dit=resident`, and 9B adds `text_encoder=layerwise-offload` so
  1024x1024 warmup fits in 24 GiB.
- **Functional only, no perf validation** (`collect_perf=False`). The
  `flux2_klein_*` case ids added here have no `perf_baselines/xpu_b60.json`
  entry. klein-4B t2i perf on XPU is
  already guarded by the CI case `flux_2_klein_image_t2i`.
- **Registered `nightly=True, disabled=`,** like its `nightly-xpu-1-gpu`
  siblings: the Intel nightly lists it as skipped and never runs it.
- **`conftest.py`** re-exports the diffusion `perf_results` fixture, as
  `test/registered/amd/conftest.py` does (#38686). Without it, a plain
  pytest run of any `DiffusionServerBase` test in `test/registered/xpu/`
  errors with `fixture 'perf_results' not found`.

### How to run

```bash
export SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR=/path/to/klein_references   # ti2i only
export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ARTIFACT_DIR=/path/to/artifacts
python3 -m pytest -v -s \
    test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_klein.py -k image_t2i    # or image_ti2i, or image for all 4
```

To create references: run the ti2i cases once without them, inspect the
images saved under `missing_consistency_gt/`, then copy them into
`$SGLANG_CONSISTENCY_GT_DIR`.

## Accuracy Tests

Run on Intel Arc Pro B60 (24 GiB), torch 2.13.0+xpu, 1 card, on this PR's
commit (`872989c6d0`, upstream base `a749d84303`), with the plain command
from "How to run" (no `-p`):

| case | result | metrics |
|---|---|---|
| `flux2_klein_4b_image_t2i` | pass | CLIP 0.4291 |
| `flux2_klein_9b_image_t2i` | pass | CLIP 0.4198 |
| `flux2_klein_4b_image_ti2i` | pass | clip 1.0000, ssim 0.9999, psnr 62.21, mad 0.019 |
| `flux2_klein_9b_image_ti2i` | pass | clip 1.0000, ssim 0.9999, psnr 62.41, mad 0.020 |

4 passed in 3m 11s. The metrics and t2i images are identical to the earlier
revisions of this PR.

Checks that the gates fail when they should:
- **Every case forced to fail** (t2i CLIP threshold raised to 1.01; ti2i
  input image swapped): 4 failed, and all 4 failing images were still saved
  to `$SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ARTIFACT_DIR`.
- **ti2i, swapped input image:** fails all four metrics (clip <= 0.49,
  ssim <= 0.62, psnr <= 10.6, mad >= 56.5), well outside the thresholds.

On the previous revision, whose test logic for these paths is unchanged:
- **ti2i, different card:** a rerun on a second card gives identical
  metrics, so the reference is not card-specific.
- **t2i, CLIP scorer forced to fail:** both cases fail with the scorer's
  own exception, rather than passing unchecked.
- **t2i, rerun:** produces byte-identical images (also true of this
  commit's run).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests (manual XPU test, registered disabled)
- [x] Provide accuracy results
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed)

title: [qwen 3.8 next] Fuse small CUDA graph input buffer copies
body: ## Motivation CUDA graph replay copies several small input tensors with separate device transfers. Copy eligible tensors in one Triton launch per phase, retaining the existing fallback for unsupported layouts and aliasing. ## Modifications Preserve raw floating-point bits, integer casts, strided MRoPE inputs, and large-buffer DMA copies. This PR is independently based on `main`. QSA KV preparation is tracked separately in #40972. Before, After, ## Accuracy Tests Added focused tests for this change: ```bash python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/test_small_copy.py ``` Independent branch test rerun: **16 passed** on NVIDIA B200. Each PR was tested from its own `main`-based source snapshot. Combined implementation validation with official `sgl-eval` 0.1.0, temperature 1, top-p 1, maximum 131072 tokens, 8 repeats over 30 questions, concurrency 128, thinking enabled, no acceptance simulation: | Mode | Correct / total | Accuracy | Length truncations | Request errors | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Normal decode | 229/240 | 95.42% | 9 | 0 | | NEXTN, 3 steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens | 228/240 | 95.00% | 8 | 0 | Real MTP acceptance length was approximately 2.146, including the bonus token, estimated by weighting the complete rounded log intervals by request count. Audited all 8 prediction files per mode against native metrics, generation settings and token totals. These are integration results with the optimization series enabled, not an isolated accuracy A/B for this PR. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Benchmark scope: the E2E results below were measured with the full optimization series combined. Reproducing that implementation requires all PRs listed below, including this PR. They are not standalone performance results for this PR.** ### Full optimization series used for integration measurements - [#40972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40972): Fuse QSA KV preparation and sparse block expansion - [#41166](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41166): Fuse small CUDA graph input buffer copies **(this PR)** - [#41167](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41167): Reduce repeated overlap batch snapshot work - [#41168](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41168): Skip speculative KV allocation transfers when no pages are needed - [#41169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41169): Fuse simulated speculative acceptance tensor preparation - [#41170](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41170): Fuse speculative relay payload stores and avoid single-request gathers - [#41171](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41171): Fuse hybrid speculative state commits across state pools - [#41172](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41172): Fuse exact greedy chain verification with argmax finalization - [#41173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41173): Fuse QSA graph replay metadata across draft steps - [#41174](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41174): Fuse Mamba tracking index lookup and skip uniform-position transfers - [#41175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41175): Fuse NEXTN verify and draft graph input preparation Each split PR is independently based on `main`; the list above describes the combined benchmark source, not a required merge order. The combined AIME26 results in Accuracy Tests also use this full series (with acceptance simulation disabled). ### Evidence specific to this change An isolated GPU microbenchmark copying ten small buffers decreased from approximately 11.0 to 1.4 microseconds at batch size 1; batch sizes 8, 128, and 512 also improved. This excludes Python dispatch overhead. The isolated host-side dispatch benchmark increased from approximately 7.7 to 57.3 microseconds because of eligibility and alias checks; the GPU savings should not be assumed to improve every model or batch shape. The combined E2E table below must not be used to infer this PR's individual throughput gain. ### Full-series E2E performance (all PRs above combined) Hardware and workload: NVIDIA B200 x4 / TP4, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, 5 requests at concurrency 1, plan stream disabled: | Mode | Median TPOT across 3 runs | Decode throughput derived from TPOT | Median fwd occupancy across 3 runs | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Normal decode | 4.1270 ms | 242.30 token/s | 98.90% | | NEXTN, 3 steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens | 1.6936 ms | 590.44 token/s | 97.79% | Forward occupancy was collected with SGLang's device timer. Per-run values were 98.90%, 98.91%, and 98.89% for normal decode, and 97.75%, 97.79%, and 97.80% for NEXTN. These are full-series integration measurements with plan stream disabled; the NEXTN runs use simulated acceptance length 3.3, as in the performance table. Every run completed 5 requests and generated 5120 output tokens. Decode throughput is 1000 / mean TPOT in milliseconds; the table reports the median of three runs. NEXTN performance uses simulated acceptance length 3.3. These measurements do not establish an isolated main-versus-this-PR speedup. ## Checklist - [x] Pre-commit formatting and checks pass. - [x] Focused regression tests included. - [x] Independent branch test rerun complete. - [x] Current combined accuracy validation complete. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36223681494](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36223681494) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36223681353](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36223681353) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36223681503](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36223681503)

title: [Fix] Align native generate statistics metadata with Python
body:
## Motivation

Rust's native `POST /generate` omits five scheduler statistics returned by Python: `cached_tokens`, `cached_tokens_details`, `reasoning_tokens`, `num_retractions`, and `dp_rank`. It also ignores `require_reasoning=true`, so the scheduler does not enable the requested reasoning accounting.

Return Python-compatible field presence and scheduler values for JSON and cumulative/incremental SSE, including zero counts, null values and nondefault statistics. Forward the reasoning flag into the existing scheduler accounting and grammar path.

## Modifications

- Collect the existing scheduler statistics for both frontends and transmit typed snapshots through the Python/Rust MessagePack header. Preserve old headers and reject incomplete or malformed columns.
- Retain the latest snapshot in the existing accumulator and expose it in both native formatters; do not add already-cumulative counters together.
- Forward the request-wide `require_reasoning` boolean at Python's existing wire position, after a null routing-key placeholder, for single and batch requests.

Weight-version metadata is reviewed separately in [the stacked Draft PR in my fork](https://github.com/lagoon0o0/sglang/pull/1). This PR retains five signed commits, ending at `083742d530`; no weight-version implementation remains in its diff.

## Accuracy Tests

The split restores the exact file tree of `0308e2afb5` (re-signed as `083742d530`). Its only change from the reasoning implementation at `18dbd0545a` (signed `5557244eb9`) is a source comment. No new code was introduced by splitting, and hardware experiments were not rerun for the split.

- **Existing A-only acceptance:** MLX and single-L4 CUDA each exercised 96 reasoning-flag requests / 136 comparisons at `18dbd0545a`, covering omitted/false/true, single/batch, JSON and cumulative/incremental SSE, repeatability, and generated text/token IDs. All focused comparisons passed.
- **CPU coverage retained:** statistics collection and MessagePack validation, legacy/idle/malformed batches, snapshot replacement, both formatter paths, and HTTP-to-wire reasoning-flag propagation. Existing scheduler grammar tests exercise the shared reasoning path.
- **Separate A+B evidence:** the later `ebf182bbd2` run included the now-separated weight-version change. All five statistics matched in 72 MLX result pairs. On CUDA, all five fields were present; forced-retraction counts differed in four paired attempts, with two unstable Rust checks and a JSON/SSE retraction-count mismatch. These are joint-run observations, not a claim of a fresh A-only run or complete parity success.

Pinned models: `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit@73e3e38d981303bc594367cd910ea6eb48349da8` and `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. The A+B parity harness was `ef1b419696`; original reports retain their original source SHAs.

Limits: two-GPU DP and hardware grammar/strict-thinking scenarios remain unverified. Retraction-count stability, response timestamps, weight versions and separate logprob metadata alignment are outside this PR's completion claim. Validation numbers for the combined A+B CPU suite are documented with the weight-version PR, rather than attributed to this narrower tree.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Existing A statistics benchmarks at `466d91e1b3` (re-signed as `54acee1cb6`) measured batch 1/128/4096 bridge encoding at 0.80/8.44/220.08 to 1.59/13.56/352.64 microseconds, five added decode allocations per batch, and `ChunkEvent` growth from 144 to 200 bytes. These are historical microbenchmarks, not model-throughput measurements. The separate weight-version overhead is not included here.

title: [VLM] Introduce FA4 into ViT for SM100/SM103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR is to fill gaps in FA4 path on Blackwell:
1. **The softmax row max ignores an sm_103 instruction.** Blackwell Ultra adds `tcgen05.ld.red`, a TMEM load that also returns a per-thread reduction of the loaded values. We can use it to get each row's max for free while reading S out of TMEM. Currently SGLang FA4 forward does not: on B300 every softmax step still reduces 128 values per row with FMNMX3.
2. **ViT attention on B300 falls back to Triton.** #25570 switched the default multimodal attention backend on SM103 from `fa4` to `triton_attn` because "FA4 is not yet validated on B300". Measured on B300, FA4's kernel is 2–20x faster than the Triton kernel on ViT shapes (head dims 64/72/80/128) and matches it numerically, so B300 ViTs pay a large, avoidable cost.
3. **The ViT CUDA graph runners do not support `fa4`.** `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` only handles `triton_attn` and `fa3`; with `fa4` (already the default on SM100) the server dies at startup with `AssertionError: cu_seqlens must be a torch.Tensor`. Changing the SM103 default without fixing this would break every B300 deployment that turned the ViT graph on. The graph is also what removes FA4's per-call host overhead for small images (see Speed Tests).


## Modifications

- `flash_fwd_sm100.py`: on sm_103, build a second TMEM copy with `tcgen05.LdRed32x32bOp(redOp=MAX)`. In `softmax_step`, tiles that need no masking (`mask_fn is None`) in kernels without `score_mod`/bias load S with it — one `cute.copy_atom_call` per 32-column chunk, each also returning that chunk's max — and pass the reduced max to the softmax. Masked tiles keep the plain load and the software max, because the hardware max is taken over the raw S. On the tiles where it is used the hardware max equals the software reduction exactly, so **outputs are bit-identical** to the current kernel. The first-iteration tile is always masked (`mask_seqlen=True`), so only steady-state tiles change.
- `softmax.py`: `SoftmaxSm100.update_row_max` accepts an optional precomputed `tile_row_max`; everything after the max (fast `exp2`, rescale threshold) is unchanged.
- `interface.py`: `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX` (default `1`; `0` restores the FMNMX reduction). It is part of the compile key, so both variants can coexist in one process. The flag is ignored on non-sm_103 GPUs.
- `vision.py`: the platform default multimodal attention backend is `fa4` for all compute capability 10.x (SM100 and SM103). Explicit `--mm-attention-backend` and per-model overrides (e.g. Kimi-K3-VL's own SM103 heuristic) are unchanged.
- `vision.py` (`VisionFlash4Attention`): accepts the graph runners' `[cu_seqlens, max_seqlen]` list. Unlike the fa3/triton wrappers it keys off the argument type, not the env var, so models without a graph runner keep passing tensors when `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` is set globally.
- `vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `internvl_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`: pass `fa4` the same layout as `fa3`. FA4 JIT-compiles a kernel variant the first time it sees a configuration, which must not happen inside stream capture; for windowed ViTs (Qwen2.5-VL) the generic runner therefore warms up both the windowed and the full-attention layout before capturing (it previously warmed up only block 0's layout). The InternVL runner already warms up every layer eagerly.
- `test_vision_backend_selection.py`: covers the CUDA default per compute capability (9.0→fa3, 10.0→fa4, 10.3→fa4, 12.0→triton_attn) and `VisionFlash4Attention` with list-form and tensor seqlens, with the graph env var on and off.

## Accuracy Tests

All on 8x B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2.

**FA4 kernel, bit-exactness.** 16 configurations run on the unpatched tree and on this branch with the flag on; outputs and LSE are identical in every case (`torch.equal`): causal / non-causal, varlen, chunked prefill (q < k), GQA and `pack_gqa`, head dims 64 / 96 / 128 / (192,128) (incl. the 2-CTA path), sliding window, learnable sink, softcap (reducing load disabled there), split-KV, paged KV (page 128 TMA and page 64 cp.async), and fp8 e4m3 with descales. The compiled PTX (`.target sm_103a`) contains 4 `tcgen05.ld.red` instructions with the flag on and none with it off.

**FA4 unit tests.** `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attention_4.py`: 330 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed.

**ViT attention, FA4 vs Triton.** sglang's own `VisionFlash4Attention` and `VisionTritonAttention` on the same inputs: max abs difference 5e-4 – 1.6e-2 in bf16 across GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes (d=64) and Qwen2.5-VL shapes (d=80, windowed and full attention), consistent with bf16 rounding.

**End to end, MMMU validation (900 questions)** Two servers from the same base commit, one per GPU:

| model (serving config) | ViT | `triton_attn` (current B300 default) | `fa4` (this PR) | same final answer | same-config baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | eager | 51.7% | 51.8% | 871 / 900 (96.8%) | eager vs graph, same backend: 887–891 / 900 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | CUDA graph | 52.0% | 51.6% | 875 / 900 (97.2%) | (same as above) |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4 + EP4, cookbook flags, chat mode; 32-layer d=64 ViT) | eager | 67.8% / 66.9% / 67.2% (3 runs) | 68.0% | 830 / 900 (92.2%) | two identical `triton_attn` servers: 834 / 900 (92.7%) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All on B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs, 1 GPU per measurement unless noted). Kernel numbers are CUDA-graph timed unless marked eager; "eager" includes the Python wrapper, as an un-graphed ViT sees it.

**`tcgen05.ld.red.max` in the FA4 forward, ViT shapes**

Command: `python benchmark/kernels/attention/bench_flash_attention_tmem_red_max.py`. It calls FA4 the way `VisionFlash4Attention` does (varlen, non-causal, no LSE, 16 heads, bf16).

Each of 10 rounds times the flag off and on back to back, alternating which goes first. "off" and "on" are the best round of each. "paired" is the median of the per-round off/on ratios, and "wins" counts the rounds where on was faster. Outputs are bit-identical for every shape.

| input | head dim | off | on | paired speedup | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 80 (Qwen2.5-VL) | 648.8 us | 588.0 us | **1.075x** | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 72 (Qwen3-VL) | 703.9 us | 681.6 us | 1.039x | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 64 (InternViT, GLM / DeepSeek-V4 ViT) | 527.4 us | 518.2 us | 1.023x | 8/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 80 | 438.2 us | 415.7 us | 1.048x | 10/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 64 | 360.5 us | 356.8 us | 1.010x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 80 | 4861.1 us | 4572.3 us | **1.058x** | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 72 | 5217.1 us | 5070.5 us | 1.030x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 64 | 3974.7 us | 3887.8 us | 1.022x | 10/10 |

**ViT attention kernel, `fa4` vs `triton_attn`** (the kernels behind the default switch):

Head-dim sweep, 16 heads, non-causal varlen, speedup of `fa4` over `triton_attn` (FA4 from the base commit, i.e. without item 1; the two wrapper tables below are on this branch):

| layout | d=64 | d=72 | d=80 | d=128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 5.4x | 20.5x | 7.9x | 6.6x |
| 1 image x 16384 tokens | 5.4x | 19.3x | 7.8x | 6.4x |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 4.2x | 16.2x | 6.1x | 5.4x |

GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 ViT shapes (16 heads, d=64), sglang's `VisionFlash4Attention` / `VisionTritonAttention`, per call:

| input | fa4 eager | triton eager | eager ratio | fa4 graph | triton graph | graph ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 image 224² (256 tok) | 62.4 us | 38.4 us | 0.62x | 7.0 us | 14.4 us | 2.05x |
| 1 image 448² (1024 tok) | 61.5 us | 49.3 us | 0.80x | 13.1 us | 44.4 us | 3.38x |
| 4 images 448² | 62.0 us | 98.3 us | 1.59x | 25.5 us | 93.5 us | 3.67x |
| 16 images 448² | 94.2 us | 370.2 us | 3.93x | 90.7 us | 364.8 us | 4.02x |
| 64 images 448² | 361.2 us | 1522.1 us | 4.21x | 357.0 us | 1516.7 us | 4.25x |
| 1 image 896² (4096 tok) | 75.9 us | 357.7 us | 4.71x | 72.5 us | 352.8 us | 4.87x |
| 4 images 896² | 258.4 us | 1351.9 us | 5.23x | 254.6 us | 1347.1 us | 5.29x |
| 1 image 1792² (16384 tok) | 904.4 us | 5200.8 us | 5.75x | 944.3 us | 5187.9 us | 5.49x |
| 8 mixed-size images (11136 tok) | 124.9 us | 610.0 us | 4.88x | 120.6 us | 606.1 us | 5.03x |
| video, 32 frames x 256 tok | 61.2 us | 62.1 us | 1.01x | 28.7 us | 57.8 us | 2.01x |

Qwen2.5-VL-7B ViT (16 heads, d=80; windows of 64 patches, 28 windowed + 4 full-attention blocks), per layer and per image:

| image | windowed layer fa4 / triton (eager) | full layer fa4 / triton (eager) | per image, eager: fa4 / triton | per image, ViT graph: fa4 / triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448x448 (16 windows) | 62.6 / 37.2 us | 61.2 / 42.3 us | 2.00 / 1.21 ms | **0.38 / 0.55 ms** |
| 720p (84 windows) | 62.3 / 64.9 us | 138.5 / 783.8 us | 2.30 / 4.95 ms | 2.11 / 4.81 ms |
| 1080p (180 windows) | 147.5 / 150.6 us | 478.0 / 3725.6 us | 6.04 / 19.12 ms | 5.98 / 18.79 ms |
| 4K (700 windows) | 977.7 / 561.5 us | 7399.8 / 60559.9 us | 57.0 / 258.0 ms | 57.6 / 257.7 ms |

Where `fa4` loses: (a) eager calls on tiny inputs (a single image of ≤1024 tokens), where its ~60 us per-call host overhead exceeds the kernel time; the ViT CUDA graph removes it (448x448: 0.38 ms vs 0.55 ms per image), and SM100 already carries this trade-off with `fa4` as its default. (b) Very many 64-token windows (Qwen2.5-VL at 4K, 700 windows): the windowed layer is 1.7x slower than Triton because FA4's 128-row tiles are half empty; the full-attention layers more than make up for it (4.5x per image). A smaller Q tile for short segments would be a follow-up, not part of this PR.

**End to end, eager ViT** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, 1 GPU per server, c=1, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, fresh images per run):

title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax-H3 packed varlen path for sla_attn backend
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 DiT attention uses a **packed varlen** path (`[text | cond | audio | video]`, `cu_seqlens=[0, used, total]`). The existing `sla_attn` backend only implements dense `forward()`, not `forward_varlen()`, so H3 admission (`validate_server_args` requires `packed_varlen=True`) rejects `sla_attn` today.

The official[ LightX2V Turbo-SLA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo-SLA) stack has two layers that should not be conflated:

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| **SLA LoRA** | Standard QKV/FFN LoRA merged into `W`; drives few-step generation quality |
| **`sla_attn` kernel** | Runtime block-sparse attention acceleration; no sparse weights in the checkpoint |

Goal: let H3 opt into `sla_attn` for DiT acceleration **without breaking existing `sla_attn` users such as TurboWan**, and correctly handle the fact that text/cond/audio prefixes in the packed sequence must not be dropped by top-k sparsification.

---

## Changes

**1. Backend — `sparse_linear_attn.py`**

- `forward_varlen()` + `_packed_sla_forward()` for H3 `[T,H,D]` packed layout
- `protect_upto` pins prefix K blocks; `_localize_protect_upto` maps global bounds per segment
- `_resolve_sla_impl_config()`: config overrides only unset/default ctor fields
- `linear_mix=false` skips `proj_l` (H3 path); shared defaults stay 128×64, `topk=0.1`

 H3 config: `topk_ratio=0.15,blkq=64,blkk=64,linear_mix=false`

**2. Kernel — `sparse_linear_attn_triton.py`**

- `get_block_map(..., protect_upto=0)` pins prefix blocks
- `topk = max(1, ...)`; GQA `repeat_interleave` fix

**3.H3 wiring — `minimax_h3.py`**

- `protect_upto` from `audio_pos.max()+1`, passed only for `SLA_ATTN`
- Ulysses keeps global token coordinates (A2A before attention)

---

## Impact on other models

- **Default `sla_attn` (e.g. TurboWan):** unchanged — same 128×64, `topk=0.1`, `proj_l`
- **Other backends (FA / Sage / SDPA):** no change
- **H3:** enabled via `forward_varlen` + admission probe; no pipeline whitelist

---

## Testing

End-to-end — FL2VA + Turbo-SLA LoRA (768p / 5s / 6 steps / merge, official HF DiT)

- Model & FL2VA keyframes: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) (`assets/fl2va.mp4` first/last frames)
- Turbo-SLA LoRA: [lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo-SLA](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo-SLA)


| Case | Task | Backend | Steps | LoRA | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base sanity | FL2VA | FA | **20** | none | Official HF DiT only (`--dit none`); confirms base packed-varlen path |
| Turbo few-step | FL2VA | FA or `sla_attn` | **6** | Turbo-SLA merge | Same recipe; swap `--attn` only for SLA check (`topk_ratio=0.15`) |

Both at 768p / 5s, DiT resident (`--no-layerwise`).


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cdfca62-9b0d-48c1-9d6e-6f071ec33fd9


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e1894d7-f4ff-4357-80ed-869df6f40f23


---

## Test plan (CI / reviewer)

- [x] `test_minimax_h3_admission::test_validate_server_args_accepts_sla_attn` passes
- [ ] `test_sla_varlen` (follow-up PR or same PR if added later)
- [ ] Default `SparseLinearAttentionImpl()` still has `proj_l`, `128×64`, `topk=0.1`
- [ ] H3 can generate with `attention_backend=sla_attn` + `attention_backend_config=topk_ratio=0.15,blkq=64,blkk=64,linear_mix=false`
- [ ] Wan regression: default-config SLA behavior unchanged (if a Wan CI case exists)
- [ ] Ulysses + SLA integration (not covered by unit tests yet; global `protect_upto` contract is documented)

**Lint (changed files):** `pre-commit` hooks pass (`ruff` F401/F821/UP037, `isort`, `black`, codespell, multimodal_gen Chinese-char check).

---

## Notes

- **Few-step quality comes from LoRA merge, not the SLA kernel**; the SLA kernel is mainly an attention speedup (and may be slower on very short schedules)
- H3 must use the **official HF 13-shard DiT**; a Comfy single-file overlay on this CLI path produces gray mud (unrelated to SLA)
- `--steps 6` means 5 denoise updates (sigmas include endpoint 0)
- Plain top-k without `protect_upto` drops most of the audio prefix blocks; always enable prefix pinning for H3 packed layout

title: [Unified Cache] Support out-of-tree external linkers
body:
## Motivation

Selecting a unified cache external linker currently requires adding a backend branch to SGLang. Allow a separately installed package to supply a `UnifiedCacheLinker`, selected explicitly by class name and Python module path, following the configuration pattern used by vLLM KV connectors.

## Ownership and connections

![Ownership and connections: SGLang owns scheduling, the radix tree, and GPU KV allocation; the external linker runs inside the worker and transfers KV to and from external storage.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/a0ce57537025948483301ee5c900e134da802dec/docs/images/linker-ownership.png)

SGLang retains prefix matching, request admission, GPU slot allocation, and tree locks. The separately installed linker runs inside the same worker and implements external storage access, KV transfers, and completion reporting. The filesystem example uses CPU staging internally. This PR changes how the linker is selected and constructed; the existing runtime ownership boundary is preserved.

## Modifications

- Add `--unified-cache-external-linker-config` with `linker`, `linker_module_path`, and optional `linker_extra_config`. Validate JSON in the frontend and import the explicitly selected module only in the cache-owning worker.
- Require a concrete `UnifiedCacheLinker` subclass and construct it as `Linker(server_args, params, components=..., extra_config=...)`, with a private copy of its extra options.
- Keep the built-in Mooncake/MORI paths unchanged when the JSON config is absent. Explicit plugin config takes precedence over the backend selector and rejects Mooncake-specific MLA deduplication.
- Document the constructor and completion contract and add generic config/factory tests with CPU CI registration.

This PR contains only the SGLang extension mechanism and its tests. The filesystem implementation, packaging, verifier, and plugin-specific tests are maintained separately in [maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker); no example package is included in this PR.

The independent plugin is published on [PyPI as `sglang-fs-linker==0.1.0`](https://pypi.org/project/sglang-fs-linker/0.1.0/) ([successful release workflow](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/actions/runs/35627801114)). Install it into a SGLang runtime containing this PR with `python -m pip install sglang-fs-linker==0.1.0`.

Example after installing that independent plugin:

```bash
--enable-unified-cache-external-linker \
--unified-cache-external-linker-config '{
  "linker": "FileSystemLinker",
  "linker_module_path": "sglang_fs_linker.linker",
  "linker_extra_config": {
    "directory": "/tmp/sglang-fs-kv",
    "namespace": "qwen3-0.6b-example-v1"
  }
}'
```

There is no `kv_role`: the linker contract includes both load and offload. This adds an extension mechanism without expanding the tree wrapper's model support.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated SGLang revision: `9f417bd5054f3ed2db54eeb07c741df6ff7c255c`, based on upstream `14e9c40a72aa247ceb07b93b32b1fe353317bcf2`.

### SGLang regressions

- Config/factory, registry, and server-argument suites: **311 passed, 108 subtests passed**.
- Existing unified linker and pool-assembler regressions on CUDA, including Python/Rust tree fixtures: **56 passed, 10 subtests passed**.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed for all changed SGLang files.

### Published PyPI package validation

The independent [sglang-fs-linker 0.1.0 package](https://pypi.org/project/sglang-fs-linker/0.1.0/) was [successfully published](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/actions/runs/35627801114) from [plugin revision 0f4a1b1](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/tree/0f4a1b1bb36c088ddf72fcd47aa86120292c9aa4). The following checks used the released wheel downloaded from the public PyPI index:

- **Clean Python 3.12 environment:** installation succeeded, installed metadata reported `0.1.0`, and `sglang-fs-linker-verify --help` succeeded.
- **CUDA runtime:** forced a fresh PyPI download and reinstallation; **4 filesystem tests passed**. These tests cover exact KV restoration into different slots, persistence across reset/close, missing prefixes, cancellation, failed writes, and corrupt pages.
- **H200 inference:** ran the installed verifier outside the plugin source checkout. A fresh cache salt forces a cold request; the verifier flushes the GPU radix cache while preserving disk files, then repeats the request.

The inference run used Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B at revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, TP=1, page size 16, BF16 KV, Triton attention, and CUDA graphs disabled:

```json
{
  "cold_cached_tokens": 0,
  "warm_cached_tokens": 640,
  "warm_cached_tokens_details": {
    "device": 0,
    "host": 640
  },
  "matching_output_tokens": 16,
  "max_output_logprob_difference": 0.0460372269153595
}
```

The server also logged `FileSystemLinker loaded 40 pages from disk`. In the existing linker path, the `host` field reports direct external loads: **640 externally restored tokens and zero device-cache hits** after the flush. The verifier checks identical generated text and output token IDs, and requires the maximum output logprob difference to be below 0.05.

For complete prerequisites, exact repository revisions, the pinned CUDA image, and the server launch command, follow the [reproduction guide](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/blob/0f4a1b1bb36c088ddf72fcd47aa86120292c9aa4/README.md#development-and-verification). Inside that prepared container, replace the plugin's source-install step with:

```bash
python -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps --no-cache-dir \
  --index-url https://pypi.org/simple sglang-fs-linker==0.1.0
python -m pytest -q /work/sglang-fs-linker/tests
```

After starting the documented server, run this in a second shell in the same container:

```bash
sglang-fs-linker-verify --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000
```

The `/work` paths above are the repository mounts established by the reproduction guide. The [verifier source](https://github.com/maobaolong/sglang-fs-linker/blob/0f4a1b1bb36c088ddf72fcd47aa86120292c9aa4/src/sglang_fs_linker/verify.py) is public. Published wheel SHA-256: `4c075946c8bb719f33473d30300bfb2a71ec9e8b432c1ae72e114c83f072b324`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance benchmark or speedup claim. The independent FS reference implementation supports a single worker with plain NHD MHA/GQA and floating-point KV. It synchronizes device transfers and blocks on disk I/O, with no eviction/capacity policy. Existing built-in linker transfer implementations are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add generic unit tests with CPU CI registration.
- [x] Document the plugin contract and link the independently maintained reference implementation.
- [x] Provide accuracy evidence; performance scope is stated above.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

title: [AMD][gfx1250] Retune sparse paged-prefill launch config for DSV4-Flash
body:
## Motivation

The Triton path in `_sparse_attn_v4_paged_prefill_triton` currently launches with a conservative configuration: `block_h = 16`, the AMD MFMA minimum tile, and no `num_stages` argument. These are safe defaults that work across architectures, and the file has no `@triton.autotune`, so they apply uniformly wherever the Triton kernel is selected.

On gfx1250 there is meaningful headroom in that choice. The kernel spends most of its time on scattered `tl.load` gathers through `kv_indices`, which benefits from software pipelining, and with `index_n_heads = 64` a larger head tile lets a single CTA cover all heads of a token. Profiling DeepSeek-V4-Flash at ISL 8192 puts this kernel at 9.9% of prefill GPU time and the highest per-call cost in the trace (473 us), so it is worth tuning for this architecture.

This PR selects a gfx1250-specific launch configuration and leaves every other target unchanged.

## Modifications

Select `BLOCK_H=64, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=4, num_stages=2` on gfx1250. `BLOCK_H=64` equals `index_n_heads`, so one CTA covers every head of a token and the grid stops splitting on the head dimension.

Gated: gfx950 takes the OPUS kernel, but gfx1250 and NVIDIA both fall through to this Triton path, and these constants were only measured on gfx1250. Every other target keeps the previous behaviour exactly.

Microbenchmark vs the shipped config (H=64, D=512, topk=512), two independent sweeps:

| T | shipped | tuned | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 279 us | 98 us | 2.84x |
| 512 | 919 us | 440 us | 2.09x |
| 2048 | 3856 us | 1709 us | 2.26x |

The optimum moves with token count — T <= 256 prefers `(32,32,8,2)`, T >= 512 prefers `(64,16,4,2)`. Measured from the scheduler log, 90.1% of prefill tokens arrive in batches with T >= 384 (358 batches at the chunked-prefill cap plus a tail of small remainders), so the config targets large T.

Hardcoded rather than `@triton.autotune`: an autotune `key=` would need a token-count bucket, since T changes on nearly every chunked prefill. Reasonable as a follow-up — several attention kernels here already use a `_BUCKET` key — but a larger change than this fix warrants.

Adds `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_paged_prefill_launch_config.py`, the first test for this kernel: each launch config against a dense torch reference; all configs against each other on identical inputs, with T in {1,5,64,512} and H in {64,48} so `BLOCK_H=64` exercises the head-mask tail; a token whose index lists are entirely `-1`; and that the wrapper dispatches the constants its arch branch claims, checked for both branches so non-gfx1250 CI validates the gate rather than skipping it. 13 tests, all passing on gfx1250.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0:

| | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.929 | 0.000 |
| this PR | **0.932** | **0.000** |

Unchanged, as expected by construction: the online softmax accumulation is tile-size invariant, so block sizes change scheduling and not numerics.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI455X (gfx1250), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=1 + EAGLE(2/1/3), ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, random sequences. Median of runs 2-5 with the warmup run dropped.

### Throughput, +5.38% geomean

| conc | baseline | tuned | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 410.9 | 433.8 | **+5.6%** |
| 16 | 658.2 | 696.5 | **+5.8%** |

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

title: [XPU][Diffusion] Use the AOT SYCL fused residual-norm-scale-shift kernel
body:
sgl-kernel-xpu's AOT SYCL kernel is about 2x cheaper per denoise step than the hand-written triton one forward_xpu used (0.137 s vs 0.275 s on Wan2.2-I2V-A14B 832x480/40f, TP=4, Arc Pro B60) and more accurate: the residual output is bit-identical to triton, the normalized output agrees to under one bf16 ULP, and it is closer to an fp32 reference (rms err 0.001660 vs 0.002153).

Add it as another backend under kernels/ops/diffusion/norm/ and prefer it in forward_xpu, keeping triton as the fallback. The facade lookup is resolved in the existing _is_xpu import block, so the sgl_kernel import stays off other platforms and an sgl-kernel-xpu without the op leaves _has_sycl_fused_norm False and keeps the triton path.

It also unblocks regional torch.compile of a Wan2.2 DiT block: inductor keeps a registered custom op opaque, while it re-lowers the triton kernel and Intel triton then fails to compile the result. The register_fake companion is what lets Dynamo trace the op, since sgl-kernel-xpu registers only the XPU implementation.

title: [GLM-5.3] Capture the KDA extend in breakable prefill CUDA graphs
body: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) interleaves 34 KDA linear-attention layers with 11 DSA layers. Prefill CUDA graphs are auto-disabled for KDA models, and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` (BCG) opts back in, but BCG breaks the graph at every linear-attention layer: the whole KDA extend runs eagerly on each replay, about sixteen Triton launches per layer plus their Python and the host syncs in `prepare_chunk_indices`. From profiling the eager prefill is CPU launch-bound, not GPU-bound. A prefill step issues about 2300 kernel launches, and with the profiler on it costs about 300 ms of CPU whether it carries 1K or 16K tokens; without the profiler a single 1K-token prompt still waits 152 ms for its first token. BCG halves the launches to 1182 per step, yet a 4K-token step still spends 116 ms on the CPU (with the profiler on), and the KDA chain with its glue is more than 60% of what is left. The KDA extend cannot simply be recorded: its launch grids and index tables come from host-side lengths that change on every replay of a bucket. - `prepare_chunk_indices` builds the (sequence, chunk) table with `.tolist()`; it and `prepare_chunk_offsets` are `tensor_cache`d on the tensor object, so inside a capture they would hand back capture-time tables without recording anything. - `causal_conv1d_fn` sizes its grid from `seq_lens_cpu`, and the delta-rule state kernel launches one program per sequence. - The prefix-cache track path selects rows with host lists or `nonzero` and scatters with data-dependent shapes. ## Design The KDA extend now runs inside the graph on static tables, and BCG breaks only at the DSA layers. - For each token bucket `T`, capture allocates tables at the bucket's bounds: `max_seqs = min(T, SGLANG_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_MAX_SEQS)` (128), `max_chunks = cdiv(T, 64) + max_seqs` and `max_conv_blocks = cdiv(T, 8) + max_seqs`. The captured kernels launch fixed grids over these bounds. - Before each replay, `KDAPrefillGraphMetadata.fill` rebuilds the tables from the batch's CPU lengths in numpy and ships them in one pinned asynchronous host-to-device copy; slots and prefix flags come from device gathers. Nothing synchronizes. - Padded rows cost nothing. Padded sequences are empty in `cu_seqlens`, padded chunk rows point past their sequence and return on an `i_t * BT >= T` guard, padded conv blocks and state slots carry `PAD_SLOT_ID`, and rows past the batch's tokens are zeroed so the MoE and the collectives see finite values. - Prefix-cache snapshots become a per-row table (none, final state, chunk-boundary state, conv window start, destination slot) read by two small Triton kernels, instead of host-selected scatters. - The hybrid backend follows the runner's existing captured-metadata contract for BCG (`init_forward_metadata_for_breakable_cuda_graph_capture` / `prepare_forward_metadata_for_breakable_cuda_graph_replay`, as DeepSeek-V4 already does). DSA keeps its eager metadata init. `RadixLinearAttention` skips the eager break when the backend runs the extend in the graph. - The path is active only under a breakable prefill backend, with the Triton KDA extend kernel and without fused-accept verify staging. A batch with more sequences than the cap runs eagerly through `can_run_prefill_cuda_graph`. `SGLANG_DISABLE_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND=1` restores the per-layer break. ## Modifications - `layers/attention/linear/kda_prefill_graph.py` (new): per-bucket tables, their refresh, the track plan, and `kda_extend_in_graph`, the forward extend on those tables. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda_prefill_graph_track.py` (new): the conv-window and SSM-state snapshot kernels over per-row modes. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda.py`: out-of-range early return in the gate cumsum, `recompute_w_u` and chunk output kernels; `chunk_kda` accepts precomputed `chunk_indices` / `chunk_offsets`. - `kernels/ops/attention/fla/chunk_delta_h.py`: accepts `chunk_offsets` instead of deriving it through `tensor_cache`. - `kernels/ops/mamba/causal_conv1d_triton.py`: optional (sequence, block) table that sets the grid instead of `seq_lens_cpu`. - `layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py`: capability checks, table capture and refresh, and the dispatch to the graph path. - `layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`, `base_attn_backend.py`, `layers/radix_linear_attention.py`: the captured-metadata contract, the replay gate and the break decision. - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_DISABLE_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`, `SGLANG_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_MAX_SEQS`. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py` (new). ## Accuracy `test_kda_prefill_graph.py` captures one bucket and replays it for five batches of different shapes, against the production eager `forward_extend` on cloned pools. The batches cover several sequences, cached prefixes, padding, chunk-aligned and unaligned prefix-cache snapshots, and no tracking. Every replay matches bit for bit on the output, the conv and SSM pools and the track slots, and no other pool slot changes. The existing KDA, GDN, `causal_conv1d`, mamba2, radix linear attention and hybrid backend tests pass on B300 (13 files). End to end, the natural-language greedy probes produce exactly the text of main's BCG, and GSM8K (200 questions, greedy) scores within one question of eager prefill: | Config | GSM8K | |---|---| | eager prefill (cookbook default) | 98.5% | | main, BCG | 98.5% | | this PR, BCG | 98.5% | | this PR, BCG, 16K chunks | 98.5% | ## Performance 8x B300, GLM-5.3-Flash, cookbook B300 FP8 recipe (TP8, TRT-LLM DSA, FP8 KV, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), random-ids, all servers on one box and one tree, no profiler: | Metric | eager (default) | main, BCG | this PR, BCG | this PR, BCG, 16K chunks | |---|---|---|---|---| | TTFT, 1 x 1K tokens | 152 ms | 47 ms | 37 ms | 39 ms | | TTFT, 1 x 4K tokens | 177 ms | 152 ms | 113 ms | 95 ms | | TTFT, 1 x 16K tokens | 495 ms | 419 ms | 384 ms | 333 ms | | c64 1024/256 median TTFT | 968 ms | 767 ms | 696 ms | 708 ms | | c64 1024/256 output tok/s | 4291 | 4167 | 4268 | 4477 | | bs64 decode median ITL | 9.69 ms | 9.63 ms | 9.62 ms | 9.70 ms | With the profiler on, a 4093-token prefill step goes from 1182 eager launches and 116 ms of CPU under main's BCG to 439 launches and 42 ms, and the GPU now finishes 33-35 ms after the last launch: the step is GPU-bound. Prefill graph capture takes 85 s instead of 165 s. "16K chunks" adds `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.78`. GLM-5 defaults BCG prefill to 4096-token chunks, so 16K buckets alone never replay; the 16K buckets cost about 22 GB more graph memory per GPU. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36285996686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36285996686) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #36285996696](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36285996696) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36285996681](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36285996681)

title: [AMD] Retry Mooncake etcd Go module fetch in rocm.Dockerfile
body:
Mooncake's etcd wrapper build rule runs `go mod tidy` inside `make -j`. That fetches the go1.25.10 toolchain named in its go.mod plus about 38 modules from proxy.golang.org, with no retry. One transient HTTP/2 stream reset on a module zip fails the whole `--no-cache` image build, as in the nightly ROCm 10 publish-gfx1250 job
(actions/runs/36257652494).

Run the same `go mod tidy` in mooncake-common/etcd before cmake, retried up to 5 times. The in-make rule then finds everything in the module cache. `go mod download` is not enough: the untidy go.mod needs x/sys/x/text bumps plus test-only imports that only tidy resolves.

title: [Bug] Reject dynamic LoRA updates when tokenizer-worker-num > 1
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #31084.

With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, each tokenizer worker process owns its own `LoRARegistry` / `lora_ref_cache`. Dynamic `/load_lora_adapter`, `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors`, and `/unload_lora_adapter` only update the worker that handled the HTTP request. Requests routed to other workers then fail with `"Got LoRA adapter that has never been loaded"`, and a retry on another worker can mint a new id and hit `"already loaded"` on the backend.

Adapters seeded at startup via `--lora-paths` are unaffected (every worker loads them at init).

Related earlier attempts: #31724, #36487 (same fail-fast direction; this PR targets current `get_serving()` / runtime-context APIs).

## Modifications

- Add `_validate_dynamic_lora_supported()` in `tokenizer_control_mixin.py` and call it from the three dynamic LoRA handlers before any backend / registry mutation.
- Document the `--tokenizer-worker-num 1` requirement under Dynamic LoRA loading in `docs/docs/advanced_features/lora.mdx`.
- Add CPU unit coverage in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dynamic_lora_multi_tokenizer_guard.py`:
  - all three endpoints reject with `tokenizer_worker_num > 1` (no communicator call, no registry mutation)
  - guard still fires when dp-attention allows `dp_size > 1`
  - single-worker load path still succeeds

title: [Bug] Accept pp_proxy_tensors in frozen-KV MTP and UNO spec-v2 workers
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40155.

The scheduler non-overlap speculative path always calls:

```python
self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(batch, pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors)
```

`FrozenKVMTPWorkerV2` and `UnoWorkerV2` did not accept `pp_proxy_tensors`, so the first step on those workers raised:

```text
TypeError: ...forward_batch_generation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'
```

`DSparkWorkerV2` / `MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2` already had the parameter; these two were the remaining gaps.

## Modifications

- Add `pp_proxy_tensors=None` to `FrozenKVMTPWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation` and pass it through to the target prefill and `verify` paths.
- Add the same parameter to `UnoWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation` / `_forward_prefill` and forward it to the target worker.
- Declare abstract `forward_batch_generation(..., pp_proxy_tensors=None)` on `BaseSpecWorker` so future workers cannot silently omit it.
- Add `test/registered/unit/spec/test_spec_worker_pp_proxy_signature.py` (AST bookkeeping) so every concrete override under `speculative/` must accept the keyword.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] Reject dynamic LoRA updates with tokenizer-worker-num > 1
body:
## What this fixes

1. With `--tokenizer-worker-num` greater than 1, each tokenizer worker process keeps its own LoRA adapter registry.
2. The dynamic endpoints `/load_lora_adapter`, `/unload_lora_adapter` and the from tensors variant only update the registry of whichever worker served the HTTP request.
3. So an adapter loaded at run time works only for requests that happen to route back to that worker, and retrying the load on another worker mints a new id and then trips the duplicate name check in the backend LoRA manager (`python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py`). The adapter appears to both not exist and already exist depending on routing.

Mitigates #31084.

## The fix

1. The three dynamic LoRA handlers in `tokenizer_control_mixin.py` now fail fast with a clear error when more than one tokenizer worker is running, before any state is changed.
2. Adapters preloaded at startup with `--lora-paths` are unaffected, because every worker seeds those at init.
3. The single worker path is unchanged.

I considered replicating the registry updates across workers over the existing pause and continue broadcast path in `multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`, but that path only confirms that the originating worker applied the change. It does not wait for the other workers, which is what LoRA state needs:

## Note on the recent dp attention change

Upstream #32708 now allows dynamic LoRA with dp attention, which relaxed the neighbouring check in these same handlers from `dp_size == 1` to `dp_size == 1 or enable_dp_attention`. That is a different axis to this change. Each tokenizer worker still keeps its own LoRA registry with no synchronization between them, so this guard is still needed, and it now also covers the dp attention setup that #32708 enabled. The new test `test_rejected_even_when_dp_attention_allows_dp_size_above_one` pins that interaction.

## Limitations

1. This makes the failure explicit. It does not add multi worker dynamic LoRA support.
2. The preload suggestion in the error message only helps adapters stored on disk. There is no startup path for adapters supplied as tensors in memory, so those callers must run with one tokenizer worker.
3. Anyone running more than one tokenizer worker today whose routing happens to pin them to a single worker will now get an explicit error where the call previously appeared to work. That is the intent, but it is a behavior change worth calling out.
4. Verified with CPU only unit tests against a mocked tokenizer manager. No multi worker server was launched end to end.
5. Unrelated to this fix, and not changed here: the `/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` route in `http_server.py` has no `auth_level` decorator, while `/load_lora_adapter` and `/unload_lora_adapter` both require the admin token. On a server launched with only an admin API key that endpoint can be called with no credentials. This already exists on main and should be handled separately.

## Testing

1. New tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, registered for CPU CI: all three dynamic operations are rejected with more than one worker, the backend is never contacted, the registry is untouched, and the single worker path still loads, loads from tensors, and unloads exactly as before.
2. Fail then pass: with the handler restored to main, the guard tests fail and the single worker tests pass. With the fix, all 8 pass.
3. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files is clean.
4. AI assistance was used for this change.

> Note: CI requires a maintainer to add the `run-ci` label.

title: [AMD] Run Quark MXFP4 MoE as W4A16 via triton_kernels on RDNA (gfx1151)
body:
## Motivation

Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints (e.g. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`) cannot run correctly on RDNA GPUs such as gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo), which have neither FP4 hardware nor an AITER FP4 MoE kernel:

- Without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the server crashes after weight loading with `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined`, because `process_weights_after_loading` calls `e8m0_shuffle` on every non-gfx1250 GPU while the import is gated on `_use_aiter`.
- With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the server starts, but the output is garbage (GSM8K 8%, chat echoes the question). The scales are preshuffled into the gfx950 `e8m0_shuffle` layout while the weights are not shuffled (`_is_shuffle_moe_mxfp4` is gfx95-only), and aiter's `fused_moe` falls back to its "2stage default" kernel on gfx1151.

`triton_kernels`' `matmul` can already upcast MXFP4 weights inside the kernel with bf16 activations, and it computes correctly on gfx1151, so this PR uses it as a W4A16 path for these GPUs.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`:

- Add `_use_triton_w4a16`, enabled on HIP when the GPU is neither gfx95x nor gfx1250 (opt out with `SGLANG_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16=0`). gfx950 and gfx1250 keep their existing AITER paths unchanged.
- `create_weights`: don't apply AITER MoE padding when the W4A16 path is active.
- `create_moe_runner`: skip the AITER runner requirement on the W4A16 path.
- `process_weights_after_loading`: on the W4A16 path, swizzle the packed MXFP4 weights and e8m0 scales with the existing `_swizzle_mxfp4` helper, build `PrecisionConfig`s (`b_microblock_size=32`, fp32 output for w2), and drop the original loaded tensors. The AITER preshuffle (and the `e8m0_shuffle` call) is no longer reached on these GPUs.
- `apply_weights`: on the W4A16 path, build expert-major ragged routing from the standard `topk_ids` / `topk_weights` entirely on device (`argsort` + `scatter_add_`, no `bincount`, so it's CUDA-graph capturable). Then run gate_up `matmul` (gather) → `silu_and_mul` → down `matmul` (scatter + router weights), and reduce the scattered `num_tokens * top_k` rows over `top_k`.
- The path asserts a serialized MXFP4 checkpoint and `silu` activation, so unsupported configurations fail loudly instead of computing wrong results.

Activations stay in bf16 (W4A16) rather than being quantized to MXFP4 as on gfx950, so accuracy is at least as good as the W4A4 path.

## Accuracy Tests

Model `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4` on 1x gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, 96 GB VRAM carve-out), `--attention-backend triton --context-length 8192`, sglang at `172b1b4825` in the `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-gfx1151-20260923` image (ROCm 7.2.4, torch 2.9.1, triton 3.7.0). The file touched here is unchanged between that commit and current `main`. Reference: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` (BF16) on the same machine and flags.

| Model | Path | MGSM-en (100, chat, thinking off) | GSM8K 5-shot (200) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16 | unquantized | 0.98 | 0.945 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | before, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` | — | 0.080 (50 q) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | before, default | crash (`NameError: e8m0_shuffle`) | — |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | **this PR** | **0.97** | **0.970** |

Kernel-level check on real layer-3 weights: the W4A16 MoE output vs. an fp32 reference built from the dequantized MXFP4 weights (`_dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16`) gives a relative error of 0.41–0.43% for m = 1 … 256 tokens.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Same setup as above.

| Model | Path | Decode bs=1 (in 512 / out 256) | Median TPOT | Throughput, 16 concurrent (MGSM) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16 | unquantized | 9.38 tok/s | 103.5 ms | 46.8 tok/s |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | **this PR** | 8.37 tok/s | 118.2 ms | 79.7 tok/s |

The W4A16 path uses the default `triton_kernels` opt flags (`num_warps=8`) with no gfx1151 tuning yet. Single-request decode is slightly slower than BF16, while batched throughput is 1.7x BF16. Weight loading takes 15.6 s (vs. 63.5 s for BF16), and CUDA graph capture works.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.
