title: [AMD] Small-M W8A8 FP8 projection GEMM for Qwen3.5 AttnFP8 on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` keeps the attention and GDN projections in FP8: per-channel weights with dynamic per-token activations. At decode sizes on MI355X TP4, each layer runs two quant + GEMM pairs through `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`. In each pair, the GEMM reads its weights far below the bandwidth a plain streaming read reaches: 21 MB for the packed GDN `in_proj`, 19 MB for `qkv_proj`, 8 MB for `out_proj` / `o_proj`. At 4 tokens the old GEMMs take 10.0 / 9.7 / 5.4 us for these, versus 4.8 / 4.5 / 2.8 us for a streaming-read kernel of the same size. The output-side activation quant, after the GDN gated norm and the attention gate multiply, also runs as its own launch. This PR adds a small-M GEMM for these shapes and folds the output-side quant into the kernel that produces the activation.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/smallm_fp8_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_fp8_gemm.hip`). It is built with `hipcc` on first use and launched through ctypes, reusing #40204's helpers. `_Kernel.launch` gains `block` / `shared` arguments whose defaults keep the MoE kernel unchanged.
- The GEMM reads the weight exactly as loaded: aiter's (16, 16)-preshuffled `[N, K]`, including #39902's packed QKVZ+BA buffer. There is no loader change and no extra weight copy.
  - Each wave issues all its 16 B non-temporal weight loads up front.
  - It uses `v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4` with fp32 accumulation.
  - For small M on K = 4096, activations are staged once in LDS.
  - `x_scale * w_scale` is applied once per output, with a bf16 store.
- `apply_fp8_linear`: one guarded swap for `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` on the aiter per-token path. It accepts an already-quantized `(fp8, x_scale [M, 1])` tuple through the existing pre-quantized branch, so it composes with #34502's input-side fusion. The input-side quant itself is unchanged here.
- Output-side quant fusion: `_layer_norm_fwd_1pass_kernel` (GDN `RMSNormGated`) and `_fused_sigmoid_mul_kernel` (attention gate) gain a `QUANT` constexpr that writes per-token FP8 plus scale, bit-identical to `_per_token_group_quant_8bit` on the unfused output. `qwen3_5.py` uses it for `out_proj` / `o_proj` when the consumer is a Quark W8A8 per-token linear and 1 <= M <= 40. The BF16 MTP layer is untouched.
- Guard: gfx950, ROCm >= 7.2, fp8 e4m3fn, bf16 output, and exact shapes with an M window per shape where the new GEMM is at least as fast as the old one:
  - packed `in_proj` (5184, 4096) and `qkv_proj` (4608, 4096): M <= 28;
  - `out_proj` / `o_proj` (4096, 2048): M <= 36.

  Everything else takes today's path.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ=0` turns both parts off. A build or load failure disables it for the process.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_fp8_proj_gfx950.py`:
  - the GEMM against `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` for the three TP4 shapes at M in {1, 4, 16, 24, 29, 36, 41}, with dispatch inside the guard and fallback outside;
  - tuple input == bf16 input;
  - the off switch;
  - the producer guard;
  - bit-exactness of the fused quant for both producers;
  - graph replay == eager.

  It passes on `v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`, together with the existing `test_qwen35_gdn_packed_fp8_in_proj.py` and `test_smallm_moe_gfx950.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

The math stays W8A8. Against `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` on the real shapes, outputs are bit-identical in 20 of 21 (shape, M) cases, and the rest differ by at most 1 bf16 ulp. The fused quant is bit-identical.

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (revision e17e5f0), MI355X TP4, InferenceX recipe (FP8 KV cache, EAGLE MTP
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real draft), lm-eval `local-chat-completions` with chat template, 5-shot GSM8K (InferenceX
task), thinking disabled, 16384-token output budget, temperature 0. At most 7 running requests (GPQA at 5 and GSM8K at 2 on the same server), so verify batches (<= 28 tokens) are inside the GEMM's range.

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |
| This PR | 97.65% (1288/1319) | 97.65% (1288/1319) |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, repeat 8, simple-evals grader), same servers, thinking on, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 20, 32768-token output budget:

| Configuration | Score |
|---|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 0.871 (1380/1584) |
| This PR | 0.869 (1376/1584) |
| Reference (Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card) | 0.884 |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X, TP4 / EP1, InferenceX MI355X agentic recipe for this model (image
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80`, EAGLE MTP
3 / 1 / 4, simulated acceptance length 3.39, BF16 MTP layer as in the recipe), baseline = main `1417345f5f` (includes
#39901, #39902 and #40204), this PR = the same commit + this PR. Full 3600 s aiperf AgentX trace replay on the same four
GPUs, one configuration at a time, nothing else on the node.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 2.60 | 2.44 | −6.2% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 3.04 | 2.88 | −5.3% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 3.14 | 2.96 | −5.7% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 372 / 795 | 383 / 782 | +3.0% / −1.6% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 657 | 686 | +4.4% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 384.0 / 328.4 | 409.5 / 347.8 | +6.6% / +5.9% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 238.3 / 137.6 | 248.5 / 137.9 | +4.3% / +0.2% |

Concurrency 8, average of two full runs per configuration (the second pass in reverse order). Verify batches are
4 x running requests, up to 32 tokens: `out_proj` / `o_proj` and the fused quant stay in range at every batch,
`in_proj` / `qkv_proj` fall back above 28 tokens:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 3.40 | 3.18 | −6.5% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 4.18 | 4.05 | −3.0% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 4.62 | 4.47 | −3.0% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 602 / 1049 | 602 / 1043 | 0.0% / −0.6% |
| Requests / generated tokens in 3600 s | 1502 / 1.481M | 1504 / 1.486M | +0.1% / +0.3% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 294.4 / 239.5 | 314.3 / 246.8 | +6.8% / +3.0% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 194.4 / 101.1 | 205.3 / 103.4 | +5.6% / +2.2% |

TPOT is reported as median and p90 rather than mean: in this replay a few short-output requests wait behind another request's long chunked prefill (up to 4.3 s for a 2-token answer), and a single such request moves the mean of a 3600 s run by up to 3 ms/token. Matching every request across the six concurrency-8 runs (baseline, #41133, #41134, two runs each), no request stalled in both runs of a PR without also stalling in a baseline run.

Decode step, same image and recipe (baseline = this PR with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ=0`; concurrency 1: 9 requests
per configuration over three alternating server instances; concurrency 4: four clients started together, overlap
window, 3 runs):

| Load | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1, 72k context | 8.65 ms | 8.21 ms | −5.1% |
| c1, 200k context | 9.11 ms | 8.71 ms | −4.4% |
| c4, 72k context | 11.50 ms | 11.02 ms | −4.2% |

With this PR the step time varies more between server instances than the baseline does (instance means 7.99–8.44 ms at
c1 / 72k, every baseline run within 8.53–8.74 ms); within an instance it is stable.

Kernel microbenchmark (MI355X, HIP-graph replay, weights streamed from HBM with buffers rotated over > 256 MB MALL,
GEMM only):

| Shape | Tokens | `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` (µs) | This kernel (µs) | % of streaming-read ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| packed GDN `in_proj` (5184 x 4096) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 9.97 / 10.00 / 10.03 / 8.39 | 5.66 / 5.85 / 5.87 / 6.37 | 85 / 82 / 82 / 75 |
| `qkv_proj` (4608 x 4096) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 9.70 / 9.72 / 9.75 / 8.17 | 5.43 / 5.53 / 5.62 / 6.12 | 82 / 81 / 79 / 73 |
| `out_proj` / `o_proj` (4096 x 2048) | 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 | 5.31 / 5.43 / 5.44 / 4.73 | 3.37 / 3.52 / 3.58 / 3.78 | 83 / 79 / 78 / 74 |

Fused producers at 4 tokens: GDN gated norm + quant 3.97 → 2.66 µs, attention gate multiply + quant 3.79 → 2.14 µs.
That removes 60 `_per_token_group_quant_8bit` launches per verify step.

title: [AMD] One-launch small-M MoE router for Qwen3.5 on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

On MI355X at low concurrency, each Qwen3.5-397B MoE layer routes a verify batch of 1 to 8 tokens through three launches before the small-M MoE kernel from #40204: the router gate GEMM (`[M, 4096] x [512, 4096]`), `_router_triton_kernel` (softmax over 512 experts, top-10, renormalize; one wave per token doing 10 serial argmax passes), and `_fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights_kernel` (the shared-expert gate GEMV and slot 11). All three are latency-bound at these sizes. In the server's verify step they cost 19.9 us per layer together (eager trace, M = 4), about 1.2 ms per step across 60 layers, plus the MTP layer in draft and draft extend. This PR replaces them with one launch.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/smallm_router_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_router.hip`). It is built with `hipcc` on first use and launched through ctypes, reusing #40204's `_hipcc`, `_hip_lib`, `_check` and `_Kernel`. No build-time or wheel change.
- One launch of 257 or 513 blocks, depending on M. Each block computes one or two of the 513 gate rows (512 routed experts plus the shared-expert gate, read in place from `gate.weight` and `shared_expert_gate.weight`) with fp32 accumulation. The last block to finish, elected by a self-resetting ticket counter so the kernel is graph-safe, rounds the routed logits to bf16, then runs top-10 (lowest id wins ties, as in `_router_triton_kernel`), softmax and renormalize. It writes slot 10 = (512, `sigmoid(shared logit) * scale`). The output is exactly the `topk_ids [M, 11] int32` / `topk_weights [M, 11] fp32` that `smallm_moe_gfx950` already consumes.
- `qwen2_moe.py`: one guarded call at the top of `_forward_router_experts` (5 lines). The guard requires gfx95, 1 <= M <= 8, bf16 hidden 4096, gate `[512, 4096]` and shared gate `[1, 4096]` in bf16, exactly one fused shared expert, EP 1, the auto/aiter MoE runner, top-10 with renormalize, no EPLB remap or simulated routing, and not inside a piecewise CUDA graph. Everything else takes today's path. The routed-expert capture and expert-distribution recorder hooks still run.
- The kernel is used for M <= 8 only. The single-block top-k tail makes it slower than today's path from 9 tokens up (0.80x at 9, 0.45x at 40), so c4 verify batches (16 tokens) keep today's path.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER=0` turns it off. A build or load failure disables it for the process.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_router_gfx950.py`. It covers ids and weights against today's `moe_fused_gate` + `fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights` at 1 / 3 / 4 / 8 tokens on exactly representable inputs (many ties), fallback at 9 and 41 tokens and for unsupported dtype and shape, the off switch, and graph replay == eager. It passes on `v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`.

## Accuracy Tests

Router logits are rounded to bf16 before top-k, as today. Against an fp64-then-bf16 reference on real activations (10,022 token rows), this kernel agrees on 100% of expert choices. Today's path agrees on 98.3%, because its bf16 gate GEMM is not correctly rounded at M >= 2.

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (revision e17e5f0), MI355X TP4, InferenceX recipe (FP8 KV cache, EAGLE MTP
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real draft), lm-eval `local-chat-completions` with chat template, 5-shot GSM8K (InferenceX
task), thinking disabled, 16384-token output budget, temperature 0. At most 2 running requests, so every verify batch (<= 8 tokens) is inside the kernel's range.

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.73% (1289/1319) | 97.73% (1289/1319) |
| This PR | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |

GPQA diamond (198 questions, repeat 8, simple-evals grader), same servers, thinking on, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 20, 32768-token output budget:

| Configuration | Score |
|---|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 0.871 (1379/1584) |
| This PR | 0.881 (1396/1584) |
| Reference (Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B model card) | 0.884 |

Same GSM8K task at TP2 (thinking disabled, at most 2 running requests):

| Configuration | Strict-match | Flexible-extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline (main `1417345f5f`) | 97.57% (1287/1319) | 97.57% (1287/1319) |
| This PR | 97.65% (1288/1319) | 97.65% (1288/1319) |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X, TP4 / EP1, InferenceX MI355X agentic recipe for this model (image
`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260923`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.80`, EAGLE MTP
3 / 1 / 4, simulated acceptance length 3.39, BF16 MTP layer as in the recipe), baseline = main `1417345f5f` (includes
#39901, #39902 and #40204), this PR = the same commit + this PR. Full 3600 s aiperf AgentX trace replay on the same four
GPUs, one configuration at a time, nothing else on the node.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 2.60 | 2.48 | −4.6% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 3.04 | 2.94 | −3.3% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 3.14 | 3.03 | −3.5% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 372 / 795 | 392 / 797 | +5.2% / +0.2% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 657 | 684 | +4.1% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 384.0 / 328.4 | 403.6 / 339.9 | +5.1% / +3.5% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 238.3 / 137.6 | 241.8 / 140.8 | +1.5% / +2.3% |

Concurrency 8, average of two full runs per configuration (the second pass in reverse order). This is a no-regression
check: verify batches are 4 x running requests, so up to 32 tokens, above this kernel's M <= 8 guard; the router
change is inactive once more than two requests run:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 3.40 | 3.29 | −3.4% |
| TPOT p90 (ms/token) | 4.18 | 4.19 | +0.4% |
| ITL p95 (ms) | 4.62 | 4.63 | +0.3% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 602 / 1049 | 591 / 1032 | −1.8% / −1.6% |
| Requests / generated tokens in 3600 s | 1502 / 1.481M | 1506 / 1.490M | +0.2% / +0.7% |
| Interactivity (1 / TPOT) p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 294.4 / 239.5 | 304.6 / 238.8 | +3.5% / −0.3% |
| E2E normalized interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 194.4 / 101.1 | 202.6 / 103.5 | +4.2% / +2.4% |

TPOT is reported as median and p90 rather than mean: in this replay a few short-output requests wait behind another request's long chunked prefill (up to 4.3 s for a 2-token answer), and a single such request moves the mean of a 3600 s run by up to 3 ms/token. Matching every request across the six concurrency-8 runs (baseline, #41133, #41134, two runs each), no request stalled in both runs of a PR without also stalling in a baseline run.

Decode step at concurrency 1, one request, same image and recipe (15 requests per configuration, three alternating
server blocks; baseline = this PR with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER=0`):

| Context | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 72k tokens | 8.79 ms | 8.07 ms | −8.2% |
| 200k tokens | 9.06 ms | 8.38 ms | −7.5% |

Kernel microbenchmark (MI355X, HIP-graph replay, 512 MB memset before each call to flush L2 / MALL, routing for one
MoE layer):

| Tokens | 3 kernels today (µs) | This kernel (µs) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 12.39 | 8.54 | −31% |
| 2 | 12.82 | 8.80 | −31% |
| 4 | 12.90 | 9.05 | −30% |
| 8 | 13.26 | 11.66 | −12% |

In the live server the step saves more than this table suggests: today's `_router_triton_kernel` runs at 11.2 µs per
layer in verify and 23.6 µs in draft extend (about 7 µs in isolation), while the new kernel costs about the same
everywhere.

title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable FP8 and MXFP4 serving on gfx950
body:
## Motivation Serve the official GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint and [`OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4) on MI355X (gfx950) at full speed and correct output. The target stack is zero-RoPE sparse attention, FP8 KV cache, and graph-enabled EAGLE 5/1/6. `main` now includes all ten Day-0 enablement PRs (#38545, #38546, #38547, #39317, #39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #39778, #39779). This PR adds the remaining correctness fixes and optimizations for serving Flash on gfx950. On the same four MI355X GPUs and AgentX replay, it measures **+14.3%** geomean output throughput over `main` at c1–c32, with higher P90 interactivity at every rung. At c48, `main` falls off the frontier, while this PR holds it. The four CI and test-hygiene fixes that used to be here now live in #40721. ## What changed Runtime paths are relative to `python/sglang/`; tests are excluded. | Area | Kind | Change | Files | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | K-pool top-k | Correctness (CUDA and HIP) | A threshold bin holding more than 4,096 candidates is rescanned with unique score/index keys, so ties or late higher scores are never clipped. The ordinary fast path is unchanged. HIP sets the dynamic shared-memory attribute. | `kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/kpool_topk_transform.cuh` | | K-pool scoring memory | Correctness · HIP | The logits row budget counts AITER's 256-column row padding, so a chunk cannot exceed AITER's 2 GiB limit, and page indices are promoted to int64 before offsetting. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py`
`srt/layers/attention/dsa/kpool_fp8_index.py` | | Unfused top-k memory | Correctness · all backends | Ragged batches above 4,096 rows run in 4,096-row chunks (`_TOPK_ROW_CHUNK`). Each row's top-k depends only on that row, so results are identical on every backend; only the scratch peak changes. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py` | | Graph variants | Correctness / capture cost | K-pool has no dense-skip path, so it is captured once instead of as a dense/sparse pair. Without a host length mirror, sparse is chosen without a device sync. | `srt/layers/attention/graph_variants.py` | | Attention backend lookup | Correctness | GLM-5.3-Flash wraps DSA inside the hybrid KDA backend, so on `main` the FP8 MHA prefix read takes the outer backend and fails with `forward_metadata is None` on the first image request (reproduced on MI355X). `resolve_attn_backend` now unwraps to the full-attention child. AITER extend also prefers the per-batch `qo_indptr`. | `srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py`
`srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` | | Visible-prefix / Mamba ownership | Correctness | A verify step can commit past the stop token; only client-visible tokens are cached. The other ping-pong slot's length is tracked, so a shorter key donates the state that actually matches it. Freed rows can no longer scatter into a reused slot. | `srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`
`srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`
`srt/mem_cache/{base_prefix_cache,common,memory_pool}.py`
`srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba.py` | | Mamba chunk fill | Correctness | Exact chunk fill is disabled for Mamba caches, because checkpoints only land on page-aligned chunk ends. | `srt/managers/schedule_policy.py` | | Graph read fences | Correctness | Without an in-graph marker (HIP), the read-done event is published after replay rather than before. Draft extend follows the backend's declared read end. | `srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | EAGLE draft on ROCm | Optimization · measured | ROCm enables rejection sampling (#37134), but verify takes argmax for all-greedy batches and never reads the draft distribution. The draft now skips the full-vocab softmax, Gumbel sample and probs stack for those batches and captures a matching greedy graph variant. | `srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | KDA fused verify | Correctness + optimization · HIP only | On top of #39524: separately rounded conv products (bit-exact with the reference on gfx950), a one-wave default, and BV16 for measured GLM shapes. The HIP gate keys on gfx950, bf16 QKV, fp32 conv weights, T ∈ {6, 8}, and batch 1–16. | `kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`
`srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py` | | Chat serving | Optimization / correctness | Send the token ids already rendered instead of re-tokenizing long text-only prompts. Apply the GLM47 full-assistant grammar only when tools are present, since its terminal state ends requests even under `ignore_eos`. | `srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py` | | Quark loading | Correctness | Block-FP8 is claimed only when the activation grouping matches the weight block. `ignore` is materialized once. Quark `weight_scale` maps to `weight_scale_inv` only when the name is missing. | `srt/layers/quantization/quark/{quark,utils}.py`
`srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Vision downsample | Optimization · measured | The non-overlapping 2×2 merge uses `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold + linear path, which avoids the MIOpen search. | `srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Small ROCm fixes | Correctness | `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` accepts any GPU device (`kDLGPU`), and a comment in the AITER MoE runner is corrected. | `kernels/jit/csrc/speculative/sampling.cuh`
`srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py` | | MI355X cookbook | Docs | FP8 and MXFP4 on the GLM-5.3-Flash selector, with TP4/EP4 commands and the ROCm runtime environment used for the measurements below. | `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.3-Flash.mdx`
`docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash.jsx`
`docs/src/snippets/_playground.jsx` | Footprint against `main`: 26 production files (+361 / −80), 14 test files (+563 / −21), 3 docs files (+179 / −26). ## Serving performance Setup: four MI355X VFs, TP4/EP4, FP8 E4M3 KV, EAGLE 5/1/6, 393-entry AgentX corpus, 900 s per rung, image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260918`. The client and server are pinned to the same NUMA placement, and `main` and this PR ran back to back on the same GPUs.
Serving command (identical for both arms; only the source differs) ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_ONLINE_TUNE=0 \ SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false \ SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1 SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1 \ HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE \ PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4 \ --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --quantization quark --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 262144 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \ --max-running-requests 96 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 96 --min-free-slots-delay 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --prefill-decode-interval 0 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-attention-mode prefill \ --speculative-accept-threshold-single 1.0 --speculative-accept-threshold-acc 1.0 \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 0.50 --hicache-write-policy write_through \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --mm-feature-transport cpu ``` Transformers is pinned to `e4052f55` for the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration classes.
| Concurrency | This PR tok/s | `main` tok/s | vs `main` | This PR P90 tok/s/user | `main` P90 tok/s/user | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 252.9 | 237.9 | +6.3% | 374.4 | 365.0 | | 2 | 443.2 | 394.6 | +12.3% | 337.5 | 326.1 | | 4 | 768.7 | 657.2 | +17.0% | 293.1 | 287.5 | | 8 | 1,253.1 | 1,137.4 | +10.2% | 237.1 | 226.8 | | 16 | 1,849.9 | 1,608.5 | +15.0% | 172.4 | 157.8 | | 32 | 2,304.8 | 1,829.2 | +26.0% | 111.0 | 94.7 | | 48 | 2,411.3 | off frontier | — | 78.1 | off frontier | Geomean output throughput: **+14.3%** over `main` at c1–c32. P90 tok/s/user is the 90th percentile of each request's reciprocal mean inter-token latency. ![AgentX frontier on four MI355X GPUs: this PR vs main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34d8e433-a9c8-41f0-a492-96cd51fe3610) ### Checkpoint and hardware context These replays were measured at `5fd4387a75`, before the Day-0 merges; this PR's head matches that source within run-to-run noise on the same AgentX ladder. Against the official `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8 checkpoint on the same four-GPU MI355X serving policy, OneNexus MXFP4 measures **+12.4%** geomean output throughput and **+18.2%** geomean P90 per-user rate over c1–c48, with zero request errors in both runs. This compares complete checkpoints, not an isolated quantization kernel. ![Measured OneNexus MXFP4 versus official FP8 AgentX frontiers on four MI355X VFs](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/fp8-mxfp4-agentx-frontier.png) Against `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` under the identical serving setup, OneNexus is within 0.1% geomean output throughput and +1.0% geomean P90 per-user rate over c1–c48 (9,223 vs 9,264 requests, zero errors in both).
OneNexus vs AMD MXFP4, per rung | Concurrency | OneNexus tok/s | AMD tok/s | Output delta | OneNexus P90 tok/s/user | AMD P90 tok/s/user | P90 delta | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 261.76 | 258.89 | +1.1% | 379.08 | 364.96 | +3.9% | | 2 | 444.88 | 444.09 | +0.2% | 333.60 | 330.21 | +1.0% | | 4 | 764.52 | 769.09 | −0.6% | 295.25 | 297.03 | −0.6% | | 8 | 1,283.08 | 1,278.38 | +0.4% | 241.23 | 237.75 | +1.5% | | 16 | 1,845.35 | 1,857.38 | −0.6% | 178.88 | 179.39 | −0.3% | | 32 | 2,279.72 | 2,290.16 | −0.5% | 110.35 | 110.00 | +0.3% | | 48 | 2,331.22 | 2,340.38 | −0.4% | 74.85 | 73.89 | +1.3% |
The next plot places the measured MI355X MXFP4 frontier next to **supplied four-GPU B300 estimates**. The B300 runs were not reproduced here, and the DSA backend and serving installation differ, so this is context rather than a controlled cross-hardware claim. ![Measured OneNexus MXFP4 MI355X frontier and supplied B300 estimate](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/final-agentx-frontier.png) The [matched serving protocol](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/fp8-mxfp4-agentx-protocol.md) has per-rung cache, capacity and acceptance data. ## Measured operator optimizations **KDA fused verify.** At batch 8 with eight verification tokens, the reference graph launches convolution and recurrence separately (**38.9 μs**). The single fused kernel with BV4 tiles is slower (**41.7 μs**), because it repeats the Q/K convolution across 32 value tiles. BV16 cuts the grid to 8 tiles and the paired time to **28.4 μs**, **27.0% less operator time**. For the six-token EAGLE 5/1/6 shape: **31.50 → 23.02 μs** at batch 8 and **37.66 → 33.03 μs** at batch 16. On this PR's head, the tuning still measures about 26% faster at batch 8 on top of #39524, with bit-exact output. ![KDA before/after GPU traces and paired graph timings: reference, initial fusion, and tuned fusion](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/resolve/main/assets/kda-trace-optimization.png) This is an isolated MI350X VF (gfx950) study with synthetic GLM TP4-shaped tensors, not model throughput. See the [study and full data](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/kda-trace-study.md). **Vision merge.** The 2×2 downsample has a non-overlapping kernel and stride, no padding and one group, so each patch is a linear projection. Reusing `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold + linear path skips the MIOpen search. On the model's actual `[256, 1024, 2, 2]` merge layout, first-call time falls **4.50 → 3.31 s (−26.5%)** and warmed graph time **63.28 → 25.62 μs (−59.5%)**, with identical output. See the [operator study](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4/blob/main/reproduction/mhc-vision-operator-study.md). The AITER mHC dispatch and its caller-applied RMSNorm fix, measured in the same study, landed in `main` via #38545. ## Accuracy On the serving configuration above (sgl-eval 0.1.2, 500 examples, reasoning effort max, temperature 0): GSM8K **0.978**, MMLU **0.870**. Checkpoint quality against `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, on identical pinned samples with one frozen runtime, graphs and speculation off, BF16 KV, greedy decoding, and truncations kept in the denominator: | Checkpoint | GSM8K | MMLU | GPQA Diamond | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4` | 490/500 | **428/500** | **139/198** | | `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` | 491/500 | 423/500 | 132/198 | The MMLU (+1.0 point) and GPQA Diamond (+3.5 points) differences do not reach `p < 0.05`; see the [quality protocol and paired statistics](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4#text-reasoning-quality). ## Validation - On gfx950, the 14 changed test files and `main`'s Mamba checkpoint and radix lock-ref tests pass (1,626 passed, 0 failed), including the native k-pool top-k and KDA bit-exactness kernels. - Every serving boot passes the basic, 30,031-token long-context, non-greedy and image-cached follow-up probes (320 cached tokens). - The cookbook-generated MI355X MXFP4 command boots on this PR and passes the same probes, with GSM8K 0.980 and MMLU 0.866. - pre-commit passes on all changed files. ## Checklist - [x] Format and lint all changed files. - [x] Keep tests to behavior and numerical regressions, with native gfx950 coverage. - [x] Measure AgentX throughput against `main`, plus accuracy on the serving configuration. - [ ] Pass the upstream CI matrix. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36263450821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36263450821) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #36263450685](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36263450685) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36263450819](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36263450819)

title: [Docs] Add Qwen3 Ascend recipes and measured A3/A2 results
body:
## Motivation and scope

The Qwen3 cookbook lacks Ascend NPU deployment recipes. This adds seven selectable combinations: four A3 8B/30B-A3B recipes, A2 TP4 recipes for 32B BF16 and W8A8, and an A2 TP8 candidate for 235B W8A8. Related task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1216.

**Stage delivery:** this PR is ready for review of the measured A3 8B/30B and A2 32B documentation, reproduction commands, and explicit validation labels. Six recipes have measured performance. Five recipes have verified accuracy: A3 8B low latency, both A3 30B recipes, and both A2 32B recipes. A3 8B TP1 retains its historical GPQA result with one rejected request and is not accuracy-verified. The 235B selector entry is an explicitly unverified candidate with no measured benchmark. This stage does not complete the full related task.

- Provide editable checkpoint paths, interfaces, service settings, and startup, inference, accuracy, and performance commands; require a draft checkpoint only when EAGLE3 is enabled.
- Label physical cards and logical NPU devices explicitly: one device per A2 card, two per measured A3 card. The shared component supports per-NPU throughput while preserving GPU defaults and hides the disabled Playground submission hint.
- Keep 235B BF16 outside the single-node selector: it requires two interconnected eight-card A2 nodes and storage for approximately 470 GB of weights. The 235B W8A8 recipe remains an untuned eight-card candidate.
- Document the 32B W8A8 source discrepancy: its A2 title says two cards but its command launches TP4; this recipe requires four actual A2 devices.

## Runtime and checkpoints

Documentation and A2 runs use SGLang source `b44e2486824e2fbde9cbcb09adad10bce5593c16`. A3 measurements are from **2026-09-12**, source `c389dd086340878934bf96bc209534f1fbb8440c`; A2 BF16 and the final W8A8 GPQA evaluation completed on **2026-09-23**. A3 results are not measurements on the newer documentation base.

- **A3:** one physical card exposing two 64 GB devices; CANN 9.0.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0, sgl-kernel-npu 2026.9.0, triton-ascend 3.2.1.dev20260530, Transformers 5.8.1.
- **A2:** four 64 GB Ascend 910B3 devices; CANN 9.0.0, torch/torch-npu 2.10.0, official 910B/aarch64 kernel 2026.9.0, Transformers 5.12.1, memfabric-hybrid 1.1.4, memfabric-zbal 1.1.2. BF16 uses `--max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8`, without EAGLE3. No additional host tuning was applied.
- **Checkpoints (main + draft):** 8B: `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-8B-w8a8` + `Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-8B-zh`; 30B: `Eco-Tech/Qwen3-30B-A3B-w8a8` + `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-a3B_eagle3`; 32B W8A8: `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-32B-W8A8` + `Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh`; 32B BF16: `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`. A2 downloads passed recorded size/SHA-256 checks.

## Accuracy

| Recipe | Evaluation | Correct / evaluated | Accuracy | Successful requests |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 8B W8A8 low latency, TP2 | GSM8K, 5-shot completion, temperature 0, output budget 512 | 1157 / 1314 | 88.05% | 1314 / 1314 |
| A3 8B W8A8 high throughput, TP1; retest pending | GPQA Diamond, 0-shot, temperature 1, output budget 40000 | 121 / 198 | 61.11% | 197 / 198 |
| A3 30B-A3B W8A8, TP2 | AIME 2025, 0-shot, temperature 1, output budget 32768 | 23 / 30 | 76.67% | 30 / 30 |
| A2 32B BF16 low latency, TP4 | Full GSM8K, 8 client threads | 1139 / 1314 | 86.68% | 1314 / 1314 |
| A2 32B W8A8, TP4 | GPQA Diamond, output budget 38000 | 132 / 198 | 66.67% | 198 / 198 |
| A2 32B W8A8, TP4; retained historical attempt | GPQA Diamond, output budget 40000 | 139 / 198 | 70.20% | 197 / 198 |

The 30B workloads share one accuracy run. GSM8K excludes five prompt examples from 1,319 rows; all scored responses were nonempty with valid answer extraction. BF16 had no API errors, with 1136 `stop` and 178 `length` outcomes; all truncations remain scored. AIME had 27 `stop` and three actual `max_tokens` truncations, with all 30 requests successful. Recorded A3 GPQA/AIME used EvalScope 1.11.1, seed 42, and client concurrency 64/16.

**GPQA correction:** both historical 40,000-budget attempts rejected index 127 because 2,829 input tokens plus 40,000 requested output tokens exceeded the 40,960 context limit. EvalScope produced a synthetic `model_length` result with `error=null`; this was not an ordinary output truncation. The scores retain all 198 questions, including the failed request. The earlier A3 claim of 198 successful requests is corrected to 197. Public examples now use 38,000; neither historical score validates that revised protocol. The independent full A2 rerun completed with 198 HTTP 200 responses, 198 `stop` outcomes, no rejections, and no empty final answers. Its 132/198 result is reported separately without splicing or selecting the higher historical score. The changed output budget and stochastic sampling do not establish a controlled accuracy regression. A3 requires its own retest when resources are available.

## Performance

Each row is one complete formal run. A3 input/output lengths are 3,500/1,500; A2 W8A8 uses 3,584/1,536 and BF16 18,000/4,000. Runs use the random ShareGPT workload, seed 1, range ratio 1, cache flushing, and detailed output. BF16 performance client concurrency is 1, independently of the server limit of 8.

| Recipe | TP | Client concurrency | Successful requests | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s, service | Total tok/s per logical NPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 8B low latency | 2 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 920.20 | 4.11 | 211.62 | 352.69 |
| A3 8B high throughput | 1 | 64 | 256 / 256 | 4578.23 | 29.94 | 1778.40 | 5927.99 |
| A3 30B-A3B low latency | 2 | 1 | 1 / 1 | 169.15 | 5.57 | 175.69 | 292.81 |
| A3 30B-A3B high throughput | 2 | 160 | 640 / 640 | 3619.48 | 46.05 | 3026.47 | 5044.12 |
| A2 32B BF16 low latency | 4 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 2888.82 | 32.96 | 29.69 | 40.83 |
| A2 32B W8A8 high throughput | 4 | 100 | 400 / 400 | 7326.95 | 73.59 | 1068.48 | 890.40 |

All 901 A3 and 404 A2 performance requests succeeded. Total throughput includes input and output tokens and is divided by the logical NPU count; A3 8B throughput uses one device of the allocated card. The one-request 30B low-latency row is not a latency distribution. Checkpoint/runtime/topology differences prevent controlled comparisons with the source TPOT references (A3: 5/37/10/50 ms; A2 W8A8: 55 ms).

## Validation and evidence

- After final GPQA score integration, checks passed for the three changed documentation files: cookbook configuration guard, pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and `mint validate`.
- The Mintlify link check found zero failures after in-memory Windows separator normalization. The stock Windows CLI still has reproduced path-resolution false positives; its unmodified result is not reported as passing.
- Earlier page checks confirmed A2 BF16 **Verified** with 86.68% / 32.96 ms / 40.83 token/s/NPU; A3 8B high throughput **Not Verified** with retained 61.11% / 5927.99 token/s/NPU; and 235B pending. Final A2 W8A8 rendering also passed: **Verified**, GPQA 66.67%, mean TPOT 73.59 ms, and 890.4 total token/s/NPU; the historical 139/198 attempt is separate and the final 198/198 natural-stop explanation is correct. This is documentation-only work.
- A3 archive: CRC and all 178 payload length/SHA-256 checks passed. A2 resource-smoke archive: CRC and eight payload checks passed.
- First A2 GPQA evidence: 83 verified files in `experiments/issue1216/a2-32b/evidence-gpqa-40000`; ZIP 6,333,748 bytes, SHA-256 `4143555dc69610bb09c2dc86b41cbc43c641bd1e71d78e911617f917877ecf1a`.
- Final A2 32B archive: `evidence-final.zip`, 10,337,895 bytes, SHA-256 `3e8906f1bc5d21cc110f63e0df2c5ce16be9639e1331c0ec9064bcea36aad6d2`; ZIP CRC and all 147 payload checks passed. The model service is stopped and final NPU inspection found no processes on any of the four cards; platform UI confirmed `Issue1216QwenA2` shut down, and the bridge is stopped; other environments were unchanged.

## Follow-up hardware work outside this stage's acceptance scope

- Retest A3 8B TP1 GPQA at the corrected budget; current resources are A2 only, and A2 results cannot validate A3.
- Validate 235B W8A8 on eight 64 GB-class A2 devices; the allocated eight-device 910B4 node was checked and has only 32 GiB HBM per device. Confirm two-node connectivity and sufficient shared storage before 235B BF16 validation on 16 devices.

These follow-ups remain open under the related task and are not claimed as completed by this PR. Review this stage on the accuracy of the published measured results, reproduction details, and explicit unverified labels. No new model run is implied by moving this documentation stage out of draft.

## Checks for the reviewed commit

Head: 89f44d2fce6554a3a476183999d422315d07ba46. The cookbook configuration guard and git diff whitespace check were re-run successfully before this metadata update; the source diff is unchanged. Previously recorded Base, Lint and NPU workflows passed at this head. Extra and Extra AMD stopped at their explicit draft-PR gate, so they are not reported as passing model tests. Check the live Checks tab for runs triggered after marking this stage ready.

title: [AMD] Add experimental MiniMax-M3 FlyDSL attention
body:
## Motivation

**Experimental, opt-in, and not qualified for general use.**

Add an opt-in native SGLang attention path for MiniMax-M3 using the AITER FlyDSL paged-attention kernel from [AITER #4332](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4332) and GPU work planner from [AITER #5546](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5546).

This calls AITER directly and does not modify its attention kernel. The PR is ready for review of the SGLang integration and its qualification gaps, using concrete gfx950 measurements.

### AITER APIs and SGLang-specific integration

The [AITER #4332](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4332) API provides FlyDSL paged attention. [AITER #5546](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5546) provides GPU-side dynamic partition planning and graph-safe refresh. SGLang uses the planner only for dense, uneven-context graph decode; sparse calls keep static partitions.

The SGLang-specific integration connects these AITER APIs to MiniMax's cache and attention lifecycle: SHUFFLE 5D main KV writes, the existing NHD indexer/top-k path, conversion of per-head sparse selections to physical page tables, graph metadata refresh, and guards for unsupported modes. The AITER kernel is unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_MINIMAX_FLYDSL_DECODE` (default false) and `SGLANG_MINIMAX_FLYDSL_PLAN` (default true; used only when the feature is enabled).
- Write the main FP8 KV cache directly in SHUFFLE 5D while keeping the existing NHD index cache, indexer, and top-k reuse policy.
- Adapt sparse selections into physical page tables without copying the whole KV cache. Handle per-head selections, partial final pages, and causal prefill rows.
- Use static FlyDSL splits for sparse attention and optionally plan dense graph decode on the GPU. Persist int32 graph lengths and capture their refresh from SGLang's int64 inputs once per forward.
- Gather/dequantize used KV for dense prefill; process sparse prefill as bounded chunks of causal query rows.
- Reject unsupported speculation/cache-transfer/parallelism configurations when opted in.
- Add an optional Docker build argument to skip the default AITER backports when selecting a newer AITER pin that already contains them. Default image dependencies and backport behavior are unchanged.
- Include manual GPU validation, serving/benchmark reproduction, and machine-readable result summaries under `test/manual/minimax_m3/flydsl/`.

**Dependencies:** measured with AITER `94dca7bc674650b6de2609eeae2bcdd58e970bf3` and FlyDSL `0.3.4.1`. The feature requires this newer kernel/compiler stack; applying the SGLang patch alone does not upgrade dependencies. The example Docker build has not been validated; measurements used source/dependency overlays in an existing ROCm container.

## Accuracy Tests

Gfx950 GPU adapter checks: **43/48 pass**. Passing coverage includes dense decode, graph replay with changed int64 lengths, sparse decode, and 12 exact comparisons against independently CPU-built page tables.

**Five short sparse-prefill cases fail the original `atol=0.01, rtol=0.08` tolerance** against dequantized FP32 attention (page16/head2; page64/head1–2; page128/head1–2). In these cases the adapter exactly matches direct AITER with independently constructed metadata. This points to FP8 arithmetic rather than page-table construction, but does not establish acceptable model accuracy. The tolerance has not been loosened. The target TP4/page16/one-KV-head group passes its six numerical checks.

MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 GSM8K chat/thinking smoke check, first 64 questions, temperature 0, maximum 4096 output tokens:

| Mode | Correct | Invalid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing SGLang | 64/64 | 0 |
| FlyDSL static | 63/64 | 0 |
| FlyDSL planned | 64/64 | 0 |

This is not full accuracy qualification or proof of equivalence. A larger paired evaluation is still needed. All three modes also passed dummy-weight startup, decode graph, mixed-length request, and chunked-prefill smoke checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Four MI355X/gfx950 GPUs, TP4, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, BF16 activations, FP8 KV, page16, chunk8192, decode graphs enabled, radix cache disabled. NCCL all-reduce; custom all-reduce disabled. No EAGLE/speculative decoding.

Two repetitions per mode/workload/concurrency, 8–40 requests per point, fixed seed and forced output lengths. All **60 measurements / 1,272 timed requests succeeded**, with matching per-request input/output lengths across modes. Loading, graph capture, and warmup are excluded from timed results.

Planned FlyDSL versus existing SGLang, medians of run-level metrics:

| Workload | Concurrency | Output throughput (tok/s) | Throughput change | Median TPOT change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K input / 256 output | 1 | 74.43 → 70.99 | **-4.6%** | 6.2% slower |
| 8K input / 256 output | 2 | 136.01 → 129.29 | **-4.9%** | 6.6% slower |
| 8K input / 256 output | 10 | 312.54 → 317.80 | +1.7% | 0.4% lower |
| 8K input / 256 output | 15 | 379.14 → 388.80 | +2.5% | 0.9% lower |
| 8K input / 256 output | 20 | 430.83 → 447.45 | **+3.9%** | 2.3% lower |
| Mixed 1K–32K input / 8–256 output | 20 | 128.79 → 138.72 | **+7.7%** | 7.8% lower |

At concurrency20, median TTFT changes 3574.75 → 3325.88 ms for fixed8K and 2165.59 → 1973.47 ms for mixed lengths.

Caveats:

- Small-batch serving regresses; this is not an unconditional speedup.
- The isolated sparse kernel has 21.8% lower latency at batch20, but that is not a whole-model speedup. It excludes indexer/KV writes/other layers/communication and repeatedly uses warm tensors.
- No separate planner benefit is established: second-repetition static/planned throughput differs by at most 0.3% at concurrency10–20. The first static sweep was slower; shared JIT caches and fixed mode order confound attribution.
- Mixed-length concurrency2 is unstable; its aggregate +13.7% throughput is not reliable evidence of improvement.
- The short pilot cannot establish production tail latency or statistical significance for small gains. No full-model kernel profile was collected.
- This pilot uses MXFP8, no speculative decoding, and NCCL all-reduce. Results do not predict other weight formats, speculation modes, or communication paths.

## Remaining work before merge

- Resolve/qualify the five numerical failures and run full paired model accuracy evaluation.
- Investigate small-batch regressions.
- Add CI integration once the required AITER/FlyDSL dependency stack is available, and qualify gfx942 separately (only gfx950 was tested).
- Validate the Docker build and decide how to roll out the dependency update.
- Run longer fully warmed traces with varied mode order before drawing conclusions about the planner or small gains.

## Checklist

- [x] Repository pre-commit checks pass on all changed files.
- [x] Include manual GPU validation and reproducible benchmark scripts.
- [x] Document launch, routing, dependencies, measured results, and limitations.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results, including failures and regressions.
- [ ] Complete numerical/model accuracy qualification and registered CI coverage.

The runtime implementation is the GPU-tested version based on `fc9e1c8d296216ff1e216dfbe7286ef392448d28`; PR preparation changed formatting only (runtime ASTs checked unchanged). It merges cleanly with upstream `df1fc6ab6441abbdf21944958b131c03e0921253`.

title: feat(deepep_v2): expanded (do_expand=True) prefill dispatch for DeepEP-V2
body: ## Motivation Add a faster **prefill** path for the **DeepEP-V2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend** (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2`) that uses DeepEP's expanded dispatch layout, gated by `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND` (default `True`). DeepEP-V2 uses `ElasticBuffer`: one buffer serves both prefill and decode, switching behavior at runtime via `do_cpu_sync` / `do_expand`. The existing deepep_v2 backend already had an "expanded non-masked" prefill branch, but it was locked off at dispatch and used a slower fallback. This change opens and optimizes that branch so prefill runs on the expanded layout, while **leaving the decode (expand + masked slab) path unchanged**. The goal is a faster prefill MoE all-to-all with identical model outputs. In production PD-disaggregated (prefill/decode split) serving, decode runs on the V1 `low_latency` backend in a separate process (rationale in *Modifications → Why decode stays on V1*); this PR's optimization deliberately targets prefill only. ## Modifications ### Core All changes live inside the expand branch; the non-expand and decode paths are untouched. - **`token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** — unlock expand at dispatch. The backend bound `use_masked = use_expand_layout = not is_extend`, pinning prefill to non-expand; split them into `use_masked = is_decode` and `use_expand_layout = is_decode or _prefill_expand_enabled` so prefill can run expanded but never masked. Quantize the expanded recv scale column-major only under ue8m0 (non-ue8m0 stays row-major for the GEMM's own `tma_align`). Use ElasticBuffer hybrid mode when `nnodes > 1` (direct is NVLink-only and hangs across nodes); an explicit `--deepep-v2-mode direct` on multi-node is rejected with a clear error rather than silently overridden. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`** — add `fill_m_indices_from_psum` (label rows from the device `psum`, no cumsum / H2D / sentinel) and `scale_expanded_rows_` (in-place row weighting, stride-aware so it also handles the column-major fp8 input scale). - **`moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`** — the expanded non-masked pre/post permute use the two new kernels; leave `hidden_states_scale_tma_aligned` False so the contiguous GEMM still runs `tma_align_input_scale` on the expanded recv scale. The expand path applies the top-k weight before combine (which ignores `topk_weights` in expand mode) by folding the weight into down_proj's fp32 input scale — down_proj is linear and fp8 dequant is `fp8_q * scale`, so a per-row scale factor is numerically exact, shrinking a ~112 µs pass over the `[expanded, H]` bf16 tensor to ~4 µs over the `[expanded, H/128]` scale. (Under ue8m0 the scale is a power of two and multiplying by the weight would need re-rounding, so that case instead weights `down_output` with `scale_expanded_rows_` before combine.) - **`model_runner.py` + `model_runner_components/moe_ep_setup.py`** — prebuild the ElasticBuffer at deployment time (in `init_cuda_graphs`, after capture and before serving), skipping it when decode graph capture already built it, so the first request does not pay the ~2 GB symmetric alloc + cross-rank NCCL barrier. ### Wiring - **`models/mimo_v2.py`** — include `is_deepep_v2()` in the EP / `_enable_a2a_moe` branches. This is **required**: without it `_enable_a2a_moe` stays `False`, MoE runs `forward_normal` whose extra `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` (which `forward_deepep` skips, since `dispatcher.combine` already reduces across ranks) hangs the first cross-node request. - **`arg_groups/moe_hook.py`** — add `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` / `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` to the validated deepep_v2 architectures; divide the prefill token-budget check by `attn_tp_size` (a per-DP chunk scatters across the DP group's attn-TP ranks before dispatch, so a per-DP chunk of N needs `N / attn_tp_size` per EP rank, not N). - **`environ.py`** — add `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND` (default `True`). The per-rank dispatch-token cap keeps the existing `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` unchanged. ### `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND` (default: on) Prefill dispatch has two layouts; the **only** differing dispatch argument is `do_expand` (`do_cpu_sync` stays `True` in both, so shapes are exact and neither uses CUDA graph): - **`do_expand=False`** — dispatch returns `recv_x=[num_recv, H]`, one row per *deduplicated* token, not grouped by expert. A bridge kernel **`ep_scatter`** (inherited from V1) physically expands it into per-(token, expert) rows grouped by expert for the contiguous grouped GEMM. `ep_scatter` is two triton kernels: a light layout kernel (`ep_scatter_1`, ~1.7 µs) and a heavy full-hidden copy (`ep_scatter_2`, ~58 µs), plus one H2D of the per-expert counts. **This path's operator chain is the community's original non-expand design (`ep_scatter` → contiguous GEMM → `ep_gather`), used here as the A/B reference for `do_expand=True`** (here weighting is folded into `ep_gather`, with no down_proj scale folding). Note this path was actually broken on `main` — `ep_scatter_from_psum` was missing the `expert_start` / `num_experts` kernel args (a #35758 regression) — so it is a path this work also depends on being repaired; that fix landed separately in #38160, which this PR is rebased on top of. - **`do_expand=True`** (default) — DeepEP's `dispatch_copy_epilogue` produces the per-(token, expert) rows grouped by expert **within dispatch's own TMA copy**, so `ep_scatter` is not needed. The heavy `ep_scatter_2` (~58 µs) and that H2D both disappear; the light layout kernel is replaced by `fill_m_indices_from_psum` (~1.5 µs, reusing DeepEP's device-side `psum` instead of recomputing a cumsum). It removes one full HBM round-trip per MoE layer at no accuracy cost. `dispatch_copy_epilogue_impl` produces different outputs based on the `do_expand` template parameter (nsys traces): V1 dispatch: V2 dispatch (do_expand=False): V2 dispatch (do_expand=True): V2 combine (do_expand=True, topk weighted before combine): V2 combine (do_expand=True, topk weight folded into down_proj's input scale) — `_fwd_kernel_scale_expanded_rows` moved from before combine to before down_proj, acting only on the small fp8 input scale: https://aie-shared-objects.cnbj1.mi-fds.com/aie-shared-objects/prefill-DeepEP-V2-weighted-before-down_proj.nsys-rep This is the nsys trace captured when using DeepEP-V2 on the prefill side. In expand mode ElasticBuffer's combine refuses `topk_weights` (it does the un-expand and reduction itself inside the kernel), so the top-k weighting must be done by SGLang before combine. **Instead of scaling down_proj's bf16 output, this design folds each row's routing weight `w` into down_proj's fp32 input scale `down_input_scale=[M, I/128]` (`[~18432, 16]`) before the GEMM**: down_proj is linear and fp8 dequant is `value = q × scale`, and `w` is one positive scalar per row, so it merges into the input scale, the output carries the weight automatically, and the result is numerically exact. The weighted tensor shrinks from `[M, H]` bf16 (`[~18432, 6144]`, ~453 MB) to `[M, I/128]` fp32 (~1.2 MB), and the multiply folds into the pre-GEMM handling that already runs — measured **~112 µs → ~4 µs** (ue8m0-packed scales fall back to weighting the output). Default is `True` because it is strictly less work than `False` with identical results; set `0` to fall back to the non-expanded path for A/B comparison. "Less work" here means `do_expand=True` versus `do_expand=False`: - `do_expand=False` needs `ep_scatter` to physically expand the deduplicated `recv_x` into the per-expert layout; its heavy `ep_scatter_2` reads and writes all of hidden once (a **~58 µs full HBM round-trip**), plus one **H2D** copying the per-expert counts back to the device. - `do_expand=True` lets DeepEP's `dispatch_copy_epilogue` do the expansion within dispatch's own TMA copy, so **`ep_scatter_2` (~58 µs) and that H2D both disappear**, leaving only a ~1.5 µs `fill_m_indices_from_psum` to label rows. That removes one full hidden HBM round-trip per MoE layer (fewer kernels, one fewer large-tensor pass), with the GEMM and expert compute unchanged and results identical. ### Why decode stays on V1 `low_latency` (not DeepEP-V2) This PR's optimization targets prefill only. The deepep_v2 decode (expand + masked slab) path is left untouched; in production PD-disaggregated serving, decode runs on V1's `low_latency` mode in a separate process. Decode requires a masked GEMM (fixed-height slab `[num_local_experts, max_m, H]`) to be CUDA-graph-capturable: | | V1 `low_latency` | V2 `direct` | |---|---|---| | Output layout | `packed_recv_x = [num_local_experts, num_ranks×cap, H]` — fixed-height grid | compact per-expert buckets — dynamic bucket lengths | | Feeds masked GEMM directly? | **Yes** — the fixed-height layout *is* the masked-GEMM input | **No** — buckets don't align with `e × max_m` | | Bridge kernels needed | **None** | **Two**: `expand_to_masked_slab` (before GEMM) + `masked_slab_to_expand` (after) | V1's `low_latency` output is *natively* the masked-GEMM input, so decode needs no bridge kernels. V2's `direct` output must be reshaped into a slab and back — two extra HBM round-trips every layer, every step, with no offsetting benefit in SGLang (unlike vLLM, whose V2 decode gain comes from a decode-only activation kernel SGLang does not use). ## Accuracy Tests Verified with `--disaggregation-mode null` (single process; deepep_v2 drives both prefill and decode MoE dispatch — a stricter check than the production split), GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy decoding, MiMoV2, tp16/dp2: ``` python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9001 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --parallel 128 ``` | MoE a2a backend | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---| | `deepep_v1` (baseline) | 0.958 | 0.002 | | `deepep_v2` | 0.964 | 0.002 | The 0.006 gap (~8 of 1319 questions) is within greedy-decoding noise, so DeepEP-V2 has **no accuracy regression**. (Production uses V2 for prefill + V1 `low_latency` for decode; both paths are independently validated.) ## Speed Tests End-to-end prefill throughput, MiMoV2, TP8/EP16/DP2, chunk 32k per DP, `bench_serving`'s **Input token throughput (tok/s)**. "single DP throughput" = all-throughput / 2. A three-way comparison: V1 baseline, the community's existing deepep_v2 (`do_expand=False`), and this PR's final design (`do_expand=True` with the topk weight folded into down_proj's input scale, weighted-before-down_proj). `Δ` is the gain over V1. | request_lens (k) | request count | V1 (tok/s) | V2 community `do_expand=False` (tok/s) | Δ vs V1 | V2 **this PR** weighted-before-down_proj (tok/s) | Δ vs V1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8 | 512 | 25255.66 | 27028.59 | +7.0% | 29106.99 | +15.2% | | 16 | 512 | 25313.40 | 27189.06 | +7.4% | 28690.07 | +13.3% | | 32 | 256 | 24334.59 | 26097.61 | +7.2% | 27480.15 | +12.9% | | 64 | 256 | 22680.25 | 24432.20 | +7.7% | 25692.17 | +13.3% | | 128 | 128 | 20537.96 | 21686.12 | +5.6% | 22272.49 | +8.4% | | 256 | 64 | 16922.24 | 17753.09 | +4.9% | 18226.55 | +7.7% | | 512 | 24 | 12291.39 | 12766.78 | +3.9% | 13027.60 | +6.0% | | 768 | 16 | 9707.58 | 10036.62 | +3.4% | 10121.12 | +4.3% | | 960 | 8 | 8175.53 | 8345.79 | +2.1% | 8585.99 | +5.0% | Two takeaways: - **Versus V1**: the community deepep_v2 (`do_expand=False`) is already ~2–8% faster than V1; this PR pushes the gain to ~4–15% (~13–15% at short/medium sequence lengths, narrowing to ~4–6% at very long ones as attention's O(L²) cost dominates and the MoE all-to-all share shrinks). - **Versus the community deepep_v2**: this PR is further ahead at every sequence length (e.g. 8k: 27028 → 29107, +7.7%; 512k: 12767 → 13028, +2.0%), from the `ep_scatter_2` full-hidden copy that `do_expand=True` removes plus folding the topk weight into down_proj's input scale (shrinking a ~112 µs large-tensor weighting to ~4 µs). The rationale for each is in the `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_ENABLE_PREFILL_EXPAND` section above and in [`weighted-before-down_proj.md`](weighted-before-down_proj.md). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Validated end-to-end on a multi-node multi-GPU setup, and the GSM8K accuracy check above passed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes for reviewers ### Runtime environment Developed and validated on (2-node × 8-GPU, Hopper-class, ~140 GB HBM per GPU): | Component | Version / detail | |---|---| | CUDA | 12.9 (toolkit 12.9.2; base image `cu12`) | | NCCL | **2.30.7+cuda12.9** — DeepEP-V2's GIN API (`ncclGinRequest_t` / `ginTrafficClass`) needs 2.30.x; the bundled 2.29.x lacks these symbols, so the image overrides every `libnccl.so` (including torch's) with 2.30.7 | | DeepEP | **2.0.0** (the ElasticBuffer build exposing `deep_ep.ElasticBuffer`), built against torch 2.13 / NCCL 2.30.7, `cp312` | | PyTorch | 2.13 | | Python | 3.12 | | sgl-kernel | 0.4.5 | Communication backend: DeepEP-V2 (ElasticBuffer) communicates over **NCCL GIN** (GPU-Initiated Networking, reusing PyTorch's NCCL communicator), **not** NVSHMEM/IBGDA — the V2 path has no NVSHMEM dependency (NVSHMEM is the DeepEP-V1 transport). `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` is required by ElasticBuffer and is set automatically. Single node uses `--deepep-v2-mode direct` (NVLink); multi-node needs `hybrid` (selected automatically when `nnodes > 1`; an explicit `--deepep-v2-mode direct` on multi-node is rejected, since NVLink-only direct hangs across nodes). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36282416068](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36282416068) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #36282415968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36282415968) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36282416000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36282416000)

title: [PD] Wait for prefill completion before Mooncake early KV transfer
body:
With overlap scheduling, `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` can enqueue a transfer while the previous prefill forward is still writing the prefix. It records a completion event on `forward_stream`, but the Mooncake sender never consumes `_early_send_wait_event`. The transfer worker can therefore read incomplete KV. The Mori path already propagates and waits for this event.

Pass the event through the existing `TransferKVChunk` field and synchronize in the Mooncake transfer worker before reading source KV. Clear the consumed event and check request status after the wait so an abort during synchronization prevents transfer. The scheduler does not block on the event; chunks without an event retain their existing path.

Five CPU regressions cover event propagation for final/nonfinal sends, one-time event consumption, queue preservation, wait-before-read ordering, abort during the wait, and the no-event path. The added tests pass when executing the actual methods in a source-isolated CPU runner; the unpatched control fails the event/wait cases while the no-event case passes. The full transfer unit suite also passes (15 tests) with real engine imports on a MI355X, using the pinned reference image plus the three hash-checked candidate files. Real-weight GLM-5.3 FP8 serving validation also passes on MI355X with same-node Mooncake P4+D4, BF16 KV and 8192-token prefill chunks. The original image passed 7/12 known-answer checks with speculation OFF and 7/12 with native MTP3; the patched image passes 12/12 in each arm across cold, warm, forced eviction/resume and rewarm. Early cached-prefix sending remains enabled. Each arm retained all 140 native captures, and MTP3 has valid verification counters on every capture. Churn exceeded the measured L1 capacity. These diagnostics establish the reproduced transfer fix, not production capacity or numerical equivalence; cross-node and longer-context follow-ups remain separate.

Normal test entry point:

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py TestMooncakeEarlySend
```

This is an independent fix against upstream main `acc15c193b9d8813cb31b66cd19980fe0de9d72d`. It does not change speculative sampling or require an MTP implementation. Multi-chunk target-only PDD is included in the ongoing GPU reproducer.

title: Fix Qwen3-Next weight loader double-fusing pre-fused gate_up_proj (fixes #13214)
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #13214. `Qwen3NextForCausalLM.load_weights()` matched shard names with a plain substring check (`if weight_name not in name`). Checkpoints that ship an already-fused `gate_up_proj` (common for AWQ-quantized Qwen3-Next MoE checkpoints, where gate/up are merged before quantization) contain `up_proj` as a substring of `gate_up_proj`, so the stacked-params pass rewrote `...mlp.shared_expert.gate_up_proj.weight` into `...mlp.shared_expert.gate_gate_up_proj.weight`, producing the `KeyError` in the issue. Community analysis on the issue (ErenAta16, Prudctual) identified the matching logic itself as the real fix.

## Modifications

- Added `_match_weight_name()` in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_next.py`: anchors weight-name matching to `.`-separated path segments via `(^|\.)<name>(\.|$)`, so a pre-fused `gate_up_proj` no longer matches the `up_proj`/`gate_proj` shard entries (trailing-dot mapping names like `experts.3.gate_proj.` and `in_proj_qkv.` are handled by stripping the trailing dot before anchoring).
- Swapped the two `weight_name not in name` checks in `load_weights()` (stacked-params loop and expert-params loop) to the anchored matcher. All other load logic, including the `replaced_name not in params_dict` guards, is untouched.
- Added `test/srt/models/test_qwen3_next_weight_mapping.py` with 5 unit tests pinning the behavior (follows the existing `test_mamba2.py` precedent in the same directory).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable - this change only affects checkpoint weight-name matching at load time and produces byte-identical load behavior for all previously-loading checkpoints (verified by an old-vs-new match-decision differential over representative checkpoint names x every mapping entry; only the double-fuse case changes).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - load-time-only change; no forward-path code touched.

## Test status (honest)

The 5 new unit tests were written but could NOT be executed in the author's environment (importing `qwen3_next` requires `triton`, which is unavailable there). The matcher's logic was verified in isolation against every test assertion, and CI must run `test/srt/models/test_qwen3_next_weight_mapping.py` before merge.

## AI disclosure

This contribution was prepared with AI assistance (code and tests drafted with an AI coding assistant, then reviewed by the author). All claims about the change were verified against the actual source as described above.

title: Allocate packed weight receive buffers directly from metadata
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Packed weight updates allocate every destination tensor and concatenate their uninitialized bytes immediately before overwriting that buffer with a broadcast. Allocate the receive buffer directly from tensor metadata to remove the discarded concatenation and temporary allocations.

This draft targets `main` at `acc15c193b9d8813cb31b66cd19980fe0de9d72d`; current head `38eb4870597efa97c7a544d90c9e82b8d70cadfb`. Full-model weight-sync benefit is unmeasured.

## Modifications

- Add `FlattenedTensorBucket.empty(names, dtypes, shapes, device)`: retain byte offsets and allocate one contiguous uint8 buffer. Reconstruction returns the original typed shared-storage views.
- Use the factory in the current receive-only path. Preserve upstream's separate begin/load/end lifecycle, single broadcast, shared-storage views and error propagation. Sender packing, mixed-dtype wire format, quantization, collective group and finalization are unchanged.
- Fail on inconsistent metadata lengths, negative shapes, empty metadata or offsets incompatible with dtype alignment. No padding or dtype promotion.
- Rebased onto the current target while retaining its receive/load lifecycle. The factory and wire contract are unchanged. No API compatibility layer is added.

## Accuracy Tests

- **CI gate:** current PR CI is blocked because this PR remains a draft; this is separate from the CPU results below.

Current head `38eb4870597efa97c7a544d90c9e82b8d70cadfb`: macOS arm64 CPU, Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.14.0. No container or GPU used for this rebase.

- Six registered tests cover mixed uint8/FP8/FP32/BF16 bytes, dtype objects/strings, scalar/empty shapes, signed zero/infinity/NaN payloads, reconstruction aliases and invalid metadata. Test contents are unchanged.
- Bounded project-local checks compile and execute the actual receiver method bodies with only the collective intercepted, using four payload versions. They check byte/shape/dtype equality, shared storage and the branch's receive-only or model-delivery behavior. These checks do not import or qualify the complete serving runtime.

title: [Fix] Load FP8 KV-cache scales for Qwen3.5
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #37379.

When `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` is used with
`--quantization-param-path`, Qwen3.5 failed during startup because its model
classes did not expose `load_kv_cache_scales`. The architecture mixes full
attention and GatedDeltaNet layers, so the implementation must only apply the
loaded factors to full-attention layers. Pipeline-parallel ranks also contain
placeholder layers for stages they do not own.

## What changed

- Added `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.load_kv_cache_scales`.
- Skip GatedDeltaNet and pipeline-placeholder layers when applying factors.
- Populate `k_scale`, `v_scale`, `k_scale_float`, and `v_scale_float` for the
  Triton/FlashInfer paths.
- Added delegation through both Qwen3.5 conditional-generation wrappers.
- Added CPU unit coverage for skipping non-attention layers and wrapper
  delegation.

No open or historical PR references #37379 or this Qwen3.5 KV-scale-loading
fix (checked immediately before submission).

title: [HiCache] Add the page-unified KV load-back JIT kernel
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The load-back half of the page-unified HiCache layout, and the mirror of the staged write-back added in #39606. That PR writes a device pool out into host pages ordered

  MHA: (page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim), K=0 V=1
  MLA: (page, layer, page_size, dim)

but stops at write-back; nothing could read those pages back. This kernel does, for one layer at a time.

Per-layer and unstaged, unlike its write-back mirror. The two directions are not symmetric in how the runtime drives them: write-back moves a whole page at once, so staging it on the device and handing the bulk copy to the copy engine costs nothing extra. Load-back is walked layer by layer by the L2 transfer engine, which unblocks the forward pass one layer at a time, so staging whole pages per layer would move num_layers times the bytes the layer actually needs. Instead the SMs read the pinned host mapping in place, the way every other layout's per-layer load already does.

Each thread moves 16 bytes; the linear index runs dim-fastest then item, so a warp's lanes read consecutive host bytes for the tokens of one (head group, layer, K/V) cell. The grid is capped by kBlockQuota as in HiCacheKernel: the load overlaps a forward pass, so extra blocks buy bandwidth by taking SMs from it.

Note that head_group == 1 is NOT page_first_direct's byte order -- the K/V axis sits inside the page block here, not outside the pool. The HG=1 cases in the test pin that.

Correctness: 123 cases pass on B200 -- 3 geometries x {uint8, fp16, bf16} x {int32, int64} indices x {0, 1, 8} tokens, for MHA and MLA, each sweeping every layer, compared for exact equality against a PyTorch-indexing reference including the rows that must keep their sentinel. Payload is seeded noise, not a counter: a counter is periodic in the layer stride, so a layer mix-up would compare equal.

Round-trip against #39606: running that PR's write-back and then this kernel over 9 configurations (including the head-cut cases) returns the device pool bit-identical, which is the actual contract between the pair.

Performance (B200, PCIe gen5, 61 layers x 8 kv heads x 128 dim, bf16, page_size 64, one layer of K+V, payload counted once):

block_quota | 1 group | 2 groups | 4 groups | 8 groups
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
2 | 15.4-16.2 GB/s | 16.2-17.1 GB/s | 16.7-17.8 GB/s | 17.3-18.2 GB/s
16 | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s


against a 53.8 GB/s contiguous cudaMemcpyAsync ceiling. Bandwidth is flat in head-group count -- the run length does not matter, the grid cap does. The shipped default stays at 2; raising it is a measurement-led change that wants an end-to-end number, not a new-kernel PR.
