title: [HiCache] Store the MHA L2 host pool as INT8, 1.78x more cached tokens per GB
body:
## Motivation

HiCache stores L1 and L2 in the same dtype, so one byte of host DRAM buys one byte of cached KV. This keeps L1 BF16 for attention and stores L2 as INT8, restoring to BF16 on a hit. Caching policy, radix tree, scheduler and transfer engine are untouched; only the L2 representation changes.

For Qwen3-8B at TP=1: 82,944 host bytes/token against 147,456, so a fixed `--hicache-size` holds **1.78x more tokens**.

## Design trade-off

Every existing host pool mirrors its device pool's dtype, so the mover stays a byte copy. This one is asymmetric. The JIT mover takes separate strides but a single `element_size`, so a 2048-byte BF16 row cannot be written into a 1152-byte encoded row. Both directions stage through a same-width device buffer:

```
D2H  device BF16 -> encode -> staging -> mover -> host arena
H2D  host arena -> mover -> staging -> decode -> device BF16
```

That is 1.78x L2 capacity for two device staging buffers and an encode/decode per direction. If the codec cost dominates on some workload, a fused kernel or a mover-side adapter is the fix, and I would rather hear that now than after merge.

## Modifications

New: `pool_host/int8_codec.py` (pure tensor logic, no SGLang imports), `pool_host/int8_staging.py` (the staging buffers), `pool_host/mha_int8.py` (`MHATokenToKVPoolHostINT8`), plus unit tests.

`pool_host/mha.py`: 7 lines of dispatch in `get_mha_host_pool_cls`. MXFP8 and asymmetric pools keep precedence, since neither is representable in this record.

`environ.py` and the env-var docs: two flags.

One 1152-byte record per `(layer, K|V, token)`: 1024 B INT8 payload, 8 BF16 per-head scales, 112 B padding. `1152 = 9 x 128` because the JIT mover needs `element_size % 128 == 0`. Per-head absmax, scale computed in float32 so the BF16 quotient is exact, and the scale can never be zero or subnormal (an all-zero head would otherwise become NaN).

Off by default behind `SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_HICACHE_INT8`. The pool rejects at startup, by name, the geometries the fixed record cannot express: non-BF16/FP16 device pools, `head_dim != v_head_dim`, `head_num * head_dim != 1024` (a TP other than 1 on an 8-KV-head model), layer-sharded pools, `page_size != 1`, `io_backend != kernel`, and layouts other than `layer_first`.

## Accuracy

The error bound `|x_hat - x| <= (0.5 + 2**-8) * s + 2**-8 * |x_hat|` is asserted elementwise against adversarial inputs on CPU, CUDA and MPS, with zero violations.

The restore path runs in practice: the Experiment B runs below restored 167,899 tokens (INT8) and 126,997 (BF16) out of L2 while serving real requests.

**Not measured:** the same prompts generated from BF16 L2 and from INT8 L2, compared token by token. My harness could not arrange for a prompt to be demoted into L2 and still resident when re-sent, so it reported no number rather than a misleading one. Guidance on exercising L2 restores deterministically in a test would be welcome.

## Speed

`Qwen3-8B`, TP=1, host tier 8 GB, four paired runs, SGLang's own benchmark client, equal host bytes per pair.

| | BF16 L2 | INT8 L2 |
|---|---|---|
| L2 capacity | 54,254 tokens | 96,451 tokens |
| Cache hit | 56.8 - 57.6% | 72.7 - 73.4% |
| TTFT | 1,193 - 2,558 ms | 1,202 - 1,259 ms |
| Throughput | 80.0 - 105.1 tok/s | 127.8 tok/s |

Hit rate is stable across all four runs. TTFT is not: three pairs showed a large win, one **+6%**, so the range is quoted rather than a single run. The reproducible claim is that the INT8 tier is the predictable one.

## Verification

On one RTX A6000 (sm_86), against this change:

```
INT8 codec unit tests (no GPU)    25 passed
INT8 host pool tests (GPU)        36 passed
```

The pool tests run the JIT mover at `element_size = 1152`, pin the encoded arena with `cudaHostRegister`, exercise the all-layer D2H with a per-layer pointer table, and decode back through H2D.

- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format`
- [x] Unit tests added, registered for CUDA and AMD CI
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Speed benchmarks
- [ ] Accuracy, per the section above

No existing flag changes. With the flag unset the dispatch falls through to the existing class.

## Possible interaction

#40608 is a draft reworking host-pool assembly around `host_pool_decls()`. It does not touch `get_mha_host_pool_cls` and the two rebase cleanly today, but if that mechanism is meant to subsume per-class dispatch, this should become a declaration rather than a dispatch branch. Happy to reshape it once that design settles.

title: dsv4.1-amd: fused mHC boundary and all-reduce + mHC post kernels
body:
> This PR was "stack 4/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the fourth kernel PR; #41018 has merged, and it does not depend on #41019 or #41020. The model wiring moved to the integration PR, #41308.

## Summary
- `ops/layernorm/mhc_boundary_hip.py`: the fused mHC sublayer boundary for ROCm. One launch applies the pending `hc_post` onto the residual, collapses it with the previous `pre` and takes the split-K mixing statistics. The reduce + Sinkhorn stays pending in `HcCoefficients`, and `rmsnorm_with_sinkhorn` runs it in the same launch as the next RMSNorm (optionally with the gfx950 fp8-grid fake quant). A row's result does not depend on M, so it is batch invariant like main's mHC.
- `jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/mhc_boundary_gfx95.cuh`: the prefill regime (M >= 1024) of that boundary on gfx950, with LDS DMA and `v_permlane*_swap`. It follows the Triton kernel's operation order, so each row is bitwise equal in both regimes.
- `ops/communication/all_reduce_mhc_hip.py` + `jit/csrc/distributed/all_reduce_mhc_hip.cu`: a TP4 all-reduce fused with `hc_post` for 1-8 rows of hidden size 5120, on aiter's `CustomAllreduce` peer buffers. aiter's `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_one_stage` has the same math, but it rejects hidden sizes above 4096 in bf16 (512 packs), so it cannot serve V4.1's 5120. The module builds through aiter's `compile_ops` because it uses aiter's `CustomAllreduce` object. It is compiled with `-ffp-contract=off`, so it is bitwise equal to the unfused all-reduce followed by `hc_post`.
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, HIP only: `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` uses `ieee` dot precision (CDNA has no TF32) and one row tile at every M, and reduces through the boundary's reduce + Sinkhorn row. CUDA is unchanged.

## Verification
- New tests: `test_hc_boundary_hip.py` covers the boundary forms against torch and fp64, batch invariance of the boundary and of HIP `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`, the hosted norm against the standalone launches (fp8-grid, MXFP8 and no fake quant), and the gfx950 prefill kernel bitwise to the Triton kernel on full and partial row blocks. `test_mhc_kernels.py` gains the CUDA check of `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn` (fp64 reference and batch invariance).
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): these tests pass on `main` + this PR.
- The fused all-reduce is tested by #41308's four-GPU `test_dsv41_tp4_hip.py`: it compares eager (registered-buffer copy-in) and graph-replay outputs of the fused and unfused handoff; all 10 cases pass.
- With #41308's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 / EP4 with DSpark scores 0.905 on GSM8K (200 questions) and serves random 4K/1K at 521 / 1,840 / 3,307 tok/s at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32; see #41308.
- [ ] Pending on a CUDA runner: `test_mhc_kernels.py::test_hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_matches_fp64_and_is_batch_invariant`.

## Stack
- Base: `main`. Independent of #41019 (KV cache layouts, FP4 indexer, compressor and router kernels) and #41020 (gfx950 sparse decode attention and sorted top-k).

title: [Simulator] Support simulating multi-turn conversations and session radix cache
body:
## Summary

Previously the simulator could not run multi-turn workloads at all -- the benchmark adapter accepted only `--backend sglang` while multi-turn replay is gated to chat backends -- so `--enable-session-radix-cache`, which only has an effect under multi-turn traffic, could not be simulated.

Now with this PR the simulator supports `--enable-session-radix-cache` on multi-turn chat workloads with one radix-native session per conversation, reports KV eviction, fixes the defects that let host wall-clock and unsimulated requests leak into its results, and has been validated against a real GPU server on the same workload.

## Results

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, B200, `SILICON` predictor, `page_size 64`. Simulator: 3 runs. Real server: 6 runs, 3 on each of two B200s whose clocks were logged throughout (SM held 1962-1965 MHz, no thermal throttling). Both sides run exactly the commands under Reproducing, with no extra instrumentation. Every difference should be read against the repeat-run spread, because a gap smaller than a run's own variance says nothing. `total_output_tokens` is identical for both, confirming both ran the same work.

### Cache Simulation Results

Same 32 x 10-turn workload in both; only the KV pool changes. The working set is ~93k tokens.

| KV pool | oversubscription | evicted tokens | duration vs real | cache vs real |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 131072 | 0.7x | 0 | +0.2% | -3.3% |
| 65536 | 1.4x | 23,573 | -1.0% | -3.3% |

Beyond roughly 2x oversubscription the cache thrashes and this no longer holds; see Known limitations.

### TTFT/ITL Simulation Results


**KV pool 131072 (0.7x oversubscribed, no eviction)**

| metric | simulated | real | diff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| duration (s) | 6.83 | 6.81 | +0.2% |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 2120.4 | 2124.9 | -0.2% |
| request throughput (req/s) | 46.86 | 46.96 | -0.2% |
| mean TTFT (ms) | 270.6 | 289.2 | -6.4% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 290.5 | 310.7 | -6.5% |
| p95 TTFT (ms) | 358.0 | 372.9 | -4.0% |
| p99 TTFT (ms) | 460.0 | 417.9 | +10.1% |
| mean ITL (ms) | 6.88 | 6.88 | +0.1% |
| median ITL (ms) | 4.77 | 5.23 | -8.8% |
| p95 ITL (ms) | 14.67 | 13.23 | +10.9% |
| p99 ITL (ms) | 17.87 | 15.40 | +16.0% |
| mean TPOT (ms) | 6.89 | 6.88 | +0.2% |
| median TPOT (ms) | 7.02 | 6.98 | +0.5% |
| mean e2e latency (ms) | 575.2 | 593.5 | -3.1% |
| median e2e latency (ms) | 587.5 | 608.6 | -3.5% |
| p95 e2e latency (ms) | 754.7 | 768.9 | -1.8% |
| p99 e2e latency (ms) | 827.0 | 816.6 | +1.3% |
| cache hit tokens | 418,496 | 432,917 | -3.3% |

**KV pool 65536 (1.4x oversubscribed, 23.5k tokens evicted)**

| metric | simulated | real | diff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| duration (s) | 6.76 | 6.83 | -1.0% |
| output throughput (tok/s) | 2141.9 | 2120.8 | +1.0% |
| request throughput (req/s) | 47.33 | 46.87 | +1.0% |
| mean TTFT (ms) | 260.4 | 289.0 | -9.9% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 283.4 | 311.1 | -8.9% |
| p95 TTFT (ms) | 334.4 | 367.4 | -9.0% |
| p99 TTFT (ms) | 426.4 | 425.7 | +0.2% |
| mean ITL (ms) | 6.83 | 6.88 | -0.8% |
| median ITL (ms) | 4.79 | 5.21 | -8.0% |
| p95 ITL (ms) | 14.08 | 13.16 | +7.0% |
| p99 ITL (ms) | 17.37 | 15.12 | +14.9% |
| mean TPOT (ms) | 6.83 | 6.88 | -0.7% |
| median TPOT (ms) | 6.93 | 6.97 | -0.6% |
| mean e2e latency (ms) | 562.5 | 593.5 | -5.2% |
| median e2e latency (ms) | 578.2 | 609.5 | -5.1% |
| p95 e2e latency (ms) | 737.7 | 766.6 | -3.8% |
| p99 e2e latency (ms) | 770.0 | 814.1 | -5.4% |
| cache hit tokens | 418,496 | 432,672 | -3.3% |

Duration, throughput, mean ITL and TPOT agree within ~1%. Mean and median TTFT are 6-10% optimistic and e2e latency 1-5%. Cache hit volume is 3.3% low. The only metrics outside 10% are tails (p99 TTFT at 0.7x, p95/p99 ITL), which sit within or near their own repeat-run spread of up to ~23%.

`concurrency` is not an independent measurement -- it is `sum(e2e_latencies) / duration`, so it is implied by the two rows above it rather than explaining them. Its small spread is an artifact of being a ratio of covarying quantities.

Cache totals are identical across simulator repeat runs (0.2% spread on the real server). Per-request cache agreement against the real server is ~41% in both configurations, against 99.5% between real repeat runs, so totals agree to 3.3% while *which* requests hit differs systematically. Part of it is first turns: OFFLINE mode releases all simultaneous arrivals in one prefill batch, while real HTTP arrivals stagger and let later same-group first turns reuse an earlier system prompt. The rest is unexplained.

### Known limitations

- **Cache thrashing.** Past ~2x KV oversubscription the numbers above no longer hold: duration drops to -34.5% at 2.8x (329k tokens evicted) and -34.3% at 5.7x (408k evicted). The error switches on between 1.4x and 2.8x and then saturates rather than scaling with eviction volume, and the real server destabilises at the same threshold (repeat-run spread 14.6% -> 31.7%), so the -34% figures sit against a very noisy reference. Cache volume stays within ~5% throughout; only latency collapses. Those two duration figures predate the warm-up fix below, so they understate the gap by roughly 5 points. Mechanism unidentified.
- TTFT is 6-10% optimistic. A debug run with per-iteration GPU timing points at prefill: `aiconfigurator`'s SILICON context attention scales a prefix-0 measurement by the FLOP ratio, which under-predicts short prefills over a long cached prefix (the common multi-turn shape) by ~15%. Tail ITL is not reliable.
- Validated on one model, one accelerator, `--request-rate inf`. No MoE, no long context beyond ~2.6k tokens, no paced arrivals.
- The simulator can only model `disable_overlap_schedule=True`; `compat.py` force-overrides it. Real deployments default to overlap enabled, so these numbers describe a configuration production does not run.
- Close ordering (`simulation/sglang/session_timeline.py`) holds a session's close until that session's turns have finished on the simulated clock. It only engages when a close reaches the simulator before its turns have run, e.g. pre-timestamped traces with pipelined closes. The multi-turn benchmark closes a session after its last round returns, so the results above do not exercise it; it is covered by unit tests only.
- `evicted_tokens` / `evict_calls` are counted on `UnifiedRadixCache`, the default tree cache. Other cache implementations report 0.
- The simulated sampler emits a filler token chosen at startup (`resolve_filler_token_id`); a tokenizer with no repetition-stable single-token probe word fails startup rather than silently shortening multi-turn history. The probe is skipped under `--skip-tokenizer-init`, where outputs are never re-tokenized.

## Reproducing

`sim_config.json`:

```json
{
  "platform": {
    "accelerator": {"name": "b200_sxm", "hbm_capacity_gb": 180},
    "disk_read_bandwidth_gb": 8, "disk_write_bandwidth_gb": 8,
    "memory_read_bandwidth_gb": 64, "memory_write_bandwidth_gb": 64,
    "num_device_per_node": 8
  },
  "predictor": {"name": "aiconfigurator", "database_mode": "SILICON"},
  "scheduler": {
    "tp_size": 1, "ep_size": 1, "dp_size": 1,
    "backend_name": "sglang", "backend_version": "0.5.10",
    "quantization": "bf16"
  }
}
```

Use `SILICON`, not `SOL`. `SOL` is Speed Of Light -- theoretical peak, a lower bound on latency by construction. It is also not the code's default; a config setting it is overriding `time_predictor/aiconfigurator.py`.

Simulator:

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1
export SGLANG_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE=OFFLINE SGLANG_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/sim-out

python -m sglang_simulator.simulation.sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path $MODEL --tokenizer-path $MODEL --load-format dummy \
  --sim-config-path sim_config.json --port 30000 \
  --max-total-tokens 131072 --max-running-requests 16 \
  --page-size 64 --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --enable-session-radix-cache --enable-cache-report

python benchmark/simulator/bench_serving.py \
  --simulator-mode=offline --backend=sglang-oai-chat \
  --base-url=http://127.0.0.1:30000 --model=$MODEL --tokenizer=$MODEL \
  --dataset-name=generated-shared-prefix \
  --gsp-num-groups 8 --gsp-prompts-per-group 4 \
  --gsp-system-prompt-len 512 --gsp-question-len 256 --gsp-output-len 64 \
  --gsp-num-turns 10 --gsp-ordered --gsp-range-ratio 0.3 \
  --gsp-group-distribution zipf --gsp-zipf-alpha 1.2 \
  --num-prompts 32 --request-rate inf --disable-tqdm --seed 42 \
  --cache-report --output-details \
  --simulator-session-per-conversation \
  --output-file=/tmp/sim-out/bench.jsonl
```

Real server, same workload:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path $MODEL --tokenizer-path $MODEL --load-format dummy --port 30001 \
  --max-total-tokens 131072 --max-running-requests 16 \
  --page-size 64 --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --enable-session-radix-cache --enable-cache-report
```

driven by the same client arguments minus `--simulator-mode` and `--simulator-session-per-conversation`, plus `--warmup-requests 0`. Each conversation must also carry its own `session_id` and be closed with `/close_session` after its last round, as the simulator adapter does, so both servers receive identical traffic.

Use `--max-total-tokens 65536` on both servers for the 1.4x table. The real client passes `--warmup-requests 0` because the simulator adapter forces it; otherwise the real server starts with conversation 0 already cached.

## Bugs fixed

- **Multi-turn history halved** (`simulation/sglang/model_runner.py:85`) -- the mocked sampler emitted a token that BPE-merges with itself, so each answer fed back as history re-tokenized to half its length. Latent before this PR: multi-turn was unreachable.
- **A Unix epoch could replace the simulated clock** (`simulation/sglang/scheduler.py:611`) -- `cpu_overhead` differenced against an uninitialised reference, so `duration` read ~1.79e9 s. Intermittent, triggered by the server's own warm-up request.
- **The request-ingest window was charged as scheduler CPU** (`simulation/sglang/scheduler.py:229`) -- 7.2-7.9 s of idle client send time per run, landing at t=0 when every request is queued. p95 TTFT +213% -> -43%.
- **The simulator charged its own predictor cost to the simulated clock** (`simulation/sglang/scheduler.py`, both modes) -- 77-80% of all charged CPU overhead was the simulator's own lookups. Single-turn duration error +23.2% -> +6.9%, and cache totals became identical across repeat runs where no eviction occurs; timings still carry host wall-clock through `cpu_overhead`.
- **The server's warm-up request was reported as a benchmark request** (`simulation/sglang/scheduler.py:661`, flag on `simulation/types.py:RequestStats`) -- it carries no simulation metadata, so its record keeps the `created_time = -1` default, which became the normalisation origin and shifted every real request by exactly 1.0 s. `duration` therefore carried 1.0 s of dead time, ~13% of a 7.9 s run.
- **Batched generate requests crashed the OFFLINE dispatcher** (`simulation/sglang/scheduler.py:187`) -- it read `sampling_params` off the `BatchTokenizedGenerateReqInput` container, which has none. Each turn in a batch is now queued individually with its own arrival time.
- **KV eviction was invisible** (`simulation/sglang/unified_radix_cache.py:39`) -- `evicted_tokens` and `evict_calls` are now accumulated and reported; without them a hit ratio cannot be interpreted.

title: [CI] Real-model Kimi-Linear PD parity at page, DCP virtual-page, chunk and cached-prefix boundaries
body:
Follow-up to #41321: moves Kimi-Linear PD boundary parity onto the real `moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` checkpoint, in deterministic mode.

- `PDLogprobParityMixin`: configurable prompt list, output length, logprob delta, and an optional cached-prefix resend (flush decode only, so prefill serves the prompt from radix). Defaults are unchanged for the unified-memory users.
- `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py`: 11 prompts at the 16-token page, 32-token DCP virtual-page and 64-token chunk edges, 8 output tokens, exact tokens + logprob delta 1e-3, on two layouts:
  - P TP2 -> D TP2 (fa3), with the cached-prefix pass (radix hits of 64/128/256 tokens)
  - P TP2 -> D TP2/DCP2 (new), deterministic flashinfer, page 16, chunk 64 (triton has no DCP MLA write path; radix is off there)
- Drops the heterogeneous-TP (TP2 -> TP1) and PP arms: those layouts have no bit-exact monolithic reference, so exact-token parity isn't a valid oracle for them. A tolerance-based heterogeneous-TP check is the planned nightly follow-up. cc @YAMY1234
- Moves the test to `extra-b` (est 400 s).

Validated with `/rerun-test` on 4-gpu-h100: 4 passes of `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` on 4ed812dc11 (~5-6 min each), and `test_disaggregation_unified_memory_{swa,tri}.py` pass with the kit change; `test_disaggregation_unified_memory.py` passes on 4xH200.

title: fuse shared experts with routed experts in MegaMoE's DeepGEMM
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
wip for #38700 (* - *)

## Motivation
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Context: Deepseek-v4-pro uses DeepseekMoE (served as MegaMoE) as its mixure of experts with a shared expert that is activated across all tokens and a fine-grained routed experts. 
- flash model: 1 shared + 256 routed
- pro model: 1 shared + 384 routed 
>Note that the authors also chose to use FP4 with QAT such that routed expert weights are in MXFP4 while all other parameters (including the shared expert in the official checkpoints) stay in blockwise fp8 format. 

For each token $t_i$ , a V4 MoE layer does two different GEMM operations:
1. shared - dense MLP on every token (in FP8)
2. routed - grouped GEMM over the top 6 selected experts (MXFP4)

Launching each kernel independently wastes launches and stream syncs on every layer (this is true even if they shared a dtype). DeepGEMM already caught this and added native MegaMoE support via (num_shared_experts, separate shared_l1/shared_l2 weights, mixed FP8 and MXFP4).

The existing Sglang fusion logic in `deepseek-v2.py` 
```python
        # num_fused_shared_experts drives weight remapping in deepseek_weight_loader:
        # mlp.shared_experts → mlp.experts.256 when > 0.
        self.num_fused_shared_experts = 0 if _fusion_disabled else n_shared_experts
```
only works if shared and routed share a dtype/layout (from `deepseel-v4.py`):
```python 
        # Need to disable if quant precision mismatch, even if
        # --enforce-shared-experts-fusion is specified
        if quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config):
            return (
                "Quantization keeps shared experts at a higher precision than the "
                "routed experts, so they cannot be fused into the quantized "
                "routed-expert path."
            )
```
but the official deepseek-ai checkpoints do not, so that path does not apply on MegaMoE (it can still run on the trtllm-gen runner if you `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` and requantize shared FP8→MXFP4, which is what #35505 did)

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

Changes mainly in mega_moe.py: 
This PR went through a lot of iterations, starting with a naive index implementation that was supposed to be easier to maintain and more local w.r.t. number of files changed. The memory and throughput overhead of maintaining a python cache of expert indices was pretty bad (as seen below) which motivated for a kernel level change in `mega_moe_predispatch.cuh`. 

Placing the FP8 shared expert inside routed MegaMoE (removing six standalone kernels per layer) does this but it regressed throughput because it bypassed the existing alternate-stream fork in `mega_moe.py`. In the unfused profiles, the shared expert’s second GEMM overlapped with the routed MegaMoE in 184/184 observed calls per rank, covering a median 94.1–95.6% of its duration. Naively fusing the path without modifying `forward_mega_moe()` function returned before the existing alternate-stream fork, leaving the whole router/top-k/pre-dispatch/MegaMoE region on the current stream...

```python
  if moe.mega_shared_l1_weights is not None:
          return _run_mega_routed(
              moe, hidden_states, forward_batch, input_ids_global, num_tokens
          )
  
      sbo_overlap_flag = (
          moe.alt_stream is not None
          and moe.num_fused_shared_experts == 0
          and num_tokens > 0
          and get_is_capture_mode()
      )
```

The current iteration of this PR keeps the same kernel changes but forks the whole fused region in `forward_mega_moe()` which lets other graph work overlap it; at BS1, main, kernel-only, and kernel-plus-fork achieved 756.90, 721.97, and 759.08 tok/s.

Major files changes:
1. `_get_mega_moe_symm_buffer` includes `num_shared_experts` in its cache key and allocates the shared-expert buffer for the fused configuration
2. `_run_mega_routed` forwards the shared-expert count and transformed L1/L2 weights through gate and top-k to `run_mega_routed_experts`
3. `run_mega_routed_experts` selects the consuming MegaMoE `BLOCK_M`, passes the shared-scale destination to pre-dispatch, and launches `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` with the shared weights
4. `forward_mega_moe` forks the entire fused router/top-k/pre-dispatch/MegaMoE region onto the existing alternate stream during CUDA-graph capture and joins before returning

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Accuracy evals are run on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with the bundled DSpark draft via 4x B300 (SM103) with sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7. On GPTQA-diamond with sgl-eval and thinking enabled, reasoning effort `max`, `max_tokens=200000`, and
`top_p=0.95`: 

| Workload | n | main | fusion index (no kernel) | fusion kernel | fusion kernel + fork (PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Greedy accuracy | 198 | 0.899 | 0.894 | 0.883 | 0.897 |
| Greedy empty at cap | 198 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 8 |
| Sampled pass@1 | 792 | 0.900 | 0.922 | 0.910 | 0.910 |
| Parsing failure | 792 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Request failures | - | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

paired per-request comparison:

| Workload | Pair | Answer flips | main right, arm wrong | arm right, main wrong | One-sided empty answers |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Greedy | main vs fusion index | 14 | 2 | 8 | 6 |
| Greedy | main vs fusion kernel | 17 | 5 | 7 | 8 |
| Greedy | main vs fusion kernel + fork | 22 | 5 | 11 | 10 |
| Sampled | main vs fusion index | 50 | 11 | 28 | 0 |
| Sampled | main vs fusion kernel | 55 | 19 | 27 | 0 |
| Sampled | main vs fusion kernel + fork (PR) | 58 | 19 | 27 | 0 |
>All request errors are empty answers truncated at 200k tokens. No request failed
 

## Speed Tests and Profiling
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.7 on 4xB300
- Workload: 1,024 input tokens, 256 requested output tokens, batch sizes 1, 8, 32, and 64
- DSpark performance uses `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=6` while regular inference omits `--speculative-algorithm` 

### DSpark

| 1 | 756.90 | 701.62 | 721.97 | 759.08 |

| 8 | 96,307.46 | 70,973.86 | 102,971.41 | 107,059.48 |

title: fix(benchmark): avoid caching partial Mooncake downloads
body:
## Motivation

`download_and_cache_file()` wrote streamed responses directly to the final cache path. If a Mooncake trace download failed after partial data had been written, the partial file remained and was treated as a cached dataset on the next load.

Fixes #41244

## Modifications

- Download into a same-directory `.part` file.
- Publish the final cache path with `os.replace()` only after the response is fully written.
- Remove the temporary file when the download fails and preserve any existing final file.
- Add CPU-only regression tests for interrupted downloads, successful downloads, and existing-file preservation.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change does not affect model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This change does not affect inference execution.

title: [DSA] Make the fused top-k exact on an overflowing threshold bin
body:
## Motivation

The coarse histogram bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so one bin spans a quarter-binade. The collect pass stores at most 2048 threshold-bin candidates; when the bin is larger, `handle_tie` ranks whichever arrived first and silently returns a wrong top-k set.

Found while profiling GLM-5.2 decode on MI355X: ~0.04% of rows entered this path across all 8 ranks, with a largest observed bin of 4139 against the 2048 cap and none of those rows bit-identical. #35257 reports the same defect independently from the CUDA side — referenced, not closed.

## Modifications

When the threshold bin overflows, narrow it with three exact-key radix rounds (12 / 12 / 8 bits), then make one final input scan to emit candidates above the selected bucket and re-stage the bucket for the existing tie handler. The refinement histogram overlays the dead arrival-order buffer, so LDS is unchanged.

The cold scan uses a separate reversed-lane load path. This keeps its load-address state out of the fast path's registers and restores most of the CUDA regression reported in review.

Replace the fp16-bin boundary conversion with exact fp32 bounds. In particular, when a bin's high edge is `+0.0`, the boundary advances to the smallest positive subnormal so `-0.0` cannot be misclassified as above the bin.

The fast path only adds the overflow comparison. The ROCm `__launch_bounds__` argument also states the physical floor of 4 waves/SIMD; the CUDA spelling is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The exactness test is ROCm-only because CUDA may route these shapes to the still-unrefined cluster path. It covers register and streaming shapes with six distributions, including adjacent fp32 values and the `+0.0/-0.0` boundary.

| suite | result before the fix |
|---|---|
| 300 pre-existing cases | 300 passed |
| 10 overflowing non-identical cases | 10 failed |
| 2 `all_equal` controls | 2 passed |

The signed-zero cases also fail on the pre-review refinement and pass with the new boundary conversion. All 312 cases pass with this change.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), five paired runs per arm on one GPU, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.430 µs | 5.338 µs | −1.7% |
| `randn` (hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.270 µs | 12.188 µs | −0.7% |
| `narrow_bin` | 6×8192 | 16.821 µs | 20.937 µs | +24.5% |
| `narrow_bin` | 4×32768 | 29.652 µs | 50.030 µs | +68.7% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 6×8192 | 11.487 µs | 34.862 µs | +203.5% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 4×32768 | 36.314 µs | 117.756 µs | +224.3% |

The cold-path delta is the cost of exact work that main skips by returning a wrong answer. It is entered on ~0.04% of rows in the serving traffic above. Against the previous PR implementation, the new scan is 2.6–5.3% faster on `narrow_bin`. On the latest tree, a clean local JIT build is 10.50 s versus 10.02 s on main (+4.8%), rather than the nearly 2× CUDA increase reported before this rewrite.

On gfx950: 63 → 71 VGPRs, zero spills, LDS unchanged at 26928 B. We do not have NVIDIA hardware; CUDA register pressure and B200 performance need CI/reviewer measurement.

## Known gap

The CUDA-only `TopKCluster` path still truncates. Refining there needs cluster-wide histogram and emit counters rather than the block-local ones used here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add exactness tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance results.
- [x] Keep documentation and comments synchronized.

title: Rust server unify datapath for mm and generate requests
body:

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

Every non-scalar payload the embedded Rust server sends to the scheduler
(`input_ids`, `token_ids_logprob`, multimodal features and their per-item
metadata) now crosses the ring and the pyo3 boundary the same way: as a named
`Buffer` beside the msgpack scalar header. An inline buffer hands its Rust
allocation to numpy without a copy; a shm buffer hands over only its segment
name. This replaces two separate mechanisms, the columnar `input_ids` cell and
the rid-keyed multimodal result store, and deletes the store, its purge hooks,
and `take_mm_result`.

Two preparatory changes are included because the buffer work builds on them:
the POSIX shm helper is rewritten on `rustix` and moved to `utils`, and the
request FSM now runs `Tokenizing` before `Encoding` so the MM worker never
tokenizes.

title: [sglang-miles] Recover disk-delta checkpoints safely across resets and retries
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Make disk-delta checkpoints safe to reuse/retry after a trainer reset or interrupted apply, reject incomplete publications, and remove unnecessary host work. An unchanged publication should not scan every checkpoint header; full model loading should not invoke memory diagnostics that only feed disabled DEBUG logs.

This targets `sglang-miles`, which already includes `/pull_weights`; the refreshed base is `571212b636baca45e10fa3b4da11a289123f3235`. Companion Miles draft: https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3711. Existing NVFP4 W4A16 disk reload/postprocessing is reused; this adds no quantization kernel or wire-format change.

## Modifications

- **Reset/retry:** explicit `pull(0)` reseeds a reused directory; stale positive pulls remain no-ops. Invalidate the applied marker before byte mutation so a failed copy/XOR apply reseeds before retry. Callers serialize startup resets before positive pulls; independent streams cannot share the same local checkpoint.
- **Publication:** validate each delta index's shard/tensor mapping before byte mutation, then verify reconstructed tensor checksums during apply. Reject indexless sharded/empty publications; preserve indexed full checkpoints and the standard unindexed single `model.safetensors` layout.
- **Empty versions:** preserve lineage, compression/encoding, and required metadata validation, then atomically advance the marker without tensor-header scans or byte-mutation setup. A failed marker replacement retains the previous valid version.
- **Loader diagnostics:** gate the two before/after GPU memory probes on DEBUG logging, avoiding their default allocator-cache eviction when the messages are disabled. Actual loading and explicit online-quantization synchronization/cache cleanup are unchanged.
- **Compatibility/scope:** companion Miles scalar staging keeps the existing per-name wire payload and checksum rules and needs no additional receiver format handling. No receiver worker batching, persistent header cache, automatic retry/rollback, selective tensor reload, or no-op GPU reload bypass. The state marker describes the materialized disk checkpoint, not active GPU weights.

## Accuracy Tests

- **CI gates:** this PR remains a draft. The inherited maintenance check also requires main commit `3fc7a669bfe3`, which is not an ancestor of the target `sglang-miles` commit `571212b636baca45e10fa3b4da11a289123f3235`. The PR is rebased and conflict-free against its selected target; this is not a claim of green upstream CI.

Exactly three feature commits; no conflicts. Range-diff reports `=` for every patch, and all four touched source/test files are byte-identical to the prior head.
- **Scope:** audited explicit reset/reseed, marker invalidation before byte mutation, fail-closed delta publication handling, empty-version marker replacement, and DEBUG-only memory diagnostics. Retained the existing behavioral tests without adding duplicate harnesses. No additional runtime change.
- **Local CPU environment:** macOS 26.4.1 arm64, Python 3.12.12, pytest 9.1.1, numpy 2.5.3, safetensors 0.8.0, xxhash 4.0.1, zstandard 0.25.0. Used an existing environment read-only. This is CPU filesystem validation, not GPU/runtime requalification.

### Historical C2 validation

The following CPU/CI and GPU experiment records were collected at their named pre-rebase commits. They were not rerun for the refreshed head.

At SGLang `2f5fb2a09f08eb9a44c0fed5a28be0bda2942b0f`, receiver and loader CPU tests passed with normal collection in the pinned C2 image:

- **Coverage:** packed U8 weights, FP8 scales, scalar FP32 scales, XOR/overwrite, empty/repeated/stale pulls, explicit stream reset, incomplete publications, checksum/copy failure, and explicit retry. Empty-map tests retain metadata checks and atomic marker failure behavior. Mocked loader subcases cover DEBUG on/off and online quantization on/off, preserving the explicit online cleanup.
- **Hosted CI at this head:** [lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192432601/job/108260452754). [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192433017/job/108260456146) and [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192433274/job/108260455995) gates require main commit `3fc7a669bfe3` and report this `sglang-miles` PR as `diverged`. [AMD](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192433191/job/108260455161), [AMD Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192432810/job/108260453767), and [NPU](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36192433397/job/108260523968) gates report `PR is draft. Blocking CI.` These are pre-test gates; hosted GPU tests were skipped. Final candidate C2 training/CPU evidence is complete below.
- **Limits:** the state marker covers disk materialization, not active GPU weights. CPU reconstruction and checksum checks do not prove GPU byte equality or learning parity. Missing expected per-tensor checksums fail verification; checksum algorithms and XOR/overwrite semantics remain unchanged. Full-checkpoint cryptographic integrity, concurrent independent streams, automatic retry, and selective/no-op GPU reload are outside scope.

<!-- Evidence bundle: artifacts/receiver-cpu-candidate-final.log and artifacts/sglang-ci-candidate-2f5fb2a-* logs/status/reason JSONs. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Historical evidence:** all commands, raw outputs, numerical tables, and source qualifications below are preserved from the original campaign. No fresh GPU run or performance claim accompanies this rebase.

### Environment and source pins

- **Hardware/image:** one C2 node, 8 × B300 SXM6 AC; 4 trainer GPUs (TP4/EP4, PP1/CP1/ETP1) + two rollout engines (TP2/DP2/EP2 each). `radixark/miles:dev-202609251434`, amd64 digest `sha256:7c4c6c8cc9e76be893941e064f0e43924ef9258b04da365c8009709592ff0984`.
- **Stack:** Python 3.12.3, driver 590.48.01, CUDA toolkit 13.0.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformer Engine 2.17.0, FlashInfer Python/cubin 0.6.18, CuTe DSL 4.6.2, Triton 3.7.1, Ray 2.58.0. Megatron `f148a32b4385b758b66a77c9c3ad1641f1295d4b`.
- **Final candidate sources:** Miles `f17ba4bce13bf7d357e7560182dc859c41a7cb37` / SGLang `2f5fb2a09f08eb9a44c0fed5a28be0bda2942b0f`. The candidate three-arm CPU/wall campaign completed and passed the strict report checks. The completed original baseline uses the earlier commits listed below.
- **Model:** `Pinaster/GLM-5.2_5layer` at `1c749139f70e158e4420ba67f342bef1de2e650d`, converted once with the public NVFP4/torch-dist converters; shared experts remain BF16 and all other native precision settings are retained.
- **Dataset:** `zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k` at `2e65612930298bde4c5d58fd97b3f23a483aaff9`; `dapo-math-17k.jsonl`, 10,490,834 bytes, SHA256 `cc9c39c2aa19177abe9464741e121cf4cac90fd25484ef3cdf86535101e3a5b6`.
- **Workload:** seven synchronous rollouts, 8 prompts × 8 samples, response limit 100, temperature 1, GRPO, LR 1e-6, trainer/rollout seeds 1234/42. Native deepscaler and explicitly synthetic balanced rewards are separate workloads. Existing disabled logprob/KL/weight-equality CI checkers remain disabled; their pass is not claimed.

### Measured sender worker replay — component only

On C2 `hu-pdx-90` in `radixark/miles:dev-202609251434`, replayed the exact `_diff_and_compress` methods from Miles `81d43908021deaf916808675d7ac78e4fbccfa2f` and `f17ba4bce13bf7d357e7560182dc859c41a7cb37`. One warmed 32-thread pool processed 4,690 sender tensors totaling **17,900,804,608 bytes**, using XOR/zstd/`xxh3-128`. Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NumPy 2.3.5, zstandard 0.25.0, xxhash 3.7.1; recorded CPU affinity was `0–1,11–129,138–255` on `hu-pdx-90`.

This isolates the **deferred snapshot-copy worker change**. Regular CPU tensors stand in for completed D2H buffers; no GPU/DMA, actual pinned pool/backpressure, gathering, scalar batching, publication, receiver apply, or reload is measured. Submission/drain, worker allocations, diff/count, snapshot copy, compression, checksum, and queue return are timed. Input preparation, pool creation, verification, and result disposal are outside timing. Process CPU counts all threads in this one process, not four trainer ranks.

Two warmup pairs precede five measured pairs; B→C/C→B order alternates. All **28 samples** passed full snapshot/decode/checksum/count verification, including unchanged old inputs. The unchanged case uses identical canonical bytes. The changed case reconstructs the published synthetic v1→v2 states: **79,500,803 changed bytes**, but only **465,303,040 bytes (2.5993%)** belong to wholly unchanged tensors. Its compressed worker payload is **182,769,068 bytes** for both implementations; this excludes safetensors headers/index and is distinct from the end-to-end shard-byte counter.

| Case | Baseline CPU median s | Candidate CPU median s | CPU change | Baseline wall median s | Candidate wall median s | Wall change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unchanged canonical | 26.897635228 | 16.222345924 | -39.69% | 1.847023436 | 1.136617184 | -38.46% |
| Synthetic v1→v2 | 37.302611630 | 38.633915017 | +3.57% | 3.640603384 | 3.750314473 | +3.01% |

The unchanged case benefits; the changed case regresses **3.57% CPU / 3.01% wall** in this replay. Avoiding whole-tensor snapshot copies has limited opportunity when only 2.5993% of tensor bytes are in entirely unchanged tensors. These component measurements establish neither an end-to-end CPU improvement nor GPU weight equality.

- **Boundaries:** driver await and builtin actor wall include nested observer work. Trainer all-thread CPU sums four updater windows; receiver process clocks bracket rank-0 updater and include inventoried controllers/compile workers. Driver CPU is separate. These windows are not an exact simultaneous whole-host total.
- **Overhead:** membership refresh and journal flush are outside trainer wall/CPU but inside driver wall; receiver snapshots are outside trainer CPU and inside trainer wall. No estimated cost is subtracted. Flush timing is lagged and the final flush has no later measurement. Other ranks can incur observer-induced synchronization delay.
- **Coverage:** before/after membership checks are non-atomic. Entirely transient or newly born children omitted during concurrent exits may remain unobserved. Receiver source is verified through configured launch/PYTHONPATH, without independent loaded-module attestation. Container CPU quota files may be unavailable; observed affinity/cgroup/thread settings are retained and matched.
- **Meaning:** wire bytes are compressed serialized shards, excluding index JSON and startup checkpoint copy; broadcast byte counters are unavailable, not zero. Checksums, acknowledgements, replay and successful training do not prove active GPU byte equality or learning equivalence. Synthetic balanced reward is an explicit transport workload, not task-quality evidence.

Synthetic arm only: define an explicit balanced reward, then use the unchanged native training recipe with `--custom-rm-path`. This assigns four zeros/four ones to each group of eight consecutive sample indices, uses ordinary GRPO/optimizer updates, and injects no weights or gradients. It is not a math-task accuracy test; require observed nonzero gradients and changed deltas before calling it changed-weight evidence.

```bash
cat > repro_reward.py <<'PYCODE'
def one(sample):
    if sample.index is None or isinstance(sample.index, bool):
        raise ValueError('Expected integer sample.index')
    index = int(sample.index)
    if index != sample.index or index < 0:
        raise ValueError('Invalid sample.index')
    return float(index % 2)
async def balanced(args, sample, **kwargs):
    if args.n_samples_per_prompt <= 0 or args.n_samples_per_prompt % 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected positive even group size')
    return [one(s) for s in sample] if isinstance(sample, list) else one(sample)
PYCODE
test ! -e repro-synthetic-publication
test ! -e repro-synthetic-checkpoint
for mode in broadcast disk-delta; do
  python - "$mode" <<'PYCODE' 2>&1 | tee "repro-logs/synthetic-$mode.log"
import os, sys
from pathlib import Path
from tests.e2e.megatron import test_glm5_2_744b_a40b_5layer_nvfp4_w4a16 as r
for key in ('http_proxy', 'https_proxy', 'HTTP_PROXY', 'HTTPS_PROXY'):
    os.environ.pop(key, None)
execute = r.U.execute_train
def with_reward(**kw):
    kw['train_args'] += ' --custom-rm-path repro_reward.balanced --seed 1234 --rollout-seed 42'
    kw['extra_env_vars'].update(PYTHONPATH=os.environ['PYTHONPATH'], RAY_DEDUP_LOGS='0')
    kw['job_lifetime'] = 'launcher'
    return execute(**kw)
r.U.execute_train = with_reward
r.execute(num_rollout=7, update_weight_transfer_mode=sys.argv[1],
    update_weight_disk_dir=str(Path.cwd()/'repro-synthetic-publication'),
    update_weight_local_checkpoint_dir=str(Path.cwd()/'repro-synthetic-checkpoint'))
PYCODE
done
```

Extract all seven full-precision native actor timings. `perf 0` reports startup; `perf 1..6` reports the preceding six post-training syncs, so `perf 2..6` is steady. These are actor wall seconds, not rounded `Timer` lines, driver wall, or CPU seconds. Timing extraction alone does not validate training completion or changed weights.

```bash
python - repro-logs/native-delta.log repro-logs/synthetic-*.log <<'PYCODE'
import re, statistics, sys
from pathlib import Path
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    values = {}
    for step, value in re.findall(r"perf\s+(\d+):\s+.*?'perf/update_weights_time':\s*([0-9.eE+-]+)", Path(name).read_text()):
        step, value = int(step), float(value)
        assert step not in values or values[step] == value, (name, step)
        values[step] = value
    assert set(values) == set(range(7)), (name, sorted(values))
    print(name, 'raw_actor_seconds', [values[i] for i in range(7)])
    steady = [values[i] for i in range(2, 7)]
    print('steady_n=5 median/min/max', statistics.median(steady), min(steady), max(steady))
PYCODE
```

title: [ROCm] Fuse GLM-5.2 indexer preparation on gfx950
body:
## Summary

- add gfx950 full indexer-prepare kernels for compatible GLM-5.2 DSA decode shapes from M=1 through M=128, including C10 M=10/M=40 graphs
- fuse indexer projections, LayerNorm, RoPE, FP8 quantization, head-gate scaling, and paged index-K cache writes
- use the same no-Hadamard cache representation as current main's AITER fused writer, so per-call fallback cannot mix cache formats within one request
- support 16/32 indexer heads, 1024/2048 query LoRA ranks, BF16/FP32 LayerNorm parameters, and non-default LayerNorm epsilon
- use an async shared-memory projection schedule for validated 32-head M=64/96/128 graphs; route the remaining admitted cases through the generic schedule
- require the current-main fused writer to be available before enabling this path; unsupported modes, layouts, shapes, or runtimes remain on that compatible fallback

## Validation

- rebased onto current main (`a1eb691ab`); PR is mergeable
- combined CPU and MI355X run: 11 tests passed, 36 subtests passed
- correctness and CUDA graph replay cover M=1/2/4/8/10/16/32/40/64/96/128
- generalized coverage includes every admitted 16/32-head and 1024/2048-rank combination at M=10 and M=64
- FP32 and BF16 LayerNorm parameters, non-default epsilon, cross-page cache writes, and negative/padded cache slots are covered
- the existing AITER fused-writer parity tests run alongside the full-prepare tests to validate the shared no-Hadamard cache representation
- performance tests require at least a 10% gain for every decode shape and generalized case; M=64/96/128 also require at least a 20% gain from the large-M schedule
- Ruff, formatting, import ordering, registered-test validation, and diff checks pass

## Kernel performance vs current main

MI355X median latency, measured back-to-back on the same GPU. The baseline is current main's three projections plus its AITER fused FP8 DSA writer.

| M | main (us) | full prepare (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 63.08 | 25.41 | 2.48x |
| 2 | 62.97 | 25.45 | 2.47x |
| 4 | 62.91 | 25.49 | 2.47x |
| 8 | 58.71 | 26.33 | 2.23x |
| 10 | 53.10 | 26.25 | 2.02x |
| 16 | 53.15 | 26.47 | 2.01x |
| 32 | 53.33 | 26.34 | 2.02x |
| 40 | 53.92 | 26.75 | 2.02x |
| 48 | 52.23 | 27.22 | 1.92x |
| 64 | 52.99 | 26.20 | 2.02x |
| 96 | 53.01 | 27.71 | 1.91x |
| 128 | 53.42 | 25.74 | 2.08x |

## TP8/EP1 end-to-end performance vs current main

GLM-5.2-MXFP4 on 8x MI355X, 100k input tokens, 100 output tokens, MTP 5 steps / 6 draft tokens, no HiCache, 3 repeats per point. Both arms were warmed before measurement and used the same server configuration. ITV is measured from client-observed streaming token timestamps.

| Concurrency | main P50 ITV (ms) | full P50 ITV (ms) | P50 change | main P90 ITV (ms) | full P90 ITV (ms) | P90 change | throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.297 | 3.182 | -3.48% | 4.385 | 4.259 | -2.89% | +5.87% |
| 10 | 5.695 | 5.731 | +0.64% | 7.651 | 7.571 | -1.04% | +1.25% |
| 16 | 6.610 | 6.530 | -1.20% | 8.804 | 8.760 | -0.50% | +2.21% |

One GPU also hosted an idle system service, so both arms used the same conservative 0.55 static-memory fraction. The comparison is paired under the same conditions.

## Direct comparison with #38583

The following is a same-host comparison against #38583 commit `ca91c497e`. Both arms used TP8/EP1, 100k input tokens, 100 output tokens, MTP 5/6, no HiCache, `max-running-requests=8`, and `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode=8`. Values are the mean of two hot runs after a full warmup run.

| Concurrency | #38583 P50 ITV (ms) | this PR P50 ITV (ms) | change | #38583 P90 ITV (ms) | this PR P90 ITV (ms) | change | throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.394 | 3.200 | -5.71% | 4.523 | 4.335 | -4.15% | +4.59% |
| 8 | 5.281 | 4.909 | -7.03% | 7.019 | 6.548 | -6.71% | +6.03% |

#38583 replaces the complete decode chain and has a faster prepare stage for M=1-16. This PR crosses over at M=32: its prepare kernel is 29% faster at M=32, 40% faster at M=40, and 48% faster at M=48, then continues through M=128. It also supports more head/rank combinations.

As currently written, #38583 stores Hadamard-rotated keys and only handles rows up to 48, while current main's fallback writer stores no-Hadamard keys. Mixing those paths at larger graph rows can therefore mix cache representations within a request. This PR follows current main's representation and only enables when the compatible fallback is active.

title: [Spec] Build DFlash draft layers under their checkpoint names and refuse tensors the draft would drop
body:
## Motivation

A quantized DFlash draft is built from its quantization config by module name and loaded by tensor name, and the two did not see the same names. `DFlashDraftModel` gave every decoder layer an empty prefix unless the checkpoint was a Nemotron 3.5 draft, so quantization matching saw a bare `qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` for all layers. Name-based `ignore` entries such as `re:.*self_attn\.q_proj$` never applied, the attention projections were built as quantized layers, and `load_weights` then dropped the checkpoint's BF16 `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` tensors without a word because the fused module had no `.weight` to put them in. The packed weight went into attention uninitialized. With the W8A16 draft from the recipe below, built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, main hits a device-side assert (`srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` in `indexSelectSmallIndex`) on the server's own warm-up request, after a startup that only logged `DFLASH fused KV materialization disabled: quantized qkv_proj is not supported for this path`.

The second half of the same problem is `fc`: outside the Nemotron path it was a plain `nn.Linear`, so a checkpoint that quantizes `fc` (`fc.weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`, or FP8 `fc.weight` + `weight_scale_inv`) had those tensors dropped the same way and `fc` kept its random init, so the draft would propose from a random projection of the target's hidden states. Several of the quantized DFlash2 drafts published on the Hub for Qwen3.8-27B quantize `fc` as well.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py` only:

- Every decoder layer is built with `layers.{i}` (or `{prefix}.layers.{i}`), not just Nemotron drafts, so a quantization config matches the same names the checkpoint uses. Unquantized drafts are unaffected; the prefix only feeds quantization matching.
- `packed_modules_mapping` on the draft model class, which the loader already injects into the quant config, so an `ignore` list that names `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` or `gate_proj`/`up_proj` applies to the fused module. llm-compressor writes the shard names it was given, as in the recipe below. As for every other model with such a mapping, an ignore list that names a single shard now fails with the fused-layer scheme mismatch error instead of matching nothing.
- `fc` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with the quant config for every draft, as it already was for Nemotron; `project_target_hidden` uses `input_size` and unpacks the `(out, bias)` tuple unconditionally. The `fc.weight` shape check keeps the packed-aware form and `encoder.fc.*` vendor names alias to `fc.*`. The unquantized `fc` now runs through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` like the Nemotron draft's, not `F.linear`, and starts uninitialized rather than randomly initialized, so `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint that fills the decoder layers but never `fc` (such a checkpoint produced unusable drafts before as well); a projector-only load, as Domino does, is unaffected.
- `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint tensor whose module the draft has, under a parameter name that module does not have (a dense tensor for a packed layer, or a packed tensor for a dense layer, under the draft's own or the vendor `encoder.` name), with the module's actual parameter names in the message. Tensors for modules the draft does not have are still ignored, and so are the ones that have no draft parameter by design: `.bias`, the `.inv_freq` / `.cos_cached` / `.sin_cached` rotary caches, and the `.input_scale` / `.output_scale` / `.k_scale` / `.v_scale` / `.kv_scale` activation and KV-cache scales.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py`: the layer names through the real decoder layer, the shard-only ignore list reaching the fused projection, `fc` quantized / ignored / dense, packed and dense `fc` loading (own and vendor name), the two refusals, and the tensors that must still be ignored. On main 8 of the 12 cases fail.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (CPU): `test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py` 12 passed (8 fail on main); `test_dflash_logits.py`, `test_dflash_domino.py`, `test_oot_dflash_hooks.py`, `model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py` 31 passed.

The quantized draft is built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ: INT8 weight-only for the MLP, `o_proj` and `fc`, with q/k/v, the candidate selector and the convolution kernels left BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W8A16",
    scheme="W8A16",
    ignore=["re:.*self_attn\\.(q|k|v)_proj$", "re:.*candidate_selector.*",
            "re:.*kernel_projection$", "re:.*norm.*"],
)
```

The target is `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` with a W4A16 body from the same tool and its `lm_head` left BF16, so that this change is tested on its own.

<details>
<summary>Target recipe</summary>

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationConfig, QuantizationScheme
from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import W4A16
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16",
    config=QuantizationConfig(config_groups={
        "body": QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], **W4A16),
    }),
    ignore=["lm_head", "re:.*visual.*", "re:.*mtp.*", "re:.*in_proj_(a|b)$", "re:.*conv1d.*",
            "re:.*norm.*", "re:.*embed_tokens.*"],
)
```
</details>

One RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB, TP=1), `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-dflash-block-size 8 --disable-overlap-schedule`. Accuracy is SGLang's own GSM8K eval, one request at a time so completions can be compared across runs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512
```

| draft | branch | result | GSM8K (200) | accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | main | serves | 0.960 | |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (BF16) | main | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (BF16) | this PR | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| W8A16 from the recipe | main | device-side assert on the server's warm-up request | | |
| W8A16 from the recipe | this PR | serves, fused KV materialization back on | 0.970 | 6.031 |

Accept length is the mean of the scheduler's `accept len` over every decode-log window of the run, bonus token included.

With the BF16 draft, this PR's 200 completions are identical to main's. The W8A16 draft's completions match the BF16 draft's on main in 196/200. Against the target decoding on its own, the W8A16 draft matches 165/200 and the BF16 draft 166/200.

With #40883 applied as well, the same W8A16 draft also serves the target from that PR, whose `lm_head` is W8A16 pack-quantized: GSM8K 0.965, accept length 6.025, and 165/200 completions matching that target decoding on its own.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for unquantized drafts on most GPUs. Their only runtime change is that `fc` runs through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` instead of `F.linear`, as the Nemotron draft's `fc` already did, and that method is `F.linear` itself unless the BF16 GEMM backend is cutedsl (the `auto` choice on sm100). There `fc` now uses the same GEMM as the rest of the draft's linears. The quantized drafts above go from not serving to serving; I have no clean timing for them, since the GPU these runs used was shared with other jobs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: fix: legacy SGL_ env vars silently dropped when the rewritten name is itself deprecated
body:
## Motivation

Setting the legacy env var `SGL_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=1` is silently ignored: the TP memory imbalance check stays enabled, and the deprecation warning tells the user to switch to `SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK`, which is itself deprecated.

Root cause: `_handle_deprecated_envs()` in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` applies the `_DEPRECATED_ENVS` registry **before** rewriting legacy `SGL_`-prefixed names to `SGLANG_`. A legacy name whose rewritten form is itself in the registry gets rewritten only after the registry pass that would forward it (inverted, via `_invert_bool`) to `SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK` has already run, so the forwarding never happens.

Repro on current main:

```
$ SGL_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=1 python -W always -c \
    "from sglang.srt.environ import envs; print(envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK.get())"
UserWarning: Environment variable SGL_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK is deprecated, please use SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK
True          # check still enabled; the setting was dropped
```

After this PR the same command prints `False`, with both warnings chaining to the final name.

## Modifications

- `_handle_deprecated_envs()`: run the `SGL_` -> `SGLANG_` prefix rewrite first, then the registry pass, so a rewritten name that is itself in the registry still gets its forwarding. No behavior change for names that only need one hop.
- `test/registered/unit/test_environ.py`: add `test_legacy_sgl_prefix_chains_into_registry_forwarding`, a fresh-import subprocess test (module-level `_handle_deprecated_envs()` runs at import, so the existing in-process `_apply` pattern cannot cover ordering).

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (env-var handling only; no model or kernel code touched).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to pre-commit (all hooks pass on the two changed files).
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_environ.py`: 13 passed + new test failing before the fix, 14 passed after).
- [ ] Update documentation (no docs reference these env vars' interaction).
- [x] N/A accuracy/speed benchmarks.

title: [Spec] Let NEXTN and the DFlash2 selector reuse a packed target lm_head
body:
## Motivation

A compressed-tensors checkpoint that quantizes `lm_head` in the pack-quantized INT format stores the head as `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`; the module has no `.weight`. The target serves fine on its own, but both speculative paths that borrow the target head refuse it:

- `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` dies at startup in `get_embed_and_head`: `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'`.
- `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with a DFlash2 draft dies on the server's own warm-up request, so the server never becomes ready: `DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head or a supported lm_head.quant_method.`

Both come from `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` refusing any head without `.weight`. That check arrived with #27906 to keep the ModelOpt `lm_head.weight.dtype` reads safe. A packed head is exactly the case where `quant_method.apply` is the only way to get logits, and the target's own `LogitsProcessor` already does that through its trailing fallback branch. #35496 added the quant-method path to the DFlash2 selector, but the gate never let a packed head reach it. GGUF heads (`qweight`, no `.weight`) sit in the same position.

Reproduced on main (525f140) with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` quantized by llm-compressor so that `lm_head` is pack-quantized; the recipe is under Accuracy Tests.

## Modifications

- `layers/logits_processor.py`: `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` no longer requires `.weight`. Only the three ModelOpt methods, whose branches read `lm_head.weight.dtype`, are refused when the tensor is missing. In `_compute_lm_head` a head without a dense weight now takes the `quant_method.apply` branch and keeps the fp32 activation cast the old fallback gave it under `--enable-fp32-lm-head` (that flag with a marlin-packed head was and stays unsupported); the old trailing fallback becomes an explicit error, since every head that used to reach it is now admitted by the gate. Only the second, bound definition of the gate is changed; #39707 removes the shadowed first copy.
- `models/qwen3_5.py`, `models/qwen3_5_text.py`: `get_embed_and_head` hands out `None` for a packed head instead of reading `.weight`. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` then shares the whole module through `set_lm_head_from_target`, which `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` already implements.
- `speculative/spec_utils.py`: `lm_head_is_packed` (no `.weight`, and not a `PPMissingLayer`). `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: when the target head is packed and the draft cannot take the module (no `set_lm_head_from_target`, or a hot-token map), fail with a clear error instead of decoding with the draft's own head; the PP+spec branch, which shares the tensor only, fails the same way.
- Out of scope: `dspark_draft_sampler.py`, `deepseek_v4_dspark.py` and `domino_utils.py` still read `lm_head.weight` and keep failing on a packed head as before. DSpark's `project_through_lm_head` goes through the gate and is fixed along the way.
- `speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`, `speculative/frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`: these two share the head tensor only, so they fail with the same clear error on a packed target instead of handing the draft `head=None`. `qwen3_5_text.set_embed_and_head` accepts `None` for either half, matching what its accessor can now return.
- Tests: the two DFlash2 selector cases in `test_dflash_logits.py` are parametrized over a head that keeps packed bytes under `.weight` and one that has no `.weight` at all. New CPU file `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` covers the gate (admission, and refusal of each ModelOpt method without a dense weight), the fp32 cast, the error path, the three accessors, and `init_lm_head` sharing the module, refusing when it cannot, and still accepting a pipeline stage without a head. On main 8 of the 23 cases fail; the rest pin behaviour that must not change.

## Accuracy Tests

Checkpoints, both built from the official weights with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ. The target has a W4A16 body and a W8A16 `lm_head`, both pack-quantized; the in-checkpoint MTP layer stays BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationConfig, QuantizationScheme
from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import W4A16, W8A16
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-lm_head-W8A16",
    config=QuantizationConfig(config_groups={
        "lm_head": QuantizationScheme(targets=["re:.*lm_head$"], **W8A16),  # first match wins
        "body": QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], **W4A16),
    }),
    ignore=["re:.*visual.*", "re:.*mtp.*", "re:.*in_proj_(a|b)$", "re:.*conv1d.*",
            "re:.*norm.*", "re:.*embed_tokens.*"],
)
```

The reference is the same call without the `lm_head` group and with `"lm_head"` added to `ignore`, so its head stays BF16. DFLASH uses the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` draft.

One RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB, TP=1), `--disable-overlap-schedule`. NEXTN: steps 3, top-k 1, draft tokens 4. DFLASH: block size 8. Accuracy is SGLang's own GSM8K eval, one request at a time so completions can be compared across runs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512
```

| target `lm_head` | branch | spec | result | GSM8K (200) | accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | main | none | serves | 0.960 | |
| BF16 | main | NEXTN | serves | 0.970 | 3.629 |
| BF16 | main | DFLASH | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| W8A16 packed | main | none | serves | 0.965 | |
| W8A16 packed | main | NEXTN | `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'` at startup | | |
| W8A16 packed | main | DFLASH | `RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense ...` on the server's warm-up request | | |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | NEXTN | serves | 0.965 | 3.629 |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | DFLASH | serves; the selector is folded into the draft CUDA graph | 0.970 | 6.035 |

Accept length is the mean of the scheduler's `accept len` over every decode-log window of the run, bonus token included. The `sglang:spec_accept_length` gauge only holds the last window, so it is not used here.

Speculative decoding matches non-speculative decoding only up to numerics, so completions are compared against the same checkpoint without speculation. With the packed head, 172/200 NEXTN and 167/200 DFLASH completions match the packed-head target decoding on its own. On main, the BF16-head target matches its own non-speculative run in 167/200 (NEXTN) and 166/200 (DFLASH) completions.

Unit tests (CPU): `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` + `test_dflash_logits.py` 23 passed (8 fail on main); `test_eagle_draft_extend_logits.py`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_packed_weight_loader.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py` 31 passed; the `lm_head_guard` cases of `model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py` 4 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for dense or ModelOpt heads: the gate returns what it returned before and the same kernel runs. A packed head goes from refusing to start to serving; the draft calls the same `quant_method.apply` the target already runs for its own logits. I have no clean timing for it yet, since the GPU these runs used was shared with other jobs.

title: feat: add fused CuTe DSL BF16 GEMM SiTU kernel
body:
## Motivation

Add an SM100 CuTe DSL kernel that fuses two BF16 GEMMs with the SiTU activation:

    gate = X @ W_gate.T
    up   = X @ W_up.T
    output = softcap(gate) * sigmoid(gate) * softcap(up)

The kernel accepts a packed [2 * intermediate_size, K] gate/up weight, accumulates both projections in FP32 TMEM, applies SiTU in registers, and writes one BF16 output tensor.

## Implementation Details

The kernel computes the gate and up projections together instead of launching two independent GEMMs, we split the packed `[2I, K]` weight into gate and up views, Load one activation tile and the corresponding gate/up weight tiles through the same pipelined TMA mainloop and issue two MMAs per K tile, reusing the activation tile for both projections. Gate and Up FP32 accumulators is kept in separate TMEM column regions. Other contributions include -

- Supports 1-CTA and 2-CTA Blackwell MMA paths.
- Pipelines gate weights, up weights, and activations with TMA.
- Uses the required TMEM ordering and load-completion fences before releasing
  TMEM.
- Provides explicit tactics covering CTA_M 64/128 and CTA_N 8/16/32/64/128.
- Uses reduced pipeline depths where required by the fused kernel's doubled A-side SMEM footprint.

## Accuracy Tests

The kernel is validated with:

- **FP32 reference:** Computes both projections with FP32 PyTorch matmuls, applies the SiTU formula in FP32, then converts the result to BF16.
- **Existing-kernel comparison:** Compares against two calls to the existing `cutedsl_bf16_gemm` kernel followed by SiTU.
- **All-tactic coverage:** Compiles and checks all 26 1-CTA and 2-CTA tactics, including CTA_M 64/128 and CTA_N 8/16/32/64/128 configurations.
- **Shape coverage:** Tests single-token, aligned, ragged, and larger token counts, including `T=1, 7, 8, 9, 16, 63, 64, and 128`.
- **Numerical tolerance:** BF16 results are checked with `rtol=2e-2, atol=0.25`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on NVIDIA B200 using CUDA graph timing. “Previous” is two cutedsl_bf16_gemm calls followed by SiTU.

| Tokens | I    | K    | Best tactic (M,N,stages,2CTA) | Fused    | Previous | Speedup |
|-------:|-----:|-----:|-------------------------------|---------:|---------:|--------:|
| 1      | 1024 | 2048 | `(64,8,6,False)`              | 8.23 us  | 10.31 us | 1.25x   |
| 8      | 1024 | 2048 | `(64,8,6,False)`              | 8.23 us  | 10.30 us | 1.25x   |
| 16     | 1024 | 2048 | `(64,16,6,True)`              | 6.20 us  | 10.28 us | 1.66x   |
| 64     | 6144 | 7168 | `(64,64,5,True)`              | 34.03 us | 37.96 us | 1.12x   |
| 128    | 6144 | 7168 | `(64,128,4,True)`             | 38.61 us | 41.31 us | 1.07x   |

title: [DSV4.1][HiCache] fix: wait for the layer transfer before reading low-ratio index-K
body:
## Motivation

`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant` and `get_low_ratio_index_k_fp4` read index-K rows without `wait_layer_transfer(layer_id)`, while every other getter in the pool waits first. Their callers are the V4.1 low-ratio indexer paths (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`: dense fp4 prefill on SM100, and the SM90 torch path), and nothing earlier in those layers waits. With HiCache L2 load-back, the indexer can therefore read index-K before the host-to-device copy of that layer lands and pick top-k from stale rows (silent quality loss, no crash).

This reproduced on V4.1-Flash TP4 with HiCache L2: re-reading the same rows after `wait_layer_transfer` showed up to 98% of the rows changed at a late layer once the per-layer load window was widened.

## Modifications

Wait for the layer's transfer at the top of both getters, like the sibling getters.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_indexer_access_uses_layer_ratio_and_waits_only_for_reads` now also covers the two low-ratio getters and checks the wait precedes each read. It fails without this change and passes with it; `test_dsv4_compressed_pools.py`: 9 passed.
